- Protocol runner: `invoke` steps → `client.request("invoke", …)` with the

  direct runner (vtt-1xv.10) uses, so both runners agree (review r2 finding
  11); refusals mapped with
  `toFixtureReason`; the coverage table now expects every scenario complete

title: Protocol and authority: faces and action state in object views
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.4 (presentation filtered by effective visibility),
§4.6 (face layouts, show-when, as written by vtt-1xv.5); FORMULAS.md §7
(propagation), §9; docs/PROTOCOL.md §7.2, §8 (deltas), §12; M5 plan decisions Q9,
Q10, Q11 (docs/plans/m5-plan.md §4); review r1 findings 4, 5, 6, 7; review r2 finding 11; review r3 finding 6.

Exclusive files: tests `packages/authority/test/protocol/face-views.test.ts`,
`packages/authority/test/protocol/action-state.test.ts`,
`packages/protocol/test/face-views.test.ts`; post-merge additive edits of
`packages/protocol/src/views.ts` (`FaceView`, `FaceElementView`,
`ActionStateView`, `ObjectView.action_states`, `ObjectView.face`), `packages/authority/src/protocol/views.ts`
(object views only), `packages/authority/src/protocol/subscriptions.ts`
(candidates only); new `packages/authority/src/protocol/face-visibility.ts`
(sorted index line) and test `packages/authority/test/protocol/face-visibility.test.ts`.

- Live action state (review r1 finding 5): a new `ActionStateView = {name;
  enabled: boolean; reason?: "when_false" | "when_error"}` and
  `ObjectView.action_states: ActionStateView[]` (one per action, in the
  order of `actions`, every viewer; the `when` result evaluated as
  vtt-1xv.8 does). It appears only in live object views (subscribe results,
  deltas, `get_objects`, `list_objects`, `zones` views); `actions` stays
  vtt-1xv.28's `ActionDefinitionView[]`, and effects and snapshots never
  carry live state.
- `ObjectView.face?: FaceView` when the view's `cells` is `"all"` and the
  object has a layout: `FaceView = {elements: FaceElementView[]; collapsed?:
  FaceElementView[]; default_action?: string}`; `FaceElementView` = the
  element plus `index` (its position in the stored list; review r1 finding
  7) and `shown: boolean`. GM views (review r3 finding 6) retain every
  stored element with its `show_when` source: `shown` is true when
  `show_when` is absent or evaluates to `true` (on the object, with
  `engine.evaluate`) and, for a button, its action exists; otherwise `shown`
  is false with `reason: "show_when_false" | "show_when_error" |
  "no_action"` (and `error: ErrorCode` for an error). Character views keep
  only the elements that would be `shown: true` for the GM and whose value
  or editor cell the viewer can read, each with `shown: true`, without
  `show_when`; `default_action` is kept only if it names an existing
  action; every kept element keeps its stored `index`.
- `faceElementVisible(table: Table, viewer: Viewer, object: ObjectId,
  element: {list: "full" | "collapsed"; index: number}): boolean` (review r2
  finding 11; defined in review r3 finding 6): true exactly when the
  viewer's live object view of that object (built by the same code) has a
  face element in that list with that stored `index` and `shown === true`;
  false when the object is absent from the view (nonexistent, invisible,
  covered) or the element is absent or has `shown: false`. vtt-1xv.10 and
  (through views) vtt-1xv.13 use exactly this definition.
- Deltas (Q10; review r1 finding 6): after each commit the candidates for
  re-viewing include every object in `summary.faceChanged` (a plain face
  edit, its removal, or its undo), and every in-scope object whose layout has
  a `show_when` or whose actions have a `when`
  (views are still sent only when their canonical JSON changed), so results
  that read other objects stay current without dependency tracking.

Done when: `faceElementVisible` tests, each asserted equal to "present with
`shown === true` in the viewer's live face view": a GM element retained
with `shown: false` (`show_when` false) is false; a GM button naming a
nonexistent action is retained with `shown: false`, `reason: "no_action"`,
and is false; the same elements are omitted from Aldric's view and false; an
invisible object, an object under a cover, an element naming an unreadable
cell (for Aldric), and a visible element; tests with a real server and
mirrors show: the Attack card's GM
view (actions invoked through vtt-1xv.11's `invoke`, scripted dice) carries
the buttons with `shown` and `action_states` matching FORMULAS §10 before and
after each action: Apply shown and disabled before the rolls, enabled after
Roll damage, absent from `shown` elements after Apply; Aldric's view lacks `show_when` and the hidden
Apply button; a value element on the goblin's GM-only `ac` is absent from
Aldric's face view; a button whose guard reads another object's cell
(`target.hp > 0`) changes `enabled` in the delta after a commit that changes
only that other object; a `show_when` error hides the element and the GM view
has its code; a `cells: "structural"` subscription carries no `face`; in
Aldric's view a visible element following one filtered out (a GM-only cell)
keeps its stored `index`; adding, changing, removing and undoing an
unconditional face (no `show_when`, no guards) each produce the delta that
makes the mirror equal a fresh subscribe; effects and snapshots in the log
window carry no `action_states`;
applying deltas equals a fresh subscribe (the M3 equivalence property for
these fields); `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test`
exit 0.

Out of scope: drawing (vtt-1xv.14, vtt-1xv.15); dependency-tracked presentation
formulas (followup in section 5); the face effect view (vtt-1xv.7).

Depends on: vtt-1xv.7, vtt-1xv.28, vtt-1xv.5, vtt-1xv.11, vtt-5su.6, vtt-5su.9.

title: Protocol and authority: `invoke` command, client retry, explain parse status
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §5.2 ("define and invoke actions"; writes carry their
base revision and are rejected on conflict), §7 Revisions; docs/PROTOCOL.md
§3, §4 (`invoke`), §6 (processing order, stale keys, deduplication, client
retries, `uncertain`), §9 (`explain_action`), §10 as written by vtt-1xv.5; review r1 finding 2;
M5 plan decisions Q2, Q3, Q12.

Exclusive files: tests `packages/protocol/test/invoke.test.ts`,
`packages/authority/test/protocol/invoke.test.ts`,
`packages/authority/test/protocol/explain-parse.test.ts`,
`packages/protocol/test/invoke-retry.test.ts`; post-merge additive edits of
`packages/protocol/src/methods.ts` (`InvokeParamsSchema`,
`InvokeResultSchema` replacing `z.never()`, `ExplainActionResultSchema` parse
fields), `packages/protocol/src/client.ts` (`isWrite` includes `invoke`;
`client.invoke(params)` with `base_revision` required and a UUID `txn_id` by
default, never retrying), `packages/protocol/src/client/recovery.ts`
(`invokeWithRetry`, the same single same-session resend and `uncertain`
reasons as `transactWithRetry`, sharing its code), `packages/authority/src/
protocol/commands.ts` (the invoke command), `packages/authority/src/protocol/
explain.ts`, `packages/authority/src/server/router.ts` (the `invoke` route
line only; vtt-5su.10).

- Command processing in PROTOCOL §6's order: structural validation (schema,
  `txn_id`, `label`, `actor` allowed only for non-agent connections, `retry`
  only with `txn_id`) → deduplication lookup (store shared with `transact`,
  key `(client.instance, txn_id)`, fingerprint the canonical JSON of
  `{method: "invoke", params minus retry}`) → state validation (`actor` an
  existing character) → floor → declared keys `obj:<object>` and
  `actions:<object>` against groups after `base_revision` → the command
  opens the transaction itself (review r1 finding 2), exactly as `transact`
  does in `commands.ts`: `transactWithDice(table, actor, {kind: "action",
  label, origin: {object, action}}, hostDice, (tx) => {…})`, inside which it
  calls `runAction` of the command context's executor (created once as
  `createExecutor({handlers: [...coreHandlers, ...placementHandlers]})`,
  vtt-1xv.8, vtt-1xv.9; review r2 finding 8) as `runAction(tx, {table, dice}, {object, action,
  tableDestination: table})`, throws `new Rejected(rejection)` on a refusal
  (remembering `step`), and, when `base_revision` < current, computes the
  touched keys of `tx.effects()` and throws `StaleWriteError` on a conflict,
  all before the transaction function returns, so nothing commits, no
  listener runs and the dice source is reset → commit. The
  result is `{status: "committed", revision, index, created}` or
  `{status: "rejected", rejection, step?}` and is stored for deduplication.
  An unknown object or action is `rejected` `invalid` (never `not_found`,
  PROTOCOL §4); an object removed since `base_revision` is `stale_write`.
  The `when` guard is evaluated at the current revision, not at
  `base_revision`.
- `explain_action` (GM only): `when_parses: boolean`, `when_syntax_error?`,
  `step_status: ({ok: true} | {ok: false; message; offset})[]` from vtt-1xv.6's
  `parseAction`; character results unchanged.

- Limits (review r3 finding 7): `max_each_items` and `max_action_writes`
  are enforced by the executor with vtt-1xv.28's constants, the same values
  `LIMITS` advertises in `welcome`; a test invokes an action whose `each`
  exceeds `LIMITS.max_each_items` and gets `step_error` `#LIMIT`.

Done when: protocol tests round-trip params and results and reject unknown
keys, `actor` from an agent, `retry` without `txn_id`; authority tests over a
real server on port 0 with Node's `WebSocket` and `ProtocolClient`: the
Attack card's three actions and the Fireball card's Lock targets (a
placement action: spawned rows in `created`) and Discard commit through
`invoke` with scripted dice
(`TableHost.inMemory` with a `ScriptedDiceSource`), `created` lists Lock
targets' rows, a second Apply is `rejected` `when_false`, a repeated `txn_id`
returns the stored result without consuming dice, the same `txn_id` with a
different action is `invalid` "txn_id reused…", a concurrent GM write to the
target's `damage_taken` after `base_revision` makes Apply `stale_write`, and
a concurrent write of `empty` to the card's `dmg` (the guard stays true) makes Roll damage `stale_write`; each
refused invoke changes neither the document, the revision, the log nor the
dice position (`ScriptedDiceSource.remaining()` unchanged after the stale
Roll damage) and sends no commit event to a second connected client; an invoke with `actor` Aldric records that
actor, `invokeWithRetry` resends once after a same-session socket drop and
returns the stored result, and reports `uncertain` after a restart; the
client's `isWrite` gap is closed: an `invoke` whose socket drops after it was
sent (plain `client.invoke`, no retry) rejects `uncertain` with `details.sent:
true`, never `disconnected`, while one never sent rejects `disconnected`;
`explain_action` reports a bad step's offset; `invoke` is no longer
`unsupported`; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test`
exit 0.

Out of scope: the MCP tool (vtt-1xv.13); object view fields (vtt-1xv.12); the UI
(vtt-1xv.16).

Depends on: vtt-1xv.8, vtt-1xv.9, vtt-1xv.7, vtt-1xv.28, vtt-1xv.6, vtt-1xv.5, vtt-5su.10, vtt-5su.5, vtt-5su.16,
vtt-5su.19, vtt-5su.7.

description:

`when_error`, `step_error`), §7 (`action`; `face_element` and setup `face`
as written by vtt-1xv.5), §8, §9 (all ten fixtures), §11; FORMULAS.md §10; review r1 finding 7; review r2 findings 8, 11;

- `setup.ts`: copies `face` into objects. `steps.ts`: `invoke` →

title: Authority: placement steps and destinations
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §8.2 (destinations), §8.3 (`move`, `spawn`,
`remove`), §3.1 (landing rule), §8.4 (as written by vtt-1xv.5); DESIGN.md §4.1
(spawn, remove, containment), §7 Smaller decisions (the `table` destination
is resolved by M5 into a board destination); M5 plan decisions Q4, Q5 (docs/plans/m5-plan.md §4); review r2 finding 8.

Exclusive files: `packages/authority/src/engine/steps-place.ts`, tests
`packages/authority/test/engine/steps-place.test.ts`; its sorted line in
`packages/authority/src/engine/index.ts`. Exports `placementHandlers:
StepHandlerEntry[]` (`move`, `spawn`, `remove`) written against vtt-1xv.8's
`StepContext`; it does not register itself and does not edit `invoke.ts`
(review r2 finding 8). Its tests compose `createExecutor({handlers:
[...coreHandlers, ...placementHandlers]})` and run through `invokeAction`;
vtt-1xv.11 runs placement actions through the protocol entry point.

- Destinations: `container` → the expression must be one reference to an
  existing object (`empty` → `#REF`, list → `#TYPE`) → M2 container
  destination without index (appends); `board(b, p)` → `b` a reference to an
  existing board (an object reference or missing id → `#REF`), `p` a list of
  two finite numbers (`#TYPE` otherwise); `beside(r)` (Q5) → `r`'s outermost
  container chain must end on a board (else `step_error` "not on a board"),
  position = that board object's anchor + `[wr / 2 + wm / 2 + 0.25, 0]` where
  `wr` and `wm` are the widths of the literal footprint bounds of that
  on-board object and of the object being placed (0 when shapeless);
  `table` → `req.tableDestination` if given, else `step_error` without code,
  message "the table destination needs the invoker's board and viewport
  centre".
- `move(ref, dest)`: M2 `move` (landing rule, containment cycle refusal kept
  as `containment_cycle`). `spawn(template, dest, {cells})`: M2 `spawn`; each
  record value evaluated in the context (with `it` inside `each`) must be
  storable; the copies' ids join `InvokeOutcome.created` in creation order;
  later steps read spawned formula cells as `empty` (M2 `ActionContext`).
  `remove(ref)`: M2 `remove` (recursive); later reads of removed objects are
  `#REF`.

Done when: tests show: Fireball's Lock targets spawns one row per target in
`targets` order with `target` and `owner` set and returns them in `created`;
Discard removes the deployed zone and the card with its rows; Draw moves the
first card of the deck into the owner's hand (contents order asserted) and
fails `when_false` on an empty deck; `board(gm_board, [3, 4])` places on top
(landing rule z); `board(goblin1, [0, 0])` → `#REF`; `beside(token)` for a
token of width 1 and a die of width 0.5 places at `x + 1.0`; `beside` of a
contained object uses its outermost on-board container; `table` with and
without `tableDestination`; a move into own descendant → `containment_cycle`
with `step`; a step after `remove(x)` reading `x.hp` → `step_error` `#REF`;
`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: the protocol (vtt-1xv.11); the UI's choice of `tableDestination`
(vtt-1xv.16).

Depends on: vtt-1xv.8.

title: Authority: action executor (guard, value steps, dice, each)
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.5, §7 (Transactions, operation records); FORMULAS.md
§8.1, §8.2 (paths), §8.3 (`set`, `add`, `append`, `roll`, `shuffle`, `each`),
§8.4 (as written by vtt-1xv.5), §2.2 (rolls act as totals in arithmetic), §7
(budget); FIXTURES.md §5 (dice consumption is transactional), §6
(rejections); M5 plan decisions Q3, Q4, Q6, Q7 (docs/plans/m5-plan.md §4;
the step table is in vtt-1xv.5); review r1 finding 2; review r2 finding 8; review r3
findings 7, 11.

The executor core over M2's `Table`, `ActionContext`, `transactWithDice` and
primitives (vtt-75c.15). Placement steps are vtt-1xv.9's `placementHandlers`;
callers compose them explicitly (no registration at import time). Exclusive files: `packages/authority/src/engine/invoke.ts`,
`packages/authority/src/engine/steps-value.ts`, tests
`packages/authority/test/engine/invoke.test.ts`,
`packages/authority/test/engine/steps-value.test.ts`; sorted lines in
`packages/authority/src/engine/index.ts`.

- Handler contract (review r2 finding 8), exported from `invoke.ts`:
  `StepOutcome = {ok: true} | {ok: false; rejection: Rejection}`;
  `StepHandler = (ctx: StepContext, step: Step) => StepOutcome`;
  `StepHandlerEntry = {kind: Step["kind"]; handle: StepHandler}`;
  `StepContext = {tx; table; dice; thisId: ObjectId; it?: Value;
  tableDestination?: {board; position}; created: ObjectId[] /* handlers
  push spawned ids in creation order */; evaluate(expr: Expr): Result /*
  through the invocation's ActionContext, scope {thisId, it}, a fresh
  20,000-unit budget */; resolvePath(path: PathNode): {ok: true; object;
  cell} | {ok: false; rejection}; primitives: {writeValue, setTag, rollInto,
  shuffleWith, move, spawn, remove} /* M2's, bound to tx and the dice
  source; each call counts one primitive call */; count(n: number): void /*
  extra primitive calls; past `MAX_ACTION_WRITES` (10,000) the executor refuses #LIMIT */;
  refuse(reason: {code?: ErrorCode; message: string}): StepOutcome /* a
  step_error at the current step index */; runStep(step: Step, scope: {it:
  Value}): StepOutcome /* used by each */}`. A primitive's `Rejected`
  thrown inside a handler is caught by the executor and mapped per the
  refusal rules below; any other exception propagates.
- `createExecutor({handlers: StepHandlerEntry[]}): Executor` (a duplicate
  kind throws; a step whose kind has no handler refuses `step_error` "not
  supported") with:
  - `runAction(tx: Transaction, ctx: {table: Table; dice: DiceSource},
    req: {object; action; tableDestination?}): RunOutcome`, which executes
    the whole action inside a transaction the caller opened and never
    commits or aborts it (review r1 finding 2): `RunOutcome` = `{ok: true;
    created: ObjectId[]}` | `{ok: false; rejection: Rejection; step?:
    number}`. On `{ok: false}` the caller must abort by throwing `new
    Rejected(rejection)` from its transaction function (the partial effects
    and the dice drawn are discarded by the store and `transactWithDice`'s
    reset); on `{ok: true}` the caller may check `tx.effects()` (vtt-1xv.11's
    stale check) before returning. Order: object exists and has an action
    of exactly that name, else `invalid`; `when` (if any) with
    `ctx.table.engine.evaluate(source, {thisId})` (the committed revision):
    `true` continues, an error is `when_error` with its code (`#SYNTAX` when
    it does not parse), anything else `when_false`; then every step is
    parsed with vtt-1xv.6's `parseStep` (first failure → `step_error`
    `#SYNTAX` with its index and message); then the steps run through the
    handlers. Nothing before the first `roll` or `shuffle` draws dice.
  - `invokeAction(table, dice, req: {object; action; actor: Actor; label?;
    tableDestination?}): InvokeOutcome` = `transactWithDice(table, actor,
    {kind: "action", label: req.label ?? action, origin: {object, action}},
    dice, (tx) => { const r = runAction(tx, {table, dice}, req); if (!r.ok)
    throw new Rejected(r.rejection); })`, returning `{ok: true; group;
    summary; created}` | `{ok: false; rejection; step?}`.
- `coreHandlers: StepHandlerEntry[]` (`steps-value.ts`): `set`, `add`,
  `append`, `roll`, `shuffle`, `each`. Callers compose `createExecutor({
  handlers: [...coreHandlers, ...placementHandlers]})` (vtt-1xv.10,
  vtt-1xv.11, vtt-1xv.22); this bead's tests use `coreHandlers` alone plus a
  test-local handler for the contract.
- Paths (Q4): `PathNode.object` null → `this`; otherwise it must evaluate to
  one reference to an existing object (`empty` → `#REF`, a list or other kind
  → `#TYPE`, an error → its code).
- Semantics (Q4): `set` writes a storable value with M2's `writeValue`
  (override on a formula cell); `tag` takes a list of text via `setTag`;
  `name` takes text; `id`, `contents`, `container`, `board`, `is_zone`,
  `template`, `shape` are refused `protected_cell` (the primitive's own
  refusal where it has one). `add`: current value (read through the context:
  read-your-writes) and increment each a number, a roll (its total) or
  `empty` (0), else `#TYPE`; writes the resulting number. `append`: current
  value a list or `empty` (as `[]`), else `#TYPE`; appends the value as one
  item. `roll(dice) -> path`: the expression must be a dice value (`#TYPE`
  otherwise); `rollInto` (cause `roll`). `shuffle(ref)`: `shuffleWith` on the
  object's contents. `each(list, step)`: the list is evaluated once (a list;
  `empty` as `[]`; a single value as a one-item list, as aggregates do), then
  the inner step runs per item with `it` bound; at most `MAX_EACH_ITEMS` (1,000) iterations.
  Any expression evaluating to an error is `step_error` with that code; a
  record where a value is needed is `#TYPE`.
- Refusal mapping (Q7): a step's evaluation error → `step_error {step, code,
  message}`; a primitive's `Rejected` inside a step keeps its type
  (`protected_cell`, `containment_cycle`, `type_error`) and the outcome
  carries `step`; a primitive's `invalid` becomes `step_error` without code
  and with the primitive's message; a `ScenarioError` from a scripted dice
  source propagates (never a refusal). `step` is the 0-based index in the
  action's step list (an `each`'s inner failure reports the `each`'s index).
- Limits (Q6): the constants are vtt-1xv.28's `MAX_EACH_ITEMS` and
  `MAX_ACTION_WRITES` (never local literals); more than `MAX_ACTION_WRITES`
  primitive calls in one invocation →
  `step_error` `#LIMIT`.

Done when: unit tests over M2 `Table`s built in-test with valid documents
(objects with `ActionDef`s that pass the M2 file schema) show: the Attack
card's Roll, Roll damage and Apply against scripted dice give the cells of
FORMULAS §10 and one `action` group each with origin and label; Apply twice →
`when_false` with nothing applied and no dice consumed; a `when` of `#REF` →
`when_error` `#REF`; a `when` of `1 +` → `when_error` `#SYNTAX`; a second step
`set(1, 2)` → `step_error` `#SYNTAX` at index 1 before the first step runs;
`add(hp, "x")` → `step_error` `#TYPE`; `add` on an empty cell with a roll
increment writes the total as a number; read-your-writes (`set(a, 1)` then
`set(b, a + 1)` gives `b` 2) and a formula cell read as of action start;
`set(contents, [])` → `protected_cell` with `step` 0; a roll after a failing
step consumes no script entry (`ScriptedDiceSource.remaining()`); `each` over
a three-item list, over `empty`, over a scalar; 1,001 iterations → `#LIMIT`;
`shuffle(this)` with a scripted permutation; undo of an invocation restores
every cell (one group); a refused invocation (a `when_false`, and a
`step_error` in the second step after a `roll` in the first) changes neither
the document, the revision, the log, nor the dice position, and no commit
listener runs; `runAction` called in a test-opened transaction that the test
then aborts leaves the store unchanged, and one the test commits produces
the same group as `invokeAction`; a test-local handler uses `evaluate`,
`resolvePath`, `primitives`, `count`, `created` and `refuse` (a primitive's
`Rejected` thrown inside it maps with the step index; `count` past the limit
refuses `#LIMIT`); a duplicate handler kind throws; an unhandled kind
(`move` without placement handlers) refuses "not supported"; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`,
`pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: `move`, `spawn`, `remove`, destinations (vtt-1xv.9); the protocol
(vtt-1xv.11); the fixture runner (vtt-1xv.10); actors other than the given one; perf
work on `ActionContext.read` (vtt-qf5.9).

Depends on: vtt-1xv.6, vtt-1xv.28, vtt-1xv.5.

description:

(face layouts, as written by vtt-1xv.5), §7 (operation records, undo keys,

The face storage and protocol changes, carried through every exhaustive

`packages/authority/src/store/face.ts`, tests
`packages/schema/test/face.test.ts`, `packages/authority/test/store/face.test.ts`,

- `FaceLayout = {elements: FaceElement[]; collapsed?: FaceElement[];
  default_action?: string}`; `FaceElement` = `{type: "value" | "editor"; cell;
  rect; show_when?; min_size?; style?}` | `{type: "button"; action; rect;
  label?; show_when?; min_size?}` | `{type: "contents"; rect; entries?:
  "collapsed" | "full"; show_when?; min_size?}`; `rect: [x, y, w, h]`
  (finite, `w`, `h` > 0) in the frame of Q8; `style = {size?: "small" |
  "normal" | "large" | "huge"; align?: "left" | "center" | "right"; caption?:

  `COLLAPSED_FRAME = [0, 0, 6, 0.6]`; `defaultFaceFrame(shape | null)`.
- `SceneObject.face?: FaceLayout` (absent = no layout); the file schema
  accepts it; canonical serialization orders keys as the schema does; no
  `schema_version` bump (Q8): older readers reject a file that uses `face`
  as an unknown key, which is acceptable because no released file exists.
- `setFace(tx, object, face | null)`: replaces the whole layout in one
  `{type: "field"; field: "face"; before: FaceLayout | null; after}` effect;
  refuses `invalid` for an unknown object or a `faceProblem`; touches key
  `face:<object>` (conflicts with itself and with `obj:<object>`); changes no
  readable cell; the change summary lists the object in a new `faceChanged`.
  Undo, replay and rewind handle the effect; spawn copies `face` verbatim (no

- Protocol: op `set_face {object, face: FaceLayout | null}` declaring

  schema in protocol `views.ts`: `FaceLayout`'s shape with every element
  carrying `index: number`, its position in the stored list, and no live
  `shown`; `FaceLayout` stays the storage and op type) is used by

  `ObjectSnapshotView.face?: FaceLayoutView | null` (create and remove

title: Formula: action step parser
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §8.2, §8.3, §8.4 (step grammar, as written by vtt-1xv.5),
review r1 finding 3,
§3.2 (expression syntax and limits), §2.3 (`#SYNTAX`).

Pure parsing, no evaluation. Exclusive files:
`packages/formula/src/actions/step-parser.ts`, tests
`packages/formula/test/actions/step-parser.test.ts`; its sorted line
`export * from "./actions/step-parser"` in `packages/formula/src/index.ts`.

- `parseStep(source: string): {ok: true; step: Step} | {ok: false; message:
  string; offset: number}` is a step-level recursive-descent parser over M1's
  lexer (`lexToken`, vtt-o9i), per the grammar written by vtt-1xv.5 (FORMULAS
  §8.4; review r1 finding 3): read the step name (an identifier), `(`, then
  the arguments the step kind takes, each an expression parsed with
  `parseExpressionPrefix` (which stops at `,`, `)` or `->`), a destination
  (the bare word `table`, `board(` expr `,` expr `)`, `beside(` expr `)`, or
  an expression), a record (an expression that must be a `Record` node), or,
  for `each`'s second argument, a step parsed recursively (not `each`); then
  `)`, then for `roll` exactly `->` and a path expression; then end of input.
  `->` is never handed to the expression parser as an operator. The
  expression limits of FORMULAS §3.2 (AST depth, node count) are counted over
  the whole step source, not per argument.
- `Step` = `{kind: "set" | "add" | "append"; path: PathNode; value: Expr}` |
  `{kind: "roll"; dice: Expr; path: PathNode}` | `{kind: "move"; object:
  Expr; to: DestinationNode}` | `{kind: "spawn"; template: Expr; to:
  DestinationNode; cells: {name: string; value: Expr}[]}` | `{kind: "remove"
  | "shuffle"; object: Expr}` | `{kind: "each"; list: Expr; step: Step}`
  (the inner step is never `each`). `PathNode` = `{object: Expr | null; cell:
  string}` (`null` is `this`; from a `NameNode`, or a `DotNode` whose object
  is any expression). `DestinationNode` = `{type: "table"}` (bare `table`) |
  `{type: "board"; board: Expr; position: Expr}` (`board(a, b)`) | `{type:
  "beside"; object: Expr}` (`beside(a)`) | `{type: "container"; container:
  Expr}` (anything else).
- Errors (all `ok: false` with an offset): unknown step name, wrong argument
  count, a path that is not a name or `.name` access, `each` inside `each`,
  `->` on a step other than `roll` or missing on `roll`, a spawn third
  argument that is not a record, duplicate record keys, trailing input, and
  every expression parse failure (its message and offset). Expression limits
  of §3.2 apply to the whole source.
- `parseAction(def: ActionDef): {when?: ParseResult; steps: ReturnType<typeof
  parseStep>[]}` (convenience for explain and the inspector; parses `when`
  with `parse`).
- Step names and `table`, `board`, `beside` are contextual: `set + 1` is an
  ordinary expression elsewhere; a cell named `table` used as a destination is
  written `this.table`.

Done when: table-driven tests parse every step line of FORMULAS §10 (Attack,
Fireball rows and card, Draw, Shuffle, die Roll) into the expected `Step`
values; `roll(attacker.damage_dice) -> dmg`; `each(targets, spawn(save_row,
this, {target: it, owner: it.owner}))`; `move(first(deck.contents),
owner.hand)`; `spawn(t, board(gm_board, [1, 2]))`; `move(x, beside(this))`;
`move(x, table)`; `move(x, this.table)` (a container destination);
`each(targets, roll(1d20) -> it.save_roll)` (a nested roll inside `each`);
`each(rows, add(it.target.damage_taken, it.damage_dealt))`; a step whose
arguments together exceed the node limit while each alone would not is
refused (the whole-source limit);
`` set(`Max HP`, 3) ``; and refusals with offsets for `roll(1d20)`,
`set(1, 2)`, `set(a)`, `each(l, each(m, remove(it)))`, `foo(a)`, `set(a, 1)
extra`, `spawn(t, this, 3)`, `spawn(t, this, {a: 1, a: 2})`, `set(a, (1`;
`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: evaluation and execution (vtt-1xv.8, vtt-1xv.9); changing the expression
grammar or the lexer; storing parsed steps (actions stay source text, D20).

Depends on: vtt-1xv.5.

title: Docs: M5 decisions
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.1, §4.5, §4.6, §4.7, §4.8, §5.2, §7, §9, §10;
FORMULAS.md §8; docs/PROTOCOL.md §4, §5, §6, §7.2, §7.6, §9, §10, §11, §12;
docs/FIXTURES.md §6, §7, §9 (Attack card), §11; CLAUDE.md Conventions; the
decisions of planning bead vtt-1xv.1 (docs/plans/m5-plan.md §4, Q1–Q22, all
accepted; review r1 findings 1, 3, 5, 7, 15; review r2 findings 1, 2, 3, 5,
10; review r3 findings 1–4, 6–8) and decision beads vtt-1xv.2,
vtt-1xv.3, vtt-1xv.4 (resolved in planning; this bead is the sole owner of
recording their outcomes, rows M5-D16–M5-D18; the orchestrator closes them
when this bead merges). Everything this bead writes is in this text; the plan
is cited only for background.

Docs only; the only M5 bead that edits docs. Exclusive files:
`docs/DESIGN.md`, `docs/FORMULAS.md`, `docs/PROTOCOL.md`, `docs/FIXTURES.md`,
`CLAUDE.md` (the orchestrator applies the CLAUDE.md edit if the implementing
agent declines). DESIGN §4.6 and §10 already hold M4's text and rows
(vtt-3l6.2, merged); add after them.

**1. FORMULAS §8 (actions).** §8.1 gains the evaluation order: the object
must exist and have an action of exactly that name (else the refusal
`invalid`); `when` is evaluated with `this` = the object at the current
revision: `true` runs, an error (`#SYNTAX` when it does not parse) refuses
`when_error` with its code, any other value refuses `when_false`; then every
step is parsed, and the first that does not parse refuses `step_error`
`#SYNTAX` with its 0-based index before any step runs; then the steps run in
order in one transaction. New §8.4 **Step syntax**, a step-level grammar:

```
step  := name "(" args ")" [ "->" path ]        -- "->" only after roll, required there
set(path, expr)   add(path, expr)   append(path, expr)   roll(expr) -> path
move(expr, dest)  spawn(expr, dest [, record])  remove(expr)  shuffle(expr)
each(expr, step)                                 -- the second argument is parsed as a step
path  := a bare name | an expression ending in ".name"   (`this` when bare)
dest  := table | board(expr, expr) | beside(expr) | expr (a container reference)
record:= "{" name ":" expr ("," name ":" expr)* "}"
```

Each `expr` argument is parsed with the expression parser in prefix mode
(it stops at `,` `)` or `->`); `->` is step syntax and never an expression
operator; `each`'s second argument is parsed recursively as a step, which
may not be `each` (one level), so `each(targets, roll(1d20) ->
it.save_roll)` is valid. The expression limits of §3.2 apply to the whole
step source. Step names and `table`, `board`, `beside` are contextual, not
reserved: a cell named `table` used as a destination is written
`this.table`. A spawn record gives evaluated values; a formula initial cell
is possible only through the protocol's `spawn` op.

§8.3 gains the semantics table (Q4):

| Step | Accepts | Writes | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `set(path, v)` | any storable value | `writeValue` (an override on a formula cell); `tag` takes a list of text via `setTag`; `name` takes text | `id`, `contents`, `container`, `board`, `is_zone`, `template`, `shape` → `protected_cell`; a record → `#TYPE` |
| `add(path, v)` | current value and `v` each a number, a roll (its total) or `empty` (0) | the resulting number | anything else `#TYPE` |
| `append(path, v)` | current value a list or `empty` (as `[]`) | the list with `v` appended as one item | other current value `#TYPE` |
| `roll(d) -> path` | a dice value | the roll result (cause `roll`) | not dice `#TYPE` |
| `shuffle(r)` | one reference | its contents reordered by a drawn permutation | |
| `move(r, dest)` | one reference | M2 `move`, landing rule | `containment_cycle` |
| `spawn(t, dest, rec)` | one reference; record values storable | M2 `spawn` with the record as initial cells | record value an error → its code |
| `remove(r)` | one reference | recursive removal; later reads `#REF` | |
| `each(list, step)` | a list; `empty` runs nothing; a scalar runs once (the aggregate rule) | the inner step per item with `it` bound; the list is evaluated once before running | more than 1,000 items `#LIMIT` |

Every path's object part must evaluate to one reference to an existing
object (`empty` → `#REF`, a list or other kind → `#TYPE`, an error → its
code); any expression evaluating to an error refuses `step_error` with that
code. Destinations (Q5): a container destination is one reference
(`empty` → `#REF`, a list → `#TYPE`) and appends; `board(b, p)` needs `b`
a board (else `#REF`) and `p` two finite numbers (else `#TYPE`);
`beside(r)` places on the board of `r`'s outermost on-board container chain
(else `step_error` "not on a board") at that object's anchor + `[wr/2 +
wm/2 + 0.25, 0]` where `wr`, `wm` are the widths of the literal footprint
bounds of that object and of the placed object (0 when shapeless);
`table` resolves to the invoke's `table` parameter and without it is
`step_error` (no code) "the table destination needs the invoker's board and
viewport centre". Limits (Q6): at most 1,000 `each` items and 10,000
primitive calls per invocation (`#LIMIT`). Refusals (Q7): an evaluation
error is `step_error {step, code, message}`; a primitive's own refusal
inside a step keeps its type (`protected_cell`, `containment_cycle`,
`type_error`) with the step index alongside; a primitive's `invalid` becomes
`step_error` without code; the index of a failure inside `each` is the
`each`'s. An action is one `action` group labelled with its name (or the
invoke's `label`), origin `{object, action}`.

**5. PROTOCOL.**
- §4 `invoke`: params `object`, `action`, `base_revision`, `txn_id?`,
  `retry?` (only with `txn_id`), `actor?` (character, non-agent only),
  `label?` (≤ 200), `table?: {board, position}`; result `{status:
  "committed", revision, index, created: ObjectId[]}` or `{status:
  "rejected", rejection: ProtocolRejection, step?: number}`. §6: processing
  order as `transact`; declared keys `obj:<object>`, `actions:<object>`; the
  action runs inside the command's transaction and its touched keys are
  checked before commit (a stale invoke consumes no randomness); the `when`
  guard is evaluated at the current revision; deduplication in the
  `transact` store, fingerprint including the method.
- §5: the 20th op `set_face {object, face: FaceLayout | null}` (key
  `face:<object>`); `ObjectInit.face`.
- §7.2: `ActionDefinitionView` (the existing `ActionView` shape: `name`,
  and for the GM `when` and `steps`), used in object views, field effects
  and snapshots; `ObjectView.action_states: ActionStateView[]` (`{name,
  enabled, reason?: "when_false" | "when_error"}`, every viewer, one per
  action in order) in live object views only; `ObjectView.face?: FaceView`
  when `cells` is `"all"` and the object has a layout: elements carry
  `index` (position in the stored list) and `shown`; the GM view keeps every
  element with its `show_when`, `shown: false` with a `reason`
  (`show_when_false`, `show_when_error` with its `error` code, or
  `no_action` for a button naming no action) when hidden; character views
  keep only elements that are shown and whose cell they can read, without
  `show_when`, keeping `index`. An element is visible to a viewer exactly
  when it is present in that viewer's view with `shown: true`.
- §7.6: the `field: "face"` effect view and `ObjectSnapshotView.face` use the
  wire type `FaceLayoutView` (the layout with `index` on every element and no
  live `shown`; `FaceLayout` stays the storage type): GM lossless;
  characters keep it when the object is visible now, without `show_when` and
  without elements naming cells unreadable now (so a removed object's
  snapshot is omitted from a character's view until an undo restores it).
- §8 Evaluation: objects with a `when` or `show_when`, and objects whose
  face changed, are re-viewed after every commit.
- §9 `explain_action`: GM-only `when_parses`, `when_syntax_error?`,
  `step_status: ({ok: true} | {ok: false; message; offset})[]`.
- §10: rejections `when_false {object, action}`, `when_error {object,
  action, code, message?}`, `step_error {object, action, step, code?,
  message}`; limits `max_each_items` 1,000, `max_action_writes` 10,000,
  `max_face_elements` 200, in the §10 table and the `limits` the `welcome`
  message advertises (§2).
- §11: tool `invoke {object, action, base_revision, label?, table?}`
  (`txn_id` generated, retried as `transact`; refusals `isError` with the
  rejection and `step`); the request-surface server has 15 tools (14 plus
  `invoke`) and the composed `vtt-mcp` process 19 (adding `subscribe`,
  `poll_changes`, `unsubscribe`, `import_asset`); `ChangeRecord` object
  facts gain `face`. §12: replace "M5 adds …" by the recorded extensions.

FORMULAS §8.2; DESIGN §7 Smaller decisions. | The authority cannot know the GM's viewport; `beside` had no placement rule. |

Schema `Rejection`; FIXTURES §6; FORMULAS §8.1. | FIXTURES §6 predicts these reasons; primitive reasons stay distinguishable. |

A binder is an object tagged `binder`; dropping a template onto a binder's contents element gives a template (one `transact`: `spawn` as `$copy`, then `set_template_flag` `$copy` true), while dropping onto any other contents element copies an instance. | The recipient must hold a reusable template that makes working copies; one atomic group keeps undo whole. |

title: Authority: asset generation in save bookkeeping
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Persistence ("references to assets (images) stored beside it"; saves atomic, two failure stages) and the autosave decision D24 as recorded by vtt-5su.2; review r2 finding 7; review r3 finding 13.

Save bookkeeping for table assets, split from vtt-3l6.16 so the persistence change is reviewed on its own. Exclusive files: additive edit after vtt-5su.4 merged: `packages/authority/src/host/table-host.ts`; tests `packages/authority/test/host/asset-generation.test.ts`.

- `TableHost.addAsset(path)`: adds a relative asset path to the host's asset list, deduplicated; a new path increments `assetsGeneration` (starting at 0 on open); `assets` returns the current list.
- Dirty state is the pair `(revision, assetsGeneration)`. Each save captures the pair and the asset list synchronously when it starts and passes that list to `saveTable`; on `saved` it records the captured pair as saved; `saved_not_durable` and `failed` do not mark it saved (retried as today, vtt-5su.4). A new asset schedules the regular autosave exactly like a commit (debounce, max delay); `save()` and coalescing compare pairs, so a save requested after an import at an already-saved revision runs, and an import during an in-flight save leaves the host dirty and gets a follow-up save; `close()` saves when the current pair differs from the saved pair.

Done when: tests with fake timers, a temp directory and the fs seam show: `addAsset` of a known path does not bump the generation; on an already-saved table, `addAsset` without any commit followed by `save()` writes a file listing it; an `addAsset` while a delayed save is in flight is followed by a second save that lists it, and the first save's file does not; `addAsset` alone triggers the autosave; `close()` right after an `addAsset` saves and the reopened file lists it; a save that ends `saved_not_durable` after an `addAsset` leaves the pair unsaved and is retried; the existing vtt-5su.4 tests still pass; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: writing image files, HTTP routes and the upload helper (vtt-3l6.16); garbage collection (vtt-qf5.12); compaction policy (vtt-qf5.6).

Depends on: vtt-5su.4, vtt-3l6.2.

title: UI: dependency tracing
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.6 **Dependency tracing** ("Hovering a formula highlights the objects and zones it references on the canvas, filtered by what the viewer may see. Hovering a zone highlights its contents"), §4.4 (presentation filtered by the viewer); FORMULAS.md §9; docs/PROTOCOL.md §9 (`explain_cell`, `zones`); decision Q13 of the M4 plan; review r1 findings 3, 10; review r2 findings 10, 13; review r3 finding 10.

Exclusive files: `packages/ui/src/inspector/tracing.ts`, tests `packages/ui/test/inspector/tracing.test.ts`, `tracing-integration.test.tsx`. Adds its own sorted `export * from "./<module>"` lines to `packages/ui/src/index.ts` (CLAUDE.md package index rule).

- `startTracing({session, ui}): () => void` (the sole writer of `UiStore.highlight`): watches `UiStore.hoveredCell` (set by vtt-3l6.11 rows and vtt-3l6.13's formula bar) and `UiStore.hoveredZone` (set by the select tool's hover, vtt-3l6.7, and the object list, vtt-3l6.12).
  - Hovered formula cell → `explain_cell {object, cell, depth: 1, viewer}` through `session.client`; every dependency node with a non-null `object` other than the cell's own object (cells and `exists` nodes) is highlighted.
  - Hovered zone → `zones {board, viewer}`; that zone's `contents` are highlighted.
  - Precedence: a hovered zone wins over a hovered cell; when both clear, the highlight clears.
  - Requests and their cache are keyed `(viewerKey, board, revision, target)`; a response whose key no longer equals the current key (hover moved, viewer switched, board switched, revision advanced) is dropped; a viewer switch at an unchanged revision recomputes for the new viewer; the disposer clears the highlight and drops pending responses.

Done when: controller tests with a fake client show cache hits per key, dropped late responses after the hover moved, zone-over-cell precedence and fallback, and recomputation on a viewer switch at an unchanged revision; integration tests (jsdom, vtt-3l6.21's helper, rendering vtt-3l6.11's real `CellList`/`CellRow` for the hovered object and driving hover with user-event) show: hovering the goblin's `hit` row highlights the die on it; hovering, as Aldric, a cell whose formula reads a GM-only object highlights nothing from that object; leaving a row before its explanation returns leaves no highlight; hovering a zone while a cell is hovered switches to the zone's contents and back to the cell's dependencies when the zone hover ends; with a zone hovered, switching to Aldric at an unchanged revision refreshes with Aldric's `zones` result; with `hoveredZone` set to a room zone lying over an imported map (as the object list sets it), the tokens inside the room are highlighted; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: setting hover state (vtt-3l6.7, vtt-3l6.11, vtt-3l6.12, vtt-3l6.13); drawing highlights (vtt-3l6.5, vtt-3l6.6).

Depends on: vtt-3l6.21, vtt-3l6.4, vtt-3l6.11, vtt-5su.16.

Exports: startTracing({session, ui}), TracingSession, TracingUi, tracedObjects, zoneContents.

title: UI: interaction runtime and React binding
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Platform, §7 Undo, §5.2 (writes carry their base revision) as written by vtt-3l6.2; docs/PROTOCOL.md §4, §6; decision Q10 of the M4 plan; review r2 findings 3, 4, 8, 12; review r3 findings 1, 2.

The interaction runtime: executes vtt-3l6.22's effects against real ports and binds them to React. Exclusive files: `packages/ui/src/interaction/runtime.ts`, `packages/ui/src/interaction/use-interaction.ts`, tests `packages/ui/test/interaction/runtime.test.ts`, `packages/ui/test/interaction/contract-composition.test.tsx`. Adds its own sorted `export * from "./<module>"` lines to `packages/ui/src/index.ts` (CLAUDE.md package index rule).

- `createInteractionRuntime({registry, inputs: RuntimeInputs, toolContext: ToolContext, ui: UiStore, editor: EditorPort, whenRevision: (r) => Promise<void>})` (`RuntimeInputs` and `ToolContext` from vtt-3l6.22, implemented by vtt-3l6.21; `whenRevision` is vtt-3l6.4's; `EditorPort` = `{open({stamp, object, cell?}), close()}`, exported from this file, implemented by vtt-3l6.13). For each event it builds a `ReducerInput` from `inputs` (`scene()`, `views`, `viewport()`, `activeBoard()`, `viewer()`, `revision()`) and `ui` (selection, camera), calls `reduce`, and executes the effects in order. It keeps every tool's state, so a `settled` result goes to the tool whose effect started it (by `interactionId`), active or not.
  - `write` → `toolContext.write.write(ops, {baseRevision: stamp.baseRevision, label})`; on settle it dispatches `settled`; on `committed` it runs the continuations in order only if the interaction was not cancelled and `stamp.board` is still the active board; otherwise none (the write still applies to `stamp.board`; a non-committed outcome is already a notice from vtt-3l6.21).
  - `upload` → `toolContext.upload(file)`, `pick_file` → `toolContext.pickFile(accept)`, each dispatching `settled` with its stamp's `interactionId`.
  - Lifecycle (review r3 finding 1; the same policy as vtt-3l6.8): the runtime subscribes to `inputs.onChange`; a board or viewer change, Escape or a tool switch calls the active tool's `cancel`, which ends unfinished gestures only (drags, marquees, polygon drafts, a file picker whose dialog is dismissed). A started upload always finishes on its stamped board: its `uploaded` result still reaches the originating tool, which creates the object on `stamp.board`; selection and tool continuations are skipped when the board or tool changed meanwhile. A pending write is always awaited; a non-committed outcome produces its notice.
  - `previews` with `hold` are kept until `whenRevision(committed revision)` resolves and cleared at once on any other outcome or on cancel; `camera` → `toolContext.camera.set`; `select`, `hover`, `set_tool` → `UiStore` setters; `notice` → `toolContext.notify`; `open_editor`/`close_editor` → `EditorPort`.
- `useInteraction({runtime})` returns `{overlays: ToolOverlay[], previews: Previews, handlers}`; `handlers` match vtt-3l6.6's `BoardCanvas` `onEvent`; vtt-3l6.17 passes `previews` into `buildScene` (vtt-3l6.5) and `overlays` to `BoardCanvas`.

- Amended for M5 (vtt-1xv.1, M5 plan decision Q1 A2), additive: `createInteractionRuntime` takes optional `extensions: {effects?: Record<string, (effect, ctx: {toolContext, ui, editor}) => Promise<unknown> | void>; continuations?: Record<string, (id: ObjectId | null, payload: unknown) => void>}`. An `extension` effect is dispatched to `extensions.effects[name]`; a returned promise is awaited and its value dispatched as `settled {interactionId: stamp.interactionId, outcome: {type: "extension", name, result}}` to the originating tool, under the same lifecycle as writes (stamp, cancellation, late results after a board or viewer change still settle but run no continuations). An `extension` continuation runs `extensions.continuations[name]` in list order on `committed`, under the same conditions as other continuations. An unknown extension name pushes a warning notice and does nothing else. `EditorPort.open` takes the optional `rect` of vtt-3l6.22's `open_editor`. Data drops (M5 plan review r1 finding 10): the runtime also takes optional `dataDropHandlers: DataDropHandler[]` with `DataDropHandler = (event: DataDropEvent, input: ReducerInput) => Effect[] | null` (exported from this file); every `data_drop` event is offered to the handlers in order before the active tool, whatever tool is active; the first non-null result's effects are executed (writes under the same stamp rules as tool effects: the handler stamps them at the drop) and the event goes no further; when every handler returns null the event goes to the active tool as before.

Done when: runtime tests with fake ports show: a write uses its stamp's `baseRevision` after the revision advanced; continuations run in order (select created, then `set_tool select`) on `committed`, and with the Shift decision recorded the tool stays; `select_created` in a mixed transaction (a `set_value`, a `create_object`, a `spawn`) selects the records matching the given `op_index` values; a board switch during a pending upload still creates the object on the stamped board and changes neither selection nor tool; a tool switch during a pending upload creates it and keeps the new tool; a tool switch during a pending write runs no continuation and still shows a rejection notice; a viewer change via `onChange` cancels a drag (no write); a held preview stays until `whenRevision` resolves and clears on rejection and on cancel. The contract-composition test (jsdom) wires vtt-3l6.4's real session (in-process authority via vtt-3l6.21's helper), vtt-3l6.21's `UiStore`, `RuntimeInputs` and write port, this runtime and hook, and vtt-3l6.6's `BoardCanvas` with a recording renderer, with no casts or adapters, plus a real view-reading tool defined in the test file (on pointer down it hit-tests `input.scene` with vtt-3l6.5's `hitTest`, reads the hit object's `ObjectView` through `input.views`, and on pointer up writes a `move` of it): a drag over a token on a real board view commits the move, and a wheel event changes the stored camera; an extension effect with a registered handler settles back to its tool with the handler's result, an unknown extension name pushes one warning notice, an extension continuation runs after `select_created` with the created id, and `open_editor` passes `rect` to `EditorPort.open` (Q1 A2); a `data_drop` handled by a registered data-drop handler executes its effects and does not reach the active tool, and one every handler declines reaches the active tool, with `select` and with a second registered tool active (review r1 finding 10); `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: the contracts and the reducer (vtt-3l6.22); concrete tools (vtt-3l6.7, vtt-3l6.8, vtt-3l6.9); the editor (vtt-3l6.13); app composition (vtt-3l6.17).

Depends on: vtt-3l6.22, vtt-3l6.21, vtt-3l6.6.

title: UI: interaction contracts and navigation reducer
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Platform (canvas scene, DOM chrome, in-place editing as a DOM overlay), §4.4 (covers above everything), §4.6 On the canvas, §7 Undo (writes carry the revision their interaction began on), all as written by vtt-3l6.2; docs/PROTOCOL.md §4 (`TransactResult` records with `op_index`), §6 (`base_revision`); review r1 findings 1, 2, 4; review r2 findings 3, 4, 8, 12; review r3 finding 2.

The public interaction contracts and the pure navigation reducer. Types and pure functions only: no session, no React, no promises executed. The runtime is vtt-3l6.23. Exclusive files: `packages/ui/src/interaction/contracts.ts`, `events.ts`, `tool.ts`, `overlays.ts`, `effects.ts`, `machine.ts`, `registry.ts`, tests `packages/ui/test/interaction/contracts.test.ts`, `machine.test.ts`. Adds its own sorted `export * from "./<module>"` lines to `packages/ui/src/index.ts` (CLAUDE.md package index rule).

- `contracts.ts` (review r2 finding 3; implemented elsewhere, defined only here):
  - `WriteOutcome` = `{status: "committed"; revision; index; created: {op_index, id}[]; copies: {op_index, root, copies}[]; bindings}` | `{status: "rejected"; rejection; op_index?}` | `{status: "uncertain"; reason}` | `{status: "failed"; error}`.
  - `WritePort = {write(ops: WireOp[], opts: {baseRevision: number; label?: string}): Promise<WriteOutcome>}` (implemented by vtt-3l6.21).
  - `CameraPort = {get(): Camera; set(camera: Camera): void}` (camera state lives in vtt-3l6.21's `UiStore`).
  - `ToolContext = {activeBoard(): BoardId | null; viewer(): Viewer; revision(): number; camera: CameraPort; write: WritePort; notify(level, text): void; pickFile(accept): Promise<File | null>; upload(file): Promise<{path; width; height}>}` (implemented by vtt-3l6.21's `createToolContext`, with `pickFile` and `upload` supplied by vtt-3l6.17).
  - `Viewport = {width: number; height: number; dpr: number}` (CSS pixels).
  - `RuntimeInputs = {views(id): ObjectView | null; scene(): Scene; viewport(): Viewport; activeBoard(): BoardId | null; viewer(): Viewer; revision(): number; onChange(fn: () => void): () => void}` (review r3 finding 2; implemented by vtt-3l6.21 over the session and `UiStore`; `onChange` fires on board, viewer, revision and viewport changes; vtt-3l6.23 subscribes to it and builds each `ReducerInput` from it).
  - `Previews` = vtt-3l6.5's `ScenePreviews` (re-exported; `buildScene` takes it as `previews`).
  - `InteractionStamp = {interactionId: string; board: BoardId; viewer: Viewer; baseRevision: number}`, captured by a tool when an interaction starts (pointer down, key press, file drop, click) (review r2 finding 8).
- `events.ts`: `InteractionEvent` = pointer down/move/up/cancel `{pointerId, screen, board, button, buttons, modifiers: {shift, alt, ctrl, meta}}` | `double_click` | `wheel {deltaX, deltaY}` | `key_down`/`key_up {key, code, modifiers, inTextField}` | `file_drop {files}` | `settled {interactionId, outcome}` with `outcome` = `{type: "write", result: WriteOutcome}` | `{type: "file_picked", file: File | null}` | `{type: "uploaded", path, width, height}` | `{type: "upload_failed", message}`; all positional events carry `screen` and `board` points.
- `tool.ts`: `ToolId` union (`select`, `token`, `card`, `note`, `zone-rect`, `zone-circle`, `zone-polygon`, `image`); `ToolOptions` tagged per tool (zone tools `{fog: boolean}`); `ToolState<TPhase> = {tool, options, phase: TPhase}`; `Tool<TPhase> = {id, cursor(state), reduce(state, event, input: ReducerInput): {state, effects: Effect[]}, cancel(state): {state, effects}}`; `ReducerInput = {scene: Scene; viewport: Viewport; activeBoard: BoardId | null; viewer: Viewer; revision: number; camera: Camera; selection: ObjectId[]; views: (id) => ObjectView | null}` (a snapshot taken from `RuntimeInputs` and `UiStore`; reducers never call ports; navigation uses `viewport` for `zoomAt`).
- `overlays.ts`: `ToolOverlay` kinds `drag_ghost`, `handles`, `creation_preview`, `polygon_draft` (object-related, drawn before covers) and `marquee`, `crosshair` (chrome, drawn after covers); `OBJECT_OVERLAY_KINDS`, `CHROME_OVERLAY_KINDS`.

title: UI: writes, notices and UI state
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Undo, §5.2 ("Writes … carry the revision they were based on, and are rejected on conflict"); docs/PROTOCOL.md §6 (`base_revision`, stale writes, `uncertain`, retries), §10 (rejections, errors); DESIGN §4.6, §7 as written by vtt-3l6.2 (undo `mine`; stale and uncertain writes shown, never retried); decisions Q9, Q10 of the M4 plan; review r1 findings 1, 10, 15; review r2 finding 3; review r3 findings 2, 11, 14.

The UI's write side, notices, local UI state and React bindings, on top of vtt-3l6.4's session. Exclusive files: `packages/ui/src/session/writes.ts`, `packages/ui/src/session/notices.ts`, `packages/ui/src/session/hooks.ts`, `packages/ui/src/state/ui-state.ts`, `packages/ui/src/state/runtime-inputs.ts`, `packages/ui/src/state/camera-store.ts`, `packages/ui/test/support/authority.ts` (the shared helper later beads import: starts an in-process authority, in memory or on a temp file, on port 0 with given `allowOrigins` and optional `http` handlers, returns `{url, token, host, server, client(name)}` and a cleanup), tests `packages/ui/test/session/writes.test.ts`, `packages/ui/test/session/notices.test.ts`, `packages/ui/test/state/ui-state.test.ts`, `packages/ui/test/session/hooks.test.tsx`. Adds its own sorted `export * from "./<module>"` lines to `packages/ui/src/index.ts` (CLAUDE.md package index rule).

- `createWritePort(session): WritePort` implementing vtt-3l6.22's `WritePort` exactly (`write(ops, {baseRevision, label?}): Promise<WriteOutcome>`, `WriteOutcome` as defined there; review r2 finding 3); review r1 finding 1: `baseRevision` is required and is sent unchanged as `base_revision` through `transactWithRetry(client, ops, {label, base_revision: baseRevision, retry: {timeoutMs: 10000}})`; the session never substitutes its latest revision. Callers capture it when an interaction begins (pointer down, editor open, formula bar focus) or at the click for instantaneous commands. A rejection pushes a notice from `describeRejection` (vtt-3l6.3); `stale_write` names the conflicting groups' labels and actors; `uncertain` pushes a sticky notice "may or may not have been applied: <label>"; nothing is retried or rebased.
- `undo(session)`: `undo {target: {type:"mine"}}`, pushing "Undid: <label>" or the refusal (`nothing_to_undo`, `undo_conflict`). `save(session)`; `save` events tracked as `{status, revision}`; `failed` and `saved_not_durable` push notices. Connection notices from vtt-3l6.4 (`onConnectionNotice`) become notices.
- `notices.ts` (sole owner of stickiness and expiry, review r3 finding 14): `Notice = {id, level: "info" | "success" | "warning" | "error", kind?: "stale" | "uncertain", text}`, `NoticeStore` (`push`, `dismiss`, `list`); one policy: `info` and `success` notices expire after 6 s (injectable clock); `warning`, `error` and every `stale`/`uncertain` notice stay until dismissed. vtt-3l6.17 only presents them and calls `dismiss`.
- `ui-state.ts`: `UiStore` = `{selection: ObjectId[], focusedCell: {object, cell} | null, hover: ObjectId | null, hoveredCell: {object, cell} | null, hoveredZone: ObjectId | null, highlight: ObjectId[], tool: {id, options}, camera: Camera, viewport: Viewport}` with setters (`select`, `focusCell`, `setHover`, `setHoveredCell`, `setHoveredZone`, `setHighlight`, `setTool(id, options?)`, `setCamera`, `setViewport`) and `cameraPort(): CameraPort` (vtt-3l6.22's interface; the only owner of camera state); `activeBoard` and `viewer` are read from and set through vtt-3l6.4's session (`setView`). Writers of `hoveredCell` are vtt-3l6.11 and vtt-3l6.13; `hover` and `hoveredZone` are written by vtt-3l6.23's runtime from the select tool's `hover` effect (vtt-3l6.7) and `hoveredZone` also by the object list (vtt-3l6.12); `highlight` is written only by tracing (vtt-3l6.24) (review r1 finding 10). Selection changes call `session.watchObjects`.
- `runtime-inputs.ts` (review r3 finding 2): `createRuntimeInputs(session, ui): RuntimeInputs` (vtt-3l6.22's interface): `views` = vtt-3l6.4's `objectView` (null when absent); `scene()` = vtt-3l6.5's `buildScene` over the current board view and covers, viewer, selection and highlight, with no previews (memoized per revision, viewer, board and selection); `viewport()` from `UiStore`; `activeBoard`, `viewer`, `revision` from the session; `onChange` fires on any change of board, viewer, revision or viewport. `createToolContext(session, ui, {pickFile, upload}): ToolContext` assembles the remaining ports (`write` = `createWritePort(session)`, `camera` = `ui.cameraPort()`, `notify` → `NoticeStore`).
- `camera-store.ts` (review r3 finding 11): `createCameraStore({ui, session, storage = localStorage})` with `restore(board): boolean` and `save(board)`, keyed by (`table.id ?? table.path`, board), every storage access in try/catch; `connect()` subscribes to the session: on an active-board change it saves the camera of the board being left and restores the new board's stored camera; when nothing is stored it marks the board `needsFit` (vtt-3l6.10's first-visit fit consumes and clears the mark).
- `hooks.ts`: `useSession(selector)`, `useUi(selector)`, `useNotices()` over `useSyncExternalStore`.

Done when: tests with the shared helper show: a write carries exactly the given `baseRevision`; the review r1 finding 1 scenario: the session begins an edit at revision r, a second client writes the same cell (r+1) and the session processes that commit, the session then submits with `baseRevision` r → `rejected` `stale_write`, a notice names the second client's label, and the second client's value is unchanged; a write with the current revision commits; `undo` undoes the session's own group and not a newer group of the other client, and a refused undo pushes the `undo_conflict` message; `save` on a file-backed host tracks `saved`; a forced `uncertain` (server dropped after the send, session changed) pushes a sticky notice; notices expire with a fake clock; notices: `info`/`success` expire after 6 s and `warning`/`error`/`stale`/`uncertain` do not (fake clock); `RuntimeInputs.onChange` fires on a board switch, a viewer switch, a commit and `setViewport`, and `scene()` reflects a commit; the camera store saves board A's camera on switching to B, restores it on returning to A, marks an unseen board `needsFit`, and tolerates a throwing `localStorage`; `UiStore` setters notify subscribers, `setTool` keeps options and `cameraPort()` reads and sets the camera; a type test assigns `createWritePort(session)` to `WritePort` and `cameraPort()` to `CameraPort` without casts; a jsdom test renders components with `useSession`, `useUi` and `useNotices` and re-renders on a commit and on a notice; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: connection, subscriptions and viewer switching (vtt-3l6.4); the interaction contracts and runtime (vtt-3l6.22, vtt-3l6.23); components (vtt-3l6.10, vtt-3l6.11, vtt-3l6.12, vtt-3l6.13, vtt-3l6.17).

Depends on: vtt-3l6.4, vtt-3l6.3, vtt-3l6.2, vtt-3l6.22, vtt-3l6.5.

title: MCP: import an image asset from a local path
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §5.2 ("anything a human can do through the UI must be
expressible through this surface"), §7 Revisions and assets as amended by
vtt-3l6.2; docs/PROTOCOL.md §1 (`POST /assets`), §11 (MCP tools, `import_asset`)
as amended by vtt-3l6.2; decision Q4 as amended (plan-m4-decisions.md, 1).

Closes the agent-parity gap for images. Exclusive files:
`packages/authority/src/mcp/import-asset.ts`, test
`packages/authority/test/mcp/import-asset.test.ts`; additive edits after their
owners merged: registration through `createMcpServer`'s `extensions` hook
(vtt-5su.11) in `packages/authority/src/bin/mcp.ts` (vtt-5su.17); the sorted
line `export * from "./mcp/import-asset"` in `packages/authority/src/index.ts`.

- Tool `import_asset {path: string, slug?: string}` (strict input schema):
  the MCP process reads the local file at `path` (absolute, or relative to
  its working directory), checks it with the same type and size rules as
  vtt-3l6.16 (`MAX_ASSET_BYTES`, PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF magic bytes) before sending,
  POSTs it to `/assets` at the authority's http origin (derived from the
  connection's ws url: same host and port, `http:`) with `Authorization:
  Bearer <token>` (the connection's current credentials, also after a
  discovery refresh) and `X-Filename`/`X-Slug`, and returns
  `{path}` as `structuredContent` plus a text block; the agent then writes
  the `image` cell with `transact`. Errors (`isError: true`): file missing or
  unreadable, unsupported type, too large, HTTP 401/409/413/415 mapped to a
  message, and the connection gate of PROTOCOL §11 (a connection error
  answers that error and sends nothing).
- The tool description says the returned path goes into an object's `image`
  cell (DESIGN §4.6 Appearance cells).

Done when: tests with a real in-process authority on a temp table file
(with vtt-3l6.16's handler) and the MCP server through an in-memory MCP client
transport show: importing a PNG returns a path listed in `host.assets`, a
following `transact` setting `image` to it commits, and `GET /assets/<path>`
returns the bytes; a missing file, an SVG and an oversize file are
`isError` and nothing is uploaded (server request count); a wrong token
(credentials replaced) maps 401 to an error; an in-memory authority maps 409;
while the client reports `disconnected` the tool returns that error; the
tool appears in `tools/list` with its schema; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`,
`pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: importing from URLs; the HTTP endpoint itself (vtt-3l6.16); the UI
image tool (vtt-3l6.8); MCP Streamable HTTP (vtt-y1w.10).

Depends on: vtt-3l6.16, vtt-5su.11, vtt-5su.17.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text: API amendment from vtt-3l6.14 (accepted by the orchestrator): HttpHandler is (req, res, ctx: {url, port, token}) => boolean | Promise<boolean>; a two-argument handler still type-checks. createUiHttpHandler({uiDir: string | null; url?; token?}) takes url/token from ctx when omitted, because with --port 0 or a generated token they are unknown before startServer returns. Register handlers via startServer({http: [...]}). The whole /ui-assets/ namespace belongs to the UI handler; /assets/ handlers (vtt-3l6.16) and import_asset (vtt-3l6.20) go before or after it in the http array as the bead text says.

Followup filed in Polish: public credentials getter on ProtocolClient. title: Authority and protocol: id_base for created objects and absent-cell visibility in GM views
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §5.3 ("Object ids … must be human-meaningful by
default"), §4.1 Identity (allocation from `next_seq`, reserved ids skipped),
§4.4 (per-cell visibility is metadata valid for absent cells), §4.2
(overrides; replacing a formula), §7 (operation records, undo); docs/PROTOCOL.md
§5 (`create_object`, `set_value`), §7.2 (GM object views) and §12 (additive extension) as
amended by vtt-3l6.2; review r1 finding 9 (absent-cell visibility rules must
be visible to the GM's inspector); review r3 finding 3 (replacing a formula,
including on structural cells, needs one invariant-preserving write).

Three additive authority/protocol extensions the M4 UI needs. Exclusive files: tests
`packages/authority/test/store/create-id-base.test.ts`,
`packages/protocol/test/create-object-id-base.test.ts`,
`packages/authority/test/protocol/create-id-base.test.ts`,
`packages/protocol/test/absent-cell-visibility.test.ts`,
`packages/authority/test/protocol/absent-cell-visibility.test.ts`,
`packages/authority/test/store/replace-formula.test.ts`,
`packages/authority/test/protocol/set-value-replace.test.ts`; additive
edits after their owners merged:
`packages/authority/src/store/structural.ts` (M2 `createObject` gains
`idBase?: string`: with no explicit id, allocate `<idBase>_<n>` exactly as
spawn allocates copies; `idBase` must be id syntax, else `invalid`; both
`id` and `idBase` is `invalid`), `packages/authority/src/store/edits.ts` (M2:
`replaceFormula(tx, obj, cell, value)`: on a cell whose stored content is a
formula, with or without override, records one cell effect from that
formula state to the literal `value` (the override is gone with the
formula); on a literal or absent cell it behaves exactly as `writeValue`;
the same guards and type checks as `writeValue`, so protected cells (`id`,
`contents`, `container`, `board`, `is_zone`) are refused and structural
cells such as `visible_to`, `position`, `rotation` are allowed),
`packages/protocol/src/ops.ts` (vtt-5su.3: `create_object.id_base?` and
`set_value.replace?: true`), `packages/authority/src/protocol/commands.ts`
(vtt-5su.5: passes `id_base` through, a bound `as` still binds the allocated
id; `set_value` with `replace: true` calls `replaceFormula`, without it
`writeValue` as before; declared keys unchanged), `packages/protocol/src/views.ts` (vtt-5su.3:
`ObjectView.absent_cell_visibility?: Record<string, WireViewers>`, optional)
and `packages/authority/src/protocol/views.ts` (vtt-5su.6: GM views carry the
object's `cell_visibility` entries whose cell name is not in the view's
`cells`, whenever there is at least one; character views never carry it).

Done when: `createObject` with `idBase: "zone"` yields `zone_<n>` and skips a
retired `zone_<n>`; the op round-trips through the protocol schema and a
`transact` (also with `as`, the binding resolving to `zone_<n>`); `id` +
`id_base` is `invalid`; an invalid base is `invalid`; an existing
`create_object` without `id_base` still allocates `obj_<n>`; a GM view of an
object with a visibility entry for an absent cell `secret` carries
`absent_cell_visibility.secret`, loses it after the entry is cleared and
after a cell `secret` is created (then it is the cell's `visibility`), and a
character view never carries the field; a subscription delta includes the
field change; the schema accepts views without the field (older servers);
`replaceFormula` on a user formula cell `hp` (overridden) and on a zone's
`visible_to` formula leaves a literal, no override, one cell effect each,
undo restores the formula (and the override), and a later edit of the same
cell makes that undo `undo_conflict`; on `contents` it is `protected_cell`;
`set_value {replace: true}` round-trips through the protocol schema and a
`transact` with the same results, and `set_value` without `replace` on a
formula cell still overrides;
`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: renaming ids (never); UI use (vtt-3l6.8, vtt-3l6.11).

Depends on: vtt-3l6.2, vtt-5su.3, vtt-5su.5, vtt-5su.6.

title: UI: app shell and composition
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Platform ("the scene is drawn on a canvas and the
chrome … is DOM"), §8.1 (undo of whole actions; save), §7 Undo; docs/
PROTOCOL.md §2 (connection errors `disconnected`, `recovering`,
`unauthorized`, `wrong_table`; explicit credentials make `unauthorized`
terminal), §6 (`uncertain`); DESIGN §4.4, §4.6 as amended by vtt-3l6.2
(covers above every object-related overlay); decisions Q9, Q14 of the M4
plan; review r1 findings 2, 4, 13; review r2 findings 3, 8, 13; review r3 findings 2, 11, 14.

Exclusive files: `packages/ui/src/App.tsx`, `src/main.tsx`,
`src/app/Toolbar.tsx`, `StatusBar.tsx`, `Notices.tsx`, `keybindings.ts`,
tests `packages/ui/test/app/*.test.tsx` (replaces the scaffold's
`test/app.test.tsx`). Adds its own sorted `export * from "./<module>"`
lines to `packages/ui/src/index.ts` (CLAUDE.md package index rule).

- `main.tsx`: `readBootstrap()`; without it a "No authority running" screen
  with the `vtt-serve` command; else `createTableSession` and `<App session
  createRenderer?>`.
- Layout: toolbar (tools registered in vtt-3l6.22's `ToolRegistry`: the
  select tool of vtt-3l6.7 wrapped by vtt-3l6.9's `withHandles`, and the
  vtt-3l6.8 tools; the fog toggle edits the zone tools' typed options through
  `UiStore.setTool`; view-as menu, undo, save), board tabs above the canvas,
  formula bar above the canvas, inspector on the right; `BoardCanvas` fed
  with `buildScene` (scene objects and `objectOverlays`) from the board view,
  `UiStore` and the `previews` returned by `useInteraction`, the hook's
  `overlays`, and the `ImageCache` with `assetUrl`; vtt-3l6.23's runtime
  created with `inputs: createRuntimeInputs(session, ui)` and `toolContext:
  createToolContext(session, ui, {pickFile: a hidden file input, upload:
  createImageBitmap measurement + vtt-3l6.16's uploadAsset})` (both
  vtt-3l6.21), `whenRevision` from vtt-3l6.4 and `editor:
  createInPlaceEditorPort(...)` (vtt-3l6.13); `BoardCanvas` resizes call
  `ui.setViewport`; vtt-3l6.21's camera store is connected on mount and
  vtt-3l6.10's `useFirstVisitFit` mounted; the in-place
  editor in the canvas overlay; `startTracing({session, ui})` (vtt-3l6.24)
  started on mount and disposed on unmount. The
  composition keeps the render order of vtt-3l6.6 (objects, object-related
  overlays, covers, chrome) and adds nothing drawn above covers except chrome.
- `StatusBar`: connection state (banner for `disconnected`/`recovering`,
  terminal message for `unauthorized` and `wrong_table`; the `unauthorized`
  banner explains that the authority restarted with a new token and offers
  "Reload", which reloads the page to fetch a new bootstrap token, review r1
  finding 13), revision, save
  status ("Saved", "Saving…", "Save failed: …"); `Notices`: presents vtt-3l6.21's `NoticeStore` list with a dismiss
  control per notice (stickiness and expiry are vtt-3l6.21's).
- `keybindings.ts`: Ctrl/Cmd+Z → `undo(session)`; Ctrl/Cmd+S →
  `save(session)` (default prevented) (vtt-3l6.21); tool keys V (select), T (token), C
  (card), N (note), R (zone rect), O (zone circle), P (zone polygon), I
  (image); none fire while focus is in a text field.

Done when: jsdom tests with an in-process authority and a recording renderer
show: without bootstrap the start screen renders; with it the app shows the
GM board tab, toolbar and an empty inspector; creating a token with the
toolbar tool and clicking it fills the inspector; Ctrl+Z undoes it and a
notice names the label; Ctrl+S produces a save event (file-backed host) and
the status shows "Saved"; camera persistence: pan board A, switch to B,
return to A and A's camera is restored; the first visit of a board fits its
items once its board view has arrived; dismissing a sticky error notice
removes it; same-token transport recovery: the helper drops
the app's socket on the same server, the disconnected banner shows and
clears automatically after resync; normal restart: the authority restarts
with a new token, the app reaches the terminal `unauthorized` state and the
banner's "Reload" calls `location.reload` (spied); a selected token under a
cover in a character view (GM selection kept while switching to view-as)
draws no outline after the cover (recording renderer call order); the
`wrong_table` and `unauthorized` messages render from a fake session
snapshot; a stale-write notice from another client's concurrent write
appears; a test runs Vite's `build()` API on the UI with `outDir` in a temp directory
and it succeeds (no browser automation, Q16); `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`,
`pnpm test` exit 0.

title: Authority and UI: image assets
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Persistence and Revisions and assets ("references
to assets (images) stored beside it"; "Asset paths in the file are relative
to the file's directory"; "how an image cell names an asset is M4's
decision"), §5.2, §8.1 (objects with image), §8.4 step 3 (import the dungeon
map); docs/PROTOCOL.md §1 (`GET /assets/<path>`, `POST /assets`) as amended
by vtt-3l6.2; decision Q4; review r2 findings 1, 7; review r3 findings 9, 13.

Exclusive files: `packages/authority/src/host/assets.ts`,
`packages/authority/src/server/http-assets.ts`, tests
`packages/authority/test/host/assets.test.ts`,
`packages/authority/test/server/http-assets.test.ts`;
`packages/ui/src/assets/upload.ts`, test `packages/ui/test/assets/upload.test.ts`;
sorted lines in
`packages/authority/src/index.ts` and `packages/ui/src/index.ts`. Wiring into
`vtt-serve` and the dev proxy are vtt-3l6.15's; `TableHost.addAsset` and its
save bookkeeping are vtt-3l6.25's. It never edits `packages/ui/package.json`
or the lockfile (the `@vtt/authority` dev dependency comes from vtt-3l6.4).

- `importAsset(host, {bytes, filename, slug?}) → {path}`: refuses an in-memory
  host; accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF by magic bytes (SVG refused: it can
  carry script), at most 50 MiB (`MAX_ASSET_BYTES`); path `<table
  basename>.assets/<slug>-<first 8 hex of sha256>.<ext>` relative to the
  table's directory (`slug` = the given slug or the file stem, lowercased,
  non-`[a-z0-9_-]` → `-`, at most 40 chars); written with temp file + rename
  into that directory (created if missing); the same bytes and slug return the
  same path without rewriting; it then calls vtt-3l6.25's `host.addAsset(path)`,
so the next save lists it.
- `createAssetHttpHandler({host, token}): HttpHandler` (vtt-3l6.14's handler type;
  the `Host` check is vtt-3l6.14's): `POST /assets` with `Authorization: Bearer
  <token>` (constant-time comparison), body = bytes, `X-Filename` and
  optional `X-Slug` (URL-encoded) → 201 `{"path"}`; 401 bad token, 413 too
  large, 415 unsupported type, 409 in-memory table. It handles `/assets/` only
  (built UI bundles are under `/ui-assets/`, vtt-3l6.14). `GET /assets/<path>`: only
  a path listed in `host.assets` (normalized, no traversal) → the bytes with
  the content type by extension and `Cache-Control: no-store`; else 404.
- UI `upload.ts`: `uploadAsset(file, {token, base = location.origin}) →
  Promise<{path}>` and `assetUrl(path)` = `"/assets/"` + the path's segments
  URI-encoded.

Done when: tests in a temp directory show: importing a PNG writes the file
under `<name>.assets/` and returns the hashed path; a reimport returns the
same path without a second file; an import followed by `host.save()` writes
a file that lists the asset and `loadTable` reports no missing asset; SVG and text bytes are
415; oversize 413; a wrong token 401; an in-memory host 409; GET of the
listed path returns the bytes with `no-store`, of an unlisted or traversal
path 404; an asset listed by a file loaded from disk (not imported) is
served; with a real in-process server (`startServer({http: [handler]})`, Node
environment) `uploadAsset` returns the path and `assetUrl` encodes spaces;
`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: garbage collection of unreferenced assets (Polish); image
tiling for very large maps (vtt-y1w.4); the MCP `import_asset` tool (vtt-3l6.20);
`vtt-serve` wiring and the dev proxy (vtt-3l6.15); the image creation tool
(vtt-3l6.8).

Depends on: vtt-3l6.14, vtt-3l6.2, vtt-3l6.25, vtt-3l6.4.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text: API amendment from vtt-3l6.14 (accepted by the orchestrator): HttpHandler is (req, res, ctx: {url, port, token}) => boolean | Promise<boolean>; a two-argument handler still type-checks. createUiHttpHandler({uiDir: string | null; url?; token?}) takes url/token from ctx when omitted, because with --port 0 or a generated token they are unknown before startServer returns. Register handlers via startServer({http: [...]}). The whole /ui-assets/ namespace belongs to the UI handler; /assets/ handlers (vtt-3l6.16) and import_asset (vtt-3l6.20) go before or after it in the http array as the bead text says.
