title: Schema: document, objects, structural cells, validation
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.1 (objects, identity reservation), §4.3 (zones and boards), §4.4 (stored `visible_to` and per-cell visibility metadata), §7 (canonical schema); FORMULAS.md §3, §3.1 (defaults, literal-only `name` and `tag`, edit-only `shape`); FIXTURES.md §3. All as written by vtt-75c.2 and vtt-o9i.12.

Build the canonical document types in @vtt/schema with zod schemas and an invariant checker, on top of vtt-o9i.2's value, id, shape and cell-content types (not redefined). Adds `zod` 4.6.7 (the version @vtt/fixtures uses) to @vtt/schema.

Files in packages/schema/src/; tests in test/ per file. Package index rule: add only this bead's `export * from "./<module>"` lines to src/index.ts; Biome requires the lines sorted, so place yours in order; never edit other beads' lines.

- ids.ts (exists from vtt-o9i.2): add `BoardId`, `RESERVED_IDS` (`gm`, `all`, `owner`), `isValidId` (matches the existing `ID_PATTERN` and is not reserved).
- shape.ts (exists): add `ShapeSchema`.
- cell.ts (exists): add `Cell = {content: CellContent; override?: Value}` and `CellSchema`; `ValueSchema` and `CellContentSchema` are zod wrappers delegating to `isValue` / `isCellContent`.
- structural.ts: `STRUCTURAL_CELLS`, `StructuralCellSpec`, `structuralDefault(name, obj)`.
- object.ts: `TableObject`, `ActionDef` (`{name, when?, steps: string[]}`, source text), schemas.
- document.ts: `Board = {id: BoardId; name?: string}` (as the fixtures `BoardSchema`), `Snapshot`, `SnapshotSchema`.
- validate.ts: `validateSnapshot(s): Violation[]`.

```ts
type TableObject = {
  id: ObjectId;
  is_template: boolean; is_zone: boolean; is_character: boolean;
  tag: string[];                                   // literal list of text
  shape: Shape | null;                             // relative to the anchor
  board: BoardId | null;                           // non-null iff on a board
  contents: ObjectId[];                            // owning, ordered
  cells: Record<string, Cell>;                     // ordinary cells plus name, visible_to, owner,
                                                   // template, face_up, opaque, position, rotation, z
  cell_visibility: Record<string, ViewersValue>;   // per-cell visibility, independent of content
  actions: ActionDef[];
};
type Snapshot = { revision: number; next_seq: number; boards: Board[];
                  objects: Record<ObjectId, TableObject>; retired_ids: ObjectId[] };
```

`position` is a cell (a list of two numbers, or a formula, with override support), present iff `board` is non-null; `rotation` and `z` are absent for objects in containers. `container` is never stored. `cells` and `cell_visibility` use null-prototype records or are validated so `__proto__` is rejected as a key (FIXTURES §1); any other non-empty string is a valid cell name.

`cell_visibility` is the canonical per-cell visibility (DESIGN §4.4): a key may name any user cell or any FORMULAS §3.1 structural cell, whether stored as a cell, stored as a field (`tag`, `contents`, `shape`, `is_zone`, …), derived (`container`), or currently absent; the value is a literal viewers value (non-empty; refs inside may dangle). A cell with no entry defaults to its object's visibility. It maps one to one onto the fixture `cell_visibility`.

Ids form one namespace across boards and objects. `retired_ids` is the monotonic set of board and object ids that were removed at some point (by removal or by undoing a creation); together with live ids and `next_seq` it makes every id reserved for the document's lifetime. A live object's or board's id may appear in `retired_ids` (restored by undo); an id is available for a new board or object iff it is neither live (as either) nor retired. `isReserved(snapshot, id)` is exported for the store.

`STRUCTURAL_CELLS` is the canonical table, one entry per FORMULAS §3.1 cell: storage (field or cell), protection (`full` for `id`, `board`, `is_zone`; `membership` for `contents`; `derived` for `container`; `edit_only` for `shape`, which no cell write or action may change and only `setShape` changes; none otherwise), literal type, whether a formula is allowed (all cells except `template`, `tag` and `name`; fields never), how it reads (`shape` as a `ShapeValue`, or empty), and the default when absent:

| Cell | Default |
|---|---|
| name | empty |
| tag | [] |
| visible_to | viewers ["all"] |
| owner, template | empty |
| contents | [] |
| container | empty |
| board, position | empty (in a container) |
| rotation, z | empty (read as 0 by geometry and ordering) |
| face_up | true |
| opaque | false |
| is_zone | false |
| shape | empty (no shape) |

The M1 test host (vtt-o9i.3) carries a copy of this table; vtt-75c.12 switches it to import this one.

`validateSnapshot` returns every violation: ids satisfy `isValidId` and are unique across boards and objects; every key of `objects` equals that object's `id`; `cells` never stores a field-backed or derived structural name (`id`, `tag`, `contents`, `container`, `board`, `shape`, `is_zone`) nor the field names `is_template` and `is_character`; an `override` is present only when `content` is a formula, and an override on a structural cell type-checks like a literal of that cell (e.g. a `position` override is a list of two finite numbers, a `visible_to` override a viewers value); every object is on exactly one board or in exactly one `contents`; containment is acyclic; `contents` and `board` name existing objects and boards; `position` present iff on a board, `position`/`rotation`/`z` absent in a container; literal structural cells type-check (`name` text; `visible_to` viewers; `owner`, `template` ref or empty; `face_up`, `opaque` boolean; `rotation`, `z` number or empty; `position` list of two finite numbers); `opaque` only on `is_zone` objects; `template`, `name` never formulas; every `cell_visibility` value a non-empty viewers value; shapes valid (circle radius > 0, rect width and height > 0, polygon at least three points and simple); `next_seq` a non-negative integer; every `retired_ids` entry a valid id, no duplicates. References inside values may dangle; they are not violations.

Done when: for each violation kind a test builds a minimal snapshot that triggers it and asserts it is reported (and a valid snapshot reports none), including a formula `name`, a formula `template`, an empty viewers value in `cell_visibility`, a duplicate retired id, an object-map key differing from the object's id, a board and an object sharing an id, a stored cell named each of `id`, `tag`, `contents`, `container`, `board`, `shape`, `is_zone`, `is_template`, `is_character`, an override on a literal cell, a `position` override that is not two finite numbers, and a `face_up` override that is not a boolean; a live object and a live board whose ids are in `retired_ids` validate; `isReserved` is true for a live board id, a live object id and a retired id; zod schemas reject unknown keys and a `__proto__` key in `cells` and `cell_visibility`; a snapshot equivalent to the `setup` of fireball.json (written by hand) validates; a snapshot whose objects carry `cell_visibility` entries for `contents` and `tag` (no such cells stored) round-trips through `JSON.stringify` → `SnapshotSchema.parse` deep-equal; a test iterates `STRUCTURAL_CELLS` against the default table above; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); operation records and file envelope (vtt-75c.4); conversion from fixtures (vtt-75c.13); geometry beyond shape validity (vtt-75c.7); face layout (M5); redefining value types (vtt-o9i.2).

Depends on: vtt-o9i.2, vtt-75c.2.

title: Docs: M2 decisions and replay expectation
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.1, §4.3, §4.4, §7 and §10 (decision log); FORMULAS.md §3.1, §6, §8.3; FIXTURES.md §3, §5, §6, §7, §8, §11. Planning bead vtt-75c.1 comments 1 and 2; the orchestrator's decisions on the M1 and M2 plans and on Codex's M2 review.

Write down every semantic decision the M2 beads implement, so each later bead cites a doc section instead of the plan. This is the only M2 bead that edits DESIGN.md, FORMULAS.md or FIXTURES.md. It runs after the M1 docs bead (vtt-o9i.12), which owns the M1 language rows (values, dice, errors, names including literal-only `name`, operators, query order and candidate set, `distance`, budgets, propagation); this bead must not write or rewrite those rows, and refers to them where it touches the same sections. Docs-only except for the additive fixture format change at the end.

Each item is an edit to the named section plus one decision-log row in DESIGN.md §10, dated 2026-11-05.

DESIGN.md §4.1 (objects):
1. `move` never changes the `owner` cell; "moving onto a board ends ownership" becomes "ends containment".
2. `is_character`: a per-object field like `is_template` (not a FORMULAS §3.1 cell), copied on spawn; view-as lists objects with `is_character` true and `is_template` false; a viewer that is not a character sees nothing; `owner` is not validated against it. Fixture runners (the M1 test host and the M2 runner) set it for ids in `setup.characters`.
3. Spawn (also FORMULAS §8.3): generated ids `<original id>_<n>` from the document counter `next_seq`, skipping any reserved id; every copy's `template` refers to its original; the root copy has `is_template: false`, descendants keep theirs; `is_zone`, `is_character`, `tag`, `shape`, `actions` and per-cell visibility are copied; refs inside copied cell values and per-cell visibility that name an object in the copied subtree are remapped to the copy, others kept; formula source is copied verbatim; a container destination without index appends, so successive spawns in one transaction append in call order.
4. Identity: an id is reserved for the document's lifetime once allocated, across boards and objects together (one namespace). `next_seq` only increases and `retired_ids` only grows; user undo never decreases the one or shrinks the other. Creating a board allocates its id; undoing a board's creation removes it and retires the id. Undoing an object's creation removes the objects and retires their ids; undoing a removal restores the objects under their own ids (which stay in `retired_ids`, so allocation never hands them out again). Only historical rewind (replaying or rewinding recorded effects from a snapshot) resets these counters.
5. Removing an object removes its contents recursively; references elsewhere dangle and evaluate to #REF; undo restores the subtree.

FORMULAS.md §3.1 (structural cells):
6. Default column: `name` empty; `tag` `[]`; `visible_to` viewers `all`; `owner`, `template` empty; `contents` `[]`; `container` empty; `board`, `position` empty in a container; `rotation`, `z` empty (read as 0 by geometry and ordering); `face_up` true; `opaque` false; `is_zone` false; `shape` empty. `is_template` and `is_character` are object fields, false by default.
7. `position` is a list of two numbers `[x, y]`, present iff the object is on a board; board units, x right, y down; `rotation` is degrees clockwise on screen about the anchor; empty `rotation` and `z` read as 0.
8. Landing rule: every `move` or `spawn` onto a board (including within the same board) puts the object on top: `z` = 1 + the maximum literal `z` of the other objects on that board (absent or empty as 0), unless the object's `z` holds a formula, which is left alone; `position` is written as a hand edit (a formula position gets an override); `rotation` is kept on board-to-board moves; entering a container deletes `position`, `rotation`, `z` (recorded, so undo restores formulas); after a move to a board `container` is empty.
9. `tag` is literal only; `set(tag, list)` is allowed. `shape` cannot be written by actions or cell writes (`set` on `shape` is refused); it changes only through the `setShape` edit primitive used by the UI and agent (its formula-side value is vtt-o9i.12's row). `template` is set on every spawned copy and is never a formula. (`name` literal-only is vtt-o9i.12's row.)

FORMULAS.md §6 (spatial functions) and DESIGN.md §4.3:
10. Exact spatial semantics live in one pure module, `packages/schema/src/geometry/`. The host returns the literal-geometry candidate set defined in vtt-o9i.12's §6 row (it never evaluates formulas); the authority's spatial index is how the authority computes exactly that set; the evaluator computes membership, overlap and distance; the opaque-cover test uses the same geometry.
11. Geometry tolerance: point membership is boundary inclusive within 1e-9 board units for every shape; for circles the test is distance-based, `sqrt(dx²+dy²) <= r + 1e-9`.
12. Overlap: two footprints overlap iff their intersection has positive area; shapes that touch or penetrate by at most 1e-9 (near-tangent) do not overlap. Explicit exception: a point footprint (shapeless object) overlaps a shape iff the point is in the shape's region (boundary inclusive); two points never overlap. Zones are never in `on()` results. Polygons must be simple.

DESIGN.md §4.4 (visibility):
13. Opaque cover is independent of `z`: an object is covered for a viewer iff it is on the same board as an opaque zone the viewer cannot effectively see and its anchor lies in the zone's region; an object inside a container is covered iff its outermost container is; a zone never covers itself; the renderer still draws the cover above everything.
14. A cell is visible to a viewer only if its object is (`object_visible`, which includes cover); then the cell's own visibility and the face-down rule apply.
15. `visible_to`: an absent cell reads as the default `all`; a present cell's evaluated value is converted with `toViewers` as vtt-o9i.12's row states (so `visible_to = owner` and lists of character refs work), and a value that fails conversion admits nobody. The `owner` viewer entry resolves against the object that holds the viewer set.
15a. Every evaluated visibility input fails closed: a `face_up` that is an error or not a boolean is treated as face down; an `opaque` that is an error or not a boolean is treated as opaque; a zone whose geometry (board, position, rotation, shape) cannot be read or is invalid, and which the viewer cannot see, is treated as covering every object on its board. The GM is unaffected.
16. Per-cell visibility is per-object metadata, `cell_visibility: {cellName: viewers}`, independent of cell content: valid for any user or structural cell name, including cells that are absent or field-backed (`tag`, `contents`, `position`, …); values are literal viewer sets; a cell with no entry defaults to its object's visibility.

DESIGN.md §7 (document, operations, persistence):
17. The operation record: a group holds resolved effects (cell before/after states with cause edit or roll; per-cell visibility changes; field changes; placements; create and remove of whole subtrees; reorders; board changes; id allocation; id retirement), the actor, kind (edit, action, undo), label, origin, `undoes`, `base_revision`, `revision`, and the names of touched objects captured at commit time (for a removed object, its name just before removal). A logged write records the resulting value (`add` logs the sum).
18. Transactions: one transaction is open at a time; the commit point is the moment the new document and the appended group are published; internal synchronization (formula invalidation, index update) runs right after it and before any public commit notification; a listener error is reported separately and never turns a commit into an abort. Before the commit point, a refusal (`Rejected`) becomes a rejection result, and any other error aborts the transaction and propagates unchanged; in both cases no dice entries or randomness are consumed. Every commit carries a change summary (created and removed objects, written cells with before/after, moved objects with derived changes).
19. Undo targets: `latest` (the most recent group that is neither an undo nor already undone; the fixture `undo` step always means this), `actor` (the latest such group by a given actor), `group` (an explicit absolute index). No redo. Undo adds its own group.
20. Undo conflict: target G conflicts with a later group H iff H is not an undo group, H is not undone, and they share a touched key: cell keys; per-cell visibility changes touch the cell's key; the `contents` key of the container at both ends of a move; creating or removing objects touches every key on those objects and the `contents` key of the container they were created in or removed from. Allocation and retirement touch nothing. Undo groups never conflict. An undo whose inverse fails an invariant on commit is refused as `undo_conflict`. This defines "surviving" in FIXTURES §8.
21. Replay and rewind: replaying a group applies its recorded effects and sets `revision` to the group's `revision` (also for groups with no effects); rewinding applies exact historical inverses (an internal representation, never persisted, distinct from user-undo effects; a retirement records exactly the ids it added, so rewind removes exactly those) and sets `revision` to the group's `base_revision`. Comparisons of stored state for replay exclude `revision`.
21a. History invariants (checked on load): retained groups have contiguous absolute indices starting at `first_index`; each group's `revision` is its `base_revision + 1` and each `base_revision` equals the previous group's `revision`; `kind: "undo"` iff `undoes` is present; `undoes` names an earlier index that is not itself an undo group (or an index below `first_index`, compacted away) and no index is undone twice; `undo_barrier` lies in `first_index … next index`; the last retained group's `revision` equals the snapshot's, except when the file was edited by hand (the barrier then equals the next index and the snapshot wins).
22. The file holds a fresh snapshot at every save plus the retained groups as history (absolute group indices, `first_index`, `undo_barrier`); there are no operations "since" the snapshot. A `snapshot_hash` detects hand edits; after one, the snapshot wins and the undo barrier is set to the next absolute group index, so every earlier group stays as record and new groups remain undoable; with an empty retained log the next index is `first_index`. Snapshots are taken at every save and at load (in-memory checkpoints are Polish; autosave cadence is M3). An older `schema_version` migrates step by step. Compaction drops old groups, keeps absolute indices, and raises the barrier to at least `first_index`.
23. Saving is atomic with two failure stages: a failure before the new file replaces the old leaves the old file intact and reports an error; a durability failure after replacement (directory fsync) leaves the new file intact and reports that the save completed but durability was not confirmed.
24. Every group records `base_revision`; stale-write policy belongs to M3's protocol. Asset paths in the file are relative to the file's directory (never absolute); parsing a file is pure and existence of assets is checked only when loading from a path; how an `image` cell names an asset is M4's.
25. Smaller decisions: the `table` destination is resolved by M5 into a board destination (M2 primitives take only board and container destinations); renaming a cell does not rewrite formulas that name it, refuses a structural name at either end and an existing destination cell, and replaces any per-cell visibility recorded for the (absent) destination with the source's; spawn initial cells may be literals or formulas; reordering `contents` by `shuffle` is allowed despite the membership protection.

FIXTURES.md:
26. §3: `cell_visibility` maps onto the canonical per-object metadata of item 16 one to one.
27. §8: confirm one group per non-rejected step; undo adds its own group; undo reverses the most recent non-undo, non-undone group (the engine also supports actor-scoped and explicit-group undo, but the `undo` step always means the default); no redo; "surviving" as item 20.
28. §5: rejected actions consume no dice (dice consumption is transactional); unused entries are an error for complete runs; link the `replay` expectation.
29. §6/§8: set-on-formula, override-on-literal, clear-without-override stay scenario errors in the format, while the engine's `writeValue` on a formula cell overrides and clearing a missing override is refused. Runners implement the rejection protocol for every step type they support (the M2 runner for `set`, `override`, `clear_override`, `move`, `spawn`, `undo`; M5 adds `when_false`, `when_error`, `step_error`).
30. §7: `object_visible` includes cover (item 13); `cell_visible` holds only if `object_visible` holds; formula positions stay in `placement` in the format while canonically `position` is a cell present iff on a board.
31. §11: the replay expectation (below), next to vtt-o9i.12's `#SYNTAX` paragraph.

Fixture format change (additive): a new expectation variant `{ "type": "replay", "note": "optional" }`, allowed at top level and step level. It holds when applying, to the document as it was right after setup, the recorded effects of every group currently in the log, in order, yields a document whose stored state equals the current one, and doing so consumes no dice-script entries and no randomness. "Stored state" is the canonical snapshot (cells as stored: literal, formula source, override; per-cell visibility; placement; contents order; structural fields; `retired_ids`; `next_seq`), never computed formula results and never `revision`. Add `ReplayExpectationSchema` (strict, `type` and optional `note`) to the `ExpectationSchema` union in packages/fixtures/src/schema.ts; the type in types.ts is inferred. Add rows to the §7 table and a §11 paragraph. Append `{ "type": "replay" }` to the `expect` of the last step of every file in packages/fixtures/scenarios/, and to step 1 of fireball.json. Edit those files only to add these entries.

Done when: test/format.test.ts in @vtt/fixtures accepts a top-level and a step-level `replay` and rejects `{ "type": "replay", "extra": 1 }`; test/scenarios.test.ts (unchanged) validates all ten scenarios with the new entries; every numbered item is present with its decision-log row dated 2026-11-05, and none of vtt-o9i.12's rows is rewritten; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: any engine code; the runner; changes to existing expectation or step variants; M1's language decisions (vtt-o9i.12); face layout and show-when (M5).

Depends on: vtt-o9i.12.

title: Formula: fixture scenario runner (set, override, move)
description:
Implements: docs/FIXTURES.md §1 (reading a scenario), §2 (values), §3 (setup), §4 and §11 (`#SYNTAX` as an additive error code, as written by vtt-o9i.12), §6 (`set`, `override`, `clear_override`, `move` only), §7 (`cell` and `cell_error` only); FORMULAS.md §10 (as the acceptance target); the runner-scope decision recorded by vtt-o9i.12.

packages/formula/test/support/runner.ts and test/scenarios.test.ts in @vtt/formula. `runFormulaScenario(scenario): Report` builds a `MemoryHost.fromSetup` (vtt-o9i.15) and an engine (vtt-o9i.9, vtt-o9i.16), then walks the scenario:

1. Top-level `expect`, then each step in order.
2. Steps of type `set`, `override`, `clear_override`, and `move` (board and container destinations) are applied as `MemoryHost` writes (`set`, `override`, `clearOverride`, `move`) and their `Change`s passed to `engine.invalidate`. These are plain content and placement changes in the test host; no log, no groups.
3. At the first step of any other type (`invoke`, `spawn`, `undo`, `bind`), stop applying: that step's and every later step's expectations are skipped with reason `after unsupported step <index> (<type>)`.
4. Expectations of type `cell` and `cell_error` before that point are checked: `engine.value(object, cell)` against the expected value (equality as FIXTURES §7: numbers exact, roll results all fields, lists elementwise and recursive, refs by object, viewers as sets) or the expected error code. All other expectation types (including every visibility expectation: the M1 runner never checks visibility) are skipped with reason `type <type>`.
5. `Report = {title, checked: Location[], skipped: {location, reason}[], failures: {location, expected, actual}[]}`.

test/scenarios.test.ts discovers every scenario (as vtt-o9i.3 does), runs it, asserts no failures, and asserts the coverage against a committed table test/scenario-coverage.ts of exactly which expectations are checked per scenario (scenario title → list of `setup#i` / `step N#i` locations), so coverage can only change on purpose. A scenario added later shows up as an uncovered entry and fails the test until the table is updated.

Coverage table: compute it by running the runner over today's scenarios and commit the result. Expected outcome (about 25 checked expectations), which the committed table must match:

- difficult-terrain: runs to completion; every `cell` expectation checked (setup and each move's `speed`).
- re-hiding-room: runs to completion; every `cell` expectation checked (`room.visible_to` at setup and after each move, override, and clear_override).
- hit-points: setup and steps 0–3 (`hp`, and `damage_taken` at step 2); stops at step 4 `undo`.
- goblin-hit: setup `hit`, step 1 `hit`, step 3 `die1.total` and `hit`; stops at step 4 `invoke`.
- dice-tray: setup `tray.tray_total` and `cup.tray_total`; stops at step 0 `invoke`.
- fireball: setup `fireball.zone`; stops at step 0 `spawn`.
- attack-card, die-with-modifier, drawing-a-card, shuffling: nothing checked (step 0 is `spawn` or `invoke`).

If the computed table differs from this, find out why before committing: a difference is a runner bug, an engine bug, or a disagreement with a fixture, to be reported, not absorbed into the table.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); `invoke`, `spawn`, `undo`, `bind`, the dice script, visibility, log, override-marker, placement, and containment expectations (the full runner is vtt-75c.13 and M5); editing any scenario or the fixture format (the `#SYNTAX` error code is added by vtt-o9i.12).

title: Formula: engine core (iterative resolution, memoization, dependency graph, invalidation, cycles)
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §7 (dependencies, invalidation, determinism, iterative resolution, propagation), §2.3 (#CYCLE, #SYNTAX, origin), §5 (`if` records only the taken branch), §2 (#REF for deleted references), as written by vtt-o9i.12; DESIGN.md §4.2 (reactive cells), §7 (revision-consistent evaluation).

The engine core: memoized, dependency-tracked, iterative evaluation over an `EvalHost` (vtt-o9i.3), without budgets, spatial callbacks, ad hoc evaluation or exception recovery (those are vtt-o9i.16). Exclusive files: packages/formula/src/engine/engine.ts, graph.ts, resolve.ts; one added export line in src/index.ts. Tests test/engine-core-*.test.ts with `MemoryHost` (vtt-o9i.15), using formulas without spatial queries.

- `createEngine(host, options?)`: `engine.value(id, cell)`: object missing → #REF; cell missing → #NAME; literal content → the literal through vtt-o9i.6's `validateRefs` (its existence checks recorded as `exists` dependencies); formula content → memoized result, recomputed if dirty. Sources are parsed once per distinct string; a parse failure (including the parser's depth, node-count and non-finite-literal rules) is #SYNTAX with the parser's message. Each evaluation runs `evaluate` with an `EvalEnv` bound to that cell that records `{cell}` for each `read` (including literal and absent cells) and `{exists}` for each existence check; the graph also stores `{index}` dependencies (recorded by vtt-o9i.16's query methods). The new set replaces the old one.
- Iterative resolution (resolve.ts), no depth limit and no JS recursion across cells: an evaluation attempt that reads an uncomputed formula cell does not recurse. Probe mode: the read returns an internal pending marker and evaluation continues, collecting every uncomputed formula cell the attempt reaches; the attempt's result is discarded; the collected cells are pushed onto an explicit work stack and computed; then the reader is retried. Reads of memoized cells are cheap and charge nothing across attempts (only the final, complete attempt's reads and dependencies count). Every dependency formula is evaluated at most once per revision, and the number of retries of one formula is bounded by the number of distinct uncomputed dependencies it has. Expose `engine.stats()` (`{evaluations, attempts, reads}`) for tests.
- Invalidation. `engine.invalidate(changes)`: for `{cell}` changes, the cell (if a formula) and, transitively through reverse edges, every dependent become dirty; if the cell is one of `position rotation shape z board tag container is_zone name`, every cell with an `{index}` dependency also becomes dirty (transitively). `object_created` and `object_deleted` dirty all `{index}` dependents and all `{exists}` dependents of that object; deletion drops the object's memo entries. Returns the dirty formula `CellKey`s. The caller (vtt-75c.12) calls `invalidate` once per committed revision before any read; the host must report every changed cell, including derived `container` and both parents' `contents` (doc comment). One global index key in v1.
- Cycles. A cell needed while it is already on the work stack (or in progress) closes a cycle: every cell on the stack from it to the top is a member; the read returns #CYCLE (origin that cell). A member's result is forced to #CYCLE (origin itself) whatever it computed (an `iserror` guard inside the cycle does not escape it). Cells outside the cycle that read a member receive the propagated #CYCLE with the member's origin. An edit that breaks the cycle dirties every member and dependent; they recompute.
- `engine.dependenciesOf(id, cell)` returns the last recorded set.

Done when: tests show: `hp = max_hp - damage_taken` 27 → 22 after `set` + `invalidate`, unaffected cells not dirtied; die-with-modifier's chain (`aldric_die.modifier = owner.attack_bonus`, `total = value + modifier`) 16 → 17 after `attack_bonus` changes; `if(flag, a, b)` depends only on the taken branch; a missing cell read gives #NAME and `createObject`/`set` + invalidate fixes the dependent; a ref to a deleted object reads #REF after `deleteObject`; cycles: self-reference, two-cell `a = b + 1, b = a + 1` (both #CYCLE; `c = a` gets propagated #CYCLE with origin in the cycle, whichever cell is read first), an `iserror` guard inside a cycle still #CYCLE, a conditional cycle that appears and disappears with a flag, and recovery after breaking each with `replaceContent`; a 5,000-cell chain resolves without a stack exception; wide dependencies, cold cache: a cell `contents.x` over a container holding 5,000 objects whose `x` are distinct formulas is computed with each `x` evaluated exactly once (`stats().evaluations` = 5,001) and total `reads` linear in 5,000 (a stated constant bound, e.g. ≤ 4 × 5,000); determinism: for the chain, a diamond, and a cycle, results are identical read cold, warm (after reading other cells first), and in reversed read order; a formula with unparseable source, one exceeding the parser depth limit, and one with a 400-digit literal are #SYNTAX; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); budgets, query methods and index-dependency recording, ad hoc `evaluate`, host exception recovery (vtt-o9i.16); applying writes, operations, undo (M2); action reads (vtt-75c.15).

Depends on: vtt-o9i.15, vtt-o9i.14, vtt-o9i.12.

title: Formula: queries and spatial functions
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §3 (`obj`, literal-only `name`), §5 (query order and candidate evaluation order), §6 (spatial and structural functions: literal-geometry candidate set, geometry-read errors, exclusions, point footprints, `distance`), §7 (query dependencies, budget charges), as written by vtt-o9i.12; DESIGN.md §4.3 (anchor-point containment, one board per query).

Fill packages/formula/src/functions/queries.ts (registrations into the default registry only; do not edit library.ts, which vtt-o9i.7 owns). Tests test/queries.test.ts with `FakeEnv` holding geometry cells (literal values, and error values standing in for failed formula geometry) and stubbed `objectsOnBoard` answers.

The host returns candidates over literal geometry (vtt-o9i.3's `objectsOnBoard(board, near)`: objects whose literal index bounds meet `near`, plus every object with formula-valued geometry). This bead computes membership, overlap and distance exactly with the schema geometry (vtt-75c.7: `pointInRegion`, `footprintsOverlap`, `shapeBounds`, `anchorDistance`, epsilon 1e-9; rotation in degrees clockwise about the anchor, y down). Every geometry value (`board`, `position`, `rotation`, `z`, `shape`, `is_zone`) is read through `env.read`, so in the engine each read is a recorded, charged dependency and a formula position yields its evaluated value (or #CYCLE). `rotation` and `z` empty read as 0; `shape` empty is a point footprint.

- Query bounds (`near`), exactly: the query's subject geometry is read first (the zone for `contents`, the object for `zones_containing` and `on`); an error from those reads is the result. Then `contents(zone)`: `shapeBounds` of the zone's region; `zones_containing(obj)`: the degenerate box at `obj`'s anchor; `on(obj)`: `shapeBounds` of `obj`'s footprint (the anchor box if shapeless).
- Candidate evaluation order. Candidates are sorted by id in code point order, then tested one by one in that order: read the candidate's geometry; an error from any geometry read (including #CYCLE) becomes the query's result immediately; a successfully read `position` that is not a list of two finite numbers excludes the candidate (not an error); then the exact test. Successful results are sorted by ascending `z` (`empty` = 0; roll results by total; any other kind → #TYPE), ties by id. Host order never matters. The `contents` cell is not a query and keeps its stored order.
- `contents(zone)`: one argument, a ref (else #TYPE; `empty` → #TYPE); deleted → #REF; `zone.is_zone` must be `true` else #TYPE. A zone not on a board, without a shape, or with an invalid position gives `[]`. Otherwise keep candidates other than the zone whose anchor satisfies `pointInRegion` for the zone's region (boundary inclusive).
- `zones_containing(obj)`: a ref, else #TYPE; deleted #REF; an object not on a board or with an invalid position gives `[]`. Keep candidates with `is_zone` true, other than `obj`, with a shape whose region contains `obj`'s anchor.
- `on(obj)`: a ref, else #TYPE; deleted #REF; not on a board or invalid position gives `[]`. Keep candidates other than `obj` that are not zones, whose `z` is strictly greater than `obj`'s, and whose footprint overlaps `obj`'s: positive-area overlap (touching does not count), except that a point footprint (shapeless object) inside the other footprint counts as overlapping.
- `distance(a, b)`: both refs (else #TYPE; deleted #REF); an error reading either position is the result; `empty` if either is not on a board or has an invalid position; #TYPE if the boards differ; else `anchorDistance`.
- `objects(expr)` (lazy): `env.allObjects()` sorted by id, evaluate `expr` per candidate in that order with `it` = candidate and `itBindsNames`; truthy kept; the first error is the result; results sorted by z then id. Domain: every object, including templates and contained objects; no position exclusion.
- `obj(x)`: `x` text, else #TYPE; if `env.exists(x)` → `ref(x)` (exact id wins); else `env.objectsNamed(x)`: exactly one → that ref (after reading its `name` cell through `env.read`, so the dependency is recorded), otherwise #REF.
- None of these broadcast over a list argument (a list → #TYPE).

Done when: direct query tests over `FakeEnv` (no `where`, `len` or other library functions; composed formulas are tested in vtt-o9i.11) show: `contents(tray)` with the tray of dice-tray.json (rect 4×4 at [10,0]) and candidates `[d2, token, d1, far]` (z: d1 0, d2 0, token 1; `far` outside the rect) returns `[d1, d2, token]`; a candidate exactly on the boundary is included; a rotated zone includes a point only inside after rotation; the fireball.json circle (radius 4 at [10,10]) with candidates `[goblin2, goblin1, rock_outside]` returns `[goblin1, goblin2]`; `contents(not_a_zone)` #TYPE; `contents(empty)` #TYPE; a zone inside a container gives `[]`; a zone whose `position` reads as an error returns that error; `zones_containing(token)` returns the zone while the token is inside and `[]` after its position moves out; `on(this)` returns overlapping objects with higher `z` nearest first, excludes an equal-`z` object, a zone, and a touching-but-not-overlapping object, and includes a shapeless object whose anchor lies inside the footprint; a candidate whose `position` reads as #DIV0 makes `contents` #DIV0 and one whose `position` reads as #CYCLE makes it #CYCLE; a candidate whose `position` reads as a valid non-position value (text, a one-number list) is excluded; permuted host answers containing two failing candidates return the lower id's error every time; a host returning extra non-matching candidates changes no result; `objects(true)` returns an object with an invalid position and a contained object; `distance` 5 for (0,0)-(3,4), `empty` for a contained object and for an invalid position, #TYPE across boards; `obj("Aldric")` by name, `obj("aldric")` by id, zero/two matches #REF, `obj(1)` #TYPE; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); the geometry functions (vtt-75c.7); computing candidates (hosts: vtt-o9i.15, vtt-75c.9); recording dependencies and charging budget (vtt-o9i.16); composed formulas such as difficult terrain's `speed` and the re-hiding room's `visible_to` (vtt-o9i.11); `unit` scaling and grid metrics (FORMULAS §11).

Depends on: vtt-o9i.14, vtt-75c.7, vtt-o9i.12.


Registry contract as implemented by vtt-o9i.14 (program against it; do not change registry.ts): `FunctionDef` is `EagerFunctionDef | LazyFunctionDef`, both `{name, minArgs, maxArgs, kind, broadcast, impl}`. Eager: `impl(args: readonly Result[], ctx: CallContext)`, `CallContext = {scope, env, evaluate(ast, scope?)}`; without `acceptsErrors` no argument is an error, and with `broadcast: "scalar"` no argument is a list (the evaluator recurses into nested lists; list arguments must have equal length else #TYPE, scalars repeat). Lazy: `broadcast: "none"`, `impl(args: readonly Expr[], ctx: LazyContext)`; `LazyContext` adds `target?: Expr` (the `xs` of `xs.where(e)` / `xs.sort(e, desc)`; the method impl evaluates it itself via `ctx.evaluate(ctx.target)`) and `desc: boolean` (true only for `.sort(e, desc)`). Method `args` hold only the method arguments, so `where` and `sort` are registered with arity 1..1. `itemScope(scope, item)` from eval/scope.ts builds the predicate scope (`it` bound, bare names read the item's cells). Register by appending to the exported array in your file (`LIBRARY_FUNCTIONS` in library.ts, `QUERY_FUNCTIONS` in queries.ts); `defaultRegistry` in eval/evaluate.ts already includes both arrays. `where`/`sort` called as plain functions are #NAME by design (`METHOD_NAMES`).

title: Formula: function library, where, sort
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §5 (`where`, `sort`, strict predicate errors), §6 (aggregates and their call shape, numbers, text, errors, dice functions), §2.2 (dice functions), §4 (scalar functions broadcast), as written by vtt-o9i.12.

Fill packages/formula/src/functions/library.ts (registrations only; do not edit queries.ts, which vtt-o9i.8 owns). Tests: test/functions-*.test.ts with `FakeEnv`.

- Aggregates: `sum count len min max avg any all first last`. Exactly one argument (so `max(a, b)` is an arity error, #TYPE: write `max([a, b])`). A list argument is consumed; `empty` is `[]`; any other scalar is a one-item list. `empty` items are ignored by all except `len`. `sum`/`avg`: numbers and roll results (as totals); anything else (including dice, text, booleans) → #TYPE; `sum([])` = 0, `avg([])` = empty. `count` = non-empty items; `len` = all items, and `len(text)` = code point count (`len` is the one aggregate that also takes text). `min`/`max`: all non-empty items must be mutually orderable (numbers/rolls, or all text) else #TYPE; return the winning item unchanged (a roll stays a roll; first occurrence on ties); `[]` → empty. `any`/`all`: truthiness; `any([])` false, `all([])` true. `first`/`last`: first/last non-empty item, else empty. Aggregates never broadcast.
- Numbers (`broadcast: "scalar"`; roll results act as totals and `empty` as 0, as in arithmetic): `round(x, places=0)` half away from zero, `places` an integer (may be negative) else #TYPE; `floor`, `ceil`, `abs`; `clamp(x, lo, hi)` (`lo > hi` → #TYPE); `number(x)`: text parsed after trimming as `-?digits(.digits)?` else #TYPE, number as is, roll → total, empty → empty, others #TYPE. Non-finite results follow vtt-o9i.6 (#TYPE).
- Text (`broadcast: "scalar"` except `join`): `text(x)` = `toText` (vtt-o9i.6); `upper`, `lower` on text (`empty` → `""`, others #TYPE); `join(list, sep)`: items through `toText`, `empty` items skipped, `sep` text.
- Dice: `max_roll`, `min_roll`, `faces`, `sides` (vtt-o9i.5 stats.ts); argument a dice value or a roll result (its `expr`); else #TYPE. `broadcast: "scalar"`.
- `list.where(expr)` (lazy): target `empty` → `[]`; a non-list target → #TYPE. For each item in order, evaluate `expr` with `it` = item and `itBindsNames` (bare names are the item's cells, vtt-o9i.14); keep items whose result is truthy; an error result makes the whole `where` that error (strict: a predicate naming a cell some items lack fails, so filter by `tag` first; treating errors as false would hide typos). `this` is still the enclosing object; a nested `where` rebinds `it` (inner shadows outer).
- `list.sort(expr)` / `.sort(expr, desc)` (lazy): same target and scope rules; keys compared with vtt-o9i.6's ordering (numbers/rolls, or text; mixed → #TYPE); `empty` keys sort last in both directions; stable (ties keep input order, also under `desc`); any key error → that error.

Done when: each bullet has table tests including the §6 empty-list column for every aggregate; `sum(contents.where(tag has "die").value)` over a `FakeEnv` cup holding two dice with roll values 4 and 6 and a non-die = 10, and = 0 for an empty cup; `any(xs.where(tag has "d20").total >= 13)` true/false cases; `all(rows.save_roll != empty)` false with one empty, true with both set; `len(zones.where(tag has "difficult")) > 0`; `floor(r / 2)` with a roll of total 28 = 14 (a number); `max([r1, r2])` returns the roll value; `max(1, 2)` #TYPE; `round(2.5)` = 3, `round(-2.5)` = -3, `round(1234, -2)` = 1200; `number("3") + 1` = 4, `number("3x")` #TYPE; `upper(["a","b"])` broadcasts; `join(["a", empty, "b"], ",")` = `"a,b"`; `max_roll(4d6dl1)` = 18, `sides(2d6 + 1d8)` = `[6,6,8]`, `faces(4d6dl1)` = 4, `max_roll(r)` uses the roll's expr; `where` with `this.x` vs bare `x`, nested `where` shadowing, non-ref items with bare names #TYPE, `[3,1,2].where(it > 1)`, a predicate error making the whole result that error; `sort` stable, `desc`, empties last, mixed keys #TYPE. `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); `contents()`, `zones_containing()`, `on()`, `distance()`, `objects()`, `obj()` and query ordering (vtt-o9i.8); dependency recording and budget (vtt-o9i.9, vtt-o9i.16).

title: Formula: value semantics (coercion, operators, equality, broadcasting)
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2 (dangling refs), §2.1 (empty, truthiness, coercion), §2.2 (roll results in arithmetic and comparison; dice arithmetic; roll result fields), §2.3 (error propagation and first-error rule), §4 (all operators, equality, ordering, broadcasting), as written by vtt-o9i.12; DESIGN.md §4.4 (viewer sets, `toViewers`).

The value semantics of the language, as pure functions over values: no AST, no environment, no scope. vtt-o9i.14 builds AST evaluation on top. Exclusive files: packages/formula/src/eval/values.ts, operators.ts, errors.ts, refs.ts. Tests: test/values-*.test.ts, all pure (no `FakeEnv`). Add this bead's `export * from` lines (values, operators, errors, refs, `toViewers`) to packages/formula/src/index.ts; Biome requires the lines sorted, so place yours in order; never edit other beads' lines.

- errors.ts: `firstError(...results)` (first error in argument order), `withOrigin(error, origin)` (sets origin only on a new error), the rule that any operator given an error operand returns that error unchanged (origin kept), and `collectList(items)`: a list built from items yields the first error in list order if any item is an error (lists never contain errors).
- values.ts: `truthy(v)` (`false`, `empty`, `0`, `""`, `[]` are false; everything else, including any ref, any roll result even of total 0, dice, viewers, ink, shape, is true); `toNumber` coercion for arithmetic (number; `empty` as 0; roll result as its total; anything else #TYPE); `toText(v)` (text as is, `empty` → `""`, number → JS `String(n)` with `-0` → `"0"`, boolean → `"true"`/`"false"`, dice → normalized notation, roll → its total as text; ref, viewers, ink, shape → #TYPE); `equals(a, b)`; `compare(a, b)` (code point order for text); `toViewers(v)`, the conversion the visibility code (vtt-75c.10) applies to every evaluated `visible_to` value (FORMULAS §2, decision written by vtt-o9i.12): a viewers value → itself; a ref → a one-entry set holding that ref (whether it names a character is the consumer's check); a list whose items are refs, viewers values, or nested such lists → the union of their entries, flattened, duplicates removed; `empty`, an empty list, an error, or any other kind → #TYPE (the consumer admits nobody). The evaluator never calls it.
- operators.ts: `binary(op, a, b)` and `unary(op, a)`, including broadcasting:
  - Arithmetic `+ - * / %`, unary `-`: operands through `toNumber`. Dice: `dice ± dice`, `dice ± number`, `number + dice`, `number - dice`, `-dice` give dice (vtt-o9i.5 `addDice`/`negateDice`; non-integer number → #TYPE); `empty` with dice acts as 0; a roll with dice acts as its total; `*`, `/`, `%` on dice → #TYPE. IEEE doubles; `/` and `%` by 0 → #DIV0; `%` takes the sign of the dividend; any other non-finite result → #TYPE. `"3" + 1` is #TYPE.
  - `&`: both operands through `toText`.
  - Equality `=`/`!=`: never #TYPE except ink: different kinds unequal, except number vs roll (total); numbers by value (`0 = -0`); text exact; booleans; `empty = empty` true, `empty = 0` and `empty = ""` false; refs by id; dice by normalized expr; roll vs roll by total; viewers as sets (order and duplicates ignored, refs by id); ink vs anything but `empty` → #TYPE; shapes structurally. Two lists → ordered recursive whole-list equality (a boolean). Exactly one list → broadcast.
  - Ordering `< <= > >=`: number/roll pairs (by total) and text pairs (code point order); `empty` acts as 0 against a number/roll and as `""` against text; `empty` vs `empty` equal; anything else (booleans, mixed number/text, refs, dice, shapes, …) → #TYPE; two lists → #TYPE; a node flagged `chained` → #TYPE (the AST bead passes the flag).
  - `has`: left a list → true iff some item `equals` the right (no broadcasting); left `empty` → false; any other left → #TYPE.
  - Broadcasting: for arithmetic, unary `-`, `&`, ordering, and equality with exactly one list: list ⊕ scalar and scalar ⊕ list elementwise; list ⊕ list of equal length elementwise for arithmetic and `&` (unequal → #TYPE); nested lists recursively; `[] ⊕ x` is `[]`. `has` and two-list `=`/`!=` never broadcast.
- refs.ts: `validateRefs(value, exists): Result`: if `value` is a ref, or contains a ref inside a list (at any depth) or a viewers value, whose object does not exist (`exists(id)` false), returns #REF; else the value unchanged. This is the single shared helper: vtt-o9i.14 wires it into `FakeEnv.read`, and the engine (vtt-o9i.9) calls it on every cell read, recording the existence checks as dependencies.

title: Formula: dice notation, normalization, arithmetic, statistics
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2.2 (dice values, modifiers, arithmetic, dice functions; the dice dialect and normalization as written by vtt-o9i.12), §4 (dice equality by normalized expression); docs/FIXTURES.md §5 (script entries match by normalized expression).

The pure, non-random half of dice: grammar, canonical form, arithmetic, and static functions. The evaluator depends only on this half; rolling is vtt-o9i.13. Files: packages/formula/src/dice/notation.ts, arith.ts, stats.ts, index.ts (this bead's exports; vtt-o9i.13 adds its own export lines without reordering). Tests: test/dice-notation.test.ts, test/dice-arith.test.ts, test/dice-stats.test.ts. Add `export * from "./dice/index"` to packages/formula/src/index.ts (Biome requires the lines sorted, so place yours in order; never edit other beads' lines; vtt-o9i.14 preserves them). Fixture access: the test that parses every dice-script `expr` reads packages/fixtures/scenarios/*.json directly with `node:fs` (path relative to the test file) and does not import @vtt/fixtures.

notation.ts: `parseDice(expr): DiceExpr | DiceError` over `DiceExpr = {terms: DiceTerm[], constant: number}`, `DiceTerm = {sign: 1|-1, count, faces: number | "F", reroll?: {op:"<"|">"|"=", n}, explode: boolean, keep?: {mode:"kh"|"kl"|"dh"|"dl", n}}`. Grammar:

```
expr     := ws? ["-"] item (ws? ("+"|"-") ws? item)* ws?
item     := pool | integer
pool     := [count] "d" (sides | "F") modifier*
modifier := ("kh"|"kl"|"dh"|"dl") integer | "!" | "r" ("<"|">"|"=") integer
```

Lowercase `d`, uppercase `F` only. Validation (each failure a `DiceError` with a message; the evaluator turns it into #TYPE): count 1–1000; sides 2–1,000,000; at least one pool; at most one modifier of each kind (keep/drop counts as one kind), any input order; `khN`/`klN` need 1 ≤ N ≤ count; `dhN`/`dlN` need 1 ≤ N < count; `!` and `r` not allowed on `dF`; reroll `n` within 1..sides. Integers are summed into `constant`.

`normalizeDice(expr): string`: terms in source order (never reordered); count always explicit (`d20` → `1d20`, `dF` → `1dF`); modifiers in the order reroll, explode, keep/drop (`1d6kh1!` → `1d6!kh1`); no semantic simplification (`1d20kh1` stays); constants folded into one trailing signed integer, omitted if 0 (`2+1d6+1` → `1d6+3`); no spaces; first term carries `-` only if negative. `diceEquals(a, b)` compares normalized strings. `renderDice(DiceExpr)` is the inverse of `parseDice` on canonical input.

arith.ts: `addDice(a, b)` where `b` is a `DiceExpr` (terms concatenated, constants summed) or an integer (non-integer → error); `negateDice(a)` (every term's sign and the constant flipped). `number + dice` equals `dice + number` after normalization.

stats.ts: `maxRoll`, `minRoll`, `faces`, `sides`. Max/min ignore explosion and rerolls and respect keep/drop: a positive pool contributes `kept × S` (max) / `kept × 1` (min) where `kept` = count, or N for kh/kl, or count − N for dh/dl; `dF` contributes `+kept` / `−kept`; a negative pool contributes the negated opposite bound; plus the constant (`maxRoll("4d6dl1") = 18`, `minRoll("1d20-1d4") = -3`). `faces` = sum of counts over all pools. `sides` = each pool's sides repeated `count` times, in term order; `dF` counts as 3.

Done when: each §2.2 example parses and normalizes (`2d6+3`, `1d20kh1`, `4d6dl1`, `1d6!`, `2d20kl1`, `dF`, `d20`, `1d20r<2`, `1d8+3`, `8d6`); the normalization cases above hold; `diceEquals("1d8+3", "1d8 + 3")` and `diceEquals("d20", "1d20")` true, `diceEquals("1d6+1d20", "1d20+1d6")` false; every validation failure above is rejected with a message; `addDice("1d8", "1d6")` + 2 → `1d8+1d6+2`; `negateDice("1d6+2")` → `-1d6-2`; the stats examples above; every `expr` in every fixture scenario's dice script parses; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); rolling and roll validation (vtt-o9i.13); the formula lexer (vtt-o9i.4); dice under formula operators (vtt-o9i.6); the dice script runner (vtt-75c.15, M5); compound explosions and success counting (FORMULAS §11).

Depends on: vtt-o9i.2, vtt-o9i.12.

title: Formula: lexer and Pratt parser
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2 (literal syntax, including record literals), §2.3 (#SYNTAX and the parser limits), §2.2 (dice literal syntax, as tokens), §3 (names, `this`, `it`, dot-access, backtick names), §4 (operators, precedence, non-chaining comparisons), §5 (`if`, `.where`, `.sort`, `desc`), §6 (call syntax).

Hand-written lexer and Pratt parser producing an AST. No evaluation, no schema dependency.

Files: packages/formula/src/syntax/tokens.ts, lexer.ts, ast.ts, parser.ts; tests test/lexer.test.ts, test/parser.test.ts.

Lexical rules (state them in lexer.ts comments):

- Whitespace (space, tab, newline) separates tokens and is otherwise ignored. No comments.
- Numbers: `digits` or `digits.digits`. No exponent, no leading `.`, no trailing `.`. A number immediately followed by an identifier character is a syntax error (`2x`). A numeric literal that converts to a non-finite number (e.g. a 400-digit literal) is a parse failure, which the engine reports as #SYNTAX.
- Text: double-quoted; escapes `\"` and `\\` only; any other backslash sequence is an error; literal newlines allowed; unterminated is an error.
- Identifiers: `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, case-sensitive. Backtick names `` `...` `` (no backtick inside, non-empty) are always names, never keywords or dice.
- Keywords: `true false empty this it all gm and or not has`. `all` and `gm` are reserved: bare, they are viewer literals; `all(` is the aggregate call. `desc` is not a keyword (it is a likely cell name): it is recognised only as the bare second argument of `.sort`. `owner` is an ordinary name (the cell), never the symbolic `"owner"` viewer entry, which exists only in stored literals.
- Dice literals: at a digit or `d`, try `[0-9]*d([0-9]+|F)` followed by modifiers `(kh|kl|dh|dl)[0-9]+`, `!`, `r(<|>|=)[0-9]+`, in any order. It is a dice token only if the character after the match is not `[A-Za-z0-9_]`; otherwise fall back (`d6x` is an identifier, `2d6kh` is a syntax error). A `!` immediately followed by `=` is never consumed as explode (`1d6!=3` is `1d6 != 3`). The token carries the raw text; vtt-o9i.5 validates it. Consequently a cell named `d6` or `dF` must be backticked.
- Punctuation: `+ - * / % & = != < <= > >= ( ) [ ] { } , . :` and `->` (lexed for M5's step syntax; the expression parser rejects it).

Grammar and precedence, loosest to tightest: `or`; `and`; comparisons `= != < <= > >=`; `has`; `&`; `+ -`; `* / %`; prefix `-` and `not`; postfix (call `f(...)`, dot `.name`, method `.where(...)`/`.sort(...)`). All binary operators are left-associative. Comparisons are parsed left-associatively but a comparison node whose unparenthesized left or right operand is itself a comparison is flagged `chained: true`; the evaluator returns #TYPE for it (§4). `(a = b) = c` is not chained.

AST node kinds (ast.ts, each with `start`/`end` offsets): `Number`, `Text`, `Boolean`, `Empty`, `Dice {raw}`, `Viewer {which: "all"|"gm"}`, `This`, `It`, `Name {name}`, `List {items}`, `Record {fields: [name, expr][]}` (duplicate field names are a syntax error), `Unary {op}`, `Binary {op, chained?}`, `Dot {target, name}`, `Call {name, args}`, `Method {target, name: "where"|"sort", args, desc: boolean}`. A call is an identifier (not a backtick name) followed by `(`, whitespace allowed. `.name(` where `name` is not `where`/`sort` is a syntax error. `.sort(e, desc)` sets `desc: true`; any other second argument, or more than two arguments, is a syntax error. `.where` takes exactly one argument. Functions are not resolved here (unknown names are #NAME at evaluation, §2.3) and arity is not checked here.

Entry points: `parse(source): ParseResult` (whole input must be one expression; failure is `{ok:false, message, offset}` with no partial AST), and `parseExpressionPrefix(source, start): {ok, ast, end} | failure`, which stops at the first token that cannot continue the expression (for M5's step parser). A parse failure becomes the error value #SYNTAX in the engine (vtt-o9i.9); the parser itself only returns the failure.

Limits (FORMULAS §2.3 as written by vtt-o9i.12): the AST depth is at most 256, counting every nesting level, including each level of a left-associative binary chain (`1+1+…`), each postfix dot, call or method (`a.b.c…`), parentheses, lists, records, and unary chains; and the AST has at most 10,000 nodes. Exceeding either is a parse failure whose message names the limit. Both limits apply to `parseExpressionPrefix` too. The parser tracks depth while parsing, so it reports the failure without overflowing the JS stack. These limits are what bound the evaluator's recursion over the AST.

Done when: every formula source and every `when` source in every scenario under packages/fixtures/scenarios/ parses (the test discovers them); each §10 formula in FORMULAS.md parses to the expected tree (snapshot of a compact s-expression printer `printAst` written in this bead), including `any(on(this).where(tag has "d20").total >= ac)` (method on call, dot on method, `>=` loosest inside the call) and `roll != empty and total >= target.ac`; precedence cases: `not a = b` is `(= (not a) b)`, `-x.y` is `(neg (. x y))`, `a & b has c` is `(has (& a b) c)`, `1 + 2 * 3`, `a or b and c`; `a < b < c` parses with `chained: true`; dice tokens `2d6`, `d20`, `dF`, `1d20kh1`, `4d6dl1`, `1d6!`, `2d20kl1`, `1d20r<2`, `` `d6` `` (a name), `d6x` (a name), `1d6!=3` (dice, `!=`, number); `2d6+3` is `(+ (dice 2d6) 3)`; record `{target: it, owner: it.owner}`; `x.sort(y, desc)` sets desc and a cell named `desc` parses as a name elsewhere; syntax errors with offsets for `2x`, `"a\q"`, `"abc`, `(1`, `a.b(1)`, `[1,]`, `x.sort(y, up)`, `{a: 1, a: 2}`; limits: 256 nested parentheses parse and 257 fail; a `1+1+…` chain 256 levels deep parses and one 257 levels deep fails with the depth message; a 300-level `a.b.c…` chain fails; a flat list literal with more than 10,000 nodes fails with the node-count message; a 100,000-term `1+1+…` source returns a failure, never a stack exception. `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (the lexical decisions and limits are written by vtt-o9i.12; this bead edits no docs); evaluation; dice semantics beyond tokenizing (vtt-o9i.5); action step syntax (`->`, step names, cell paths, destinations: M5); mapping parse failures to #SYNTAX (vtt-o9i.9).

Depends on: none. Every lexical rule and limit is stated above, so this bead does not wait for vtt-o9i.12.
notes: Codex review: no findings. AST notes for vtt-o9i.6/.14: no Paren node (offsets widened); chained:true only when set; -2 is Unary over Number; Method.args is exactly one expr with desc as a boolean; Call.name may be 'all'; if() arrives as a plain Call and must be special-cased; Record.fields ordered pairs; Dice.raw unvalidated; non-finite numeric literal is a lex failure. Depth: leaf 0, each nesting level +1, parentheses add a level.

title: Formula: evaluation host interface, FakeEnv, fixture conversion
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §3 (literal-only `name`), §3.1 (structural cells and defaults), §6 (spatial candidate set), §7 (query dependencies, budget, viewer-independence), as written by vtt-o9i.12 and vtt-75c.2; DESIGN.md §4.3; docs/FIXTURES.md §2, §3.

The boundary between the pure language and the document, plus the stateless test doubles. The mutable test document is vtt-o9i.15. M2's engine adapter (vtt-75c.12) implements `EvalHost` over the document store.

packages/formula/src/host.ts (types plus doc comments that are the contract):

- `EvalHost`, a view of one revision of the raw document; it never evaluates formulas:
  - `exists(id): boolean`: object (or board) exists at this revision.
  - `cell(id, name): CellContent | undefined`: stored content; an override is returned as its literal; unstored structural cells read as their default (table below); `undefined` = no such cell.
  - `objectsNamed(name): ObjectId[]`: exact match over literal `name`s (`name` is literal-only).
  - `allObjects(): ObjectId[]`: every object in the document.
  - `objectsOnBoard(board, near: Bounds): ObjectId[]`: the candidate set, defined over literal geometry (FORMULAS §6): every object placed directly on `board` (never inside a container) whose literal `indexBounds` (vtt-75c.7: union of footprint bounds and anchor, expanded by epsilon) intersect `near` (inclusive), plus every object on `board` with any formula-valued geometry cell (`position`, `rotation`, `z`, `shape`; a cell with an override counts as literal) regardless of bounds. Each id once, any order. An object whose literal position is not two finite numbers is not a candidate by bounds (the evaluator would exclude it).
  Contract: the host never filters by visibility; result ordering and exact tests are the evaluator's (vtt-o9i.8).
- `EvalEnv`, what the evaluator sees (implemented by the engine, by M2's action context vtt-75c.15, by `FakeEnv`): `read(id, cell): Result | undefined`, `exists`, `objectsNamed`, `allObjects`, `objectsOnBoard(board, near)`.
- `Change = {type:"cell", object, cell} | {type:"object_created", object} | {type:"object_deleted", object}`; `CellKey` (object id + cell name with an unambiguous separator); `Dependency = {type:"cell", object, cell} | {type:"exists", object} | {type:"index"}`.

Structural cell value shapes and defaults (canonical: `STRUCTURAL_CELLS` in @vtt/schema, vtt-75c.3; stated here so M1 and M2 agree; FORMULAS §3.1 as written by vtt-75c.2):

| Cell | Reads as | Default when not stored |
|---|---|---|
| id | text | (always present) |
| name | text, literal only | empty |
| tag | list of text, literal only | [] |
| visible_to | viewers | viewers ["all"] |
| owner, template | ref or empty | empty |
| contents | list of refs, stored order | [] |
| container | ref or empty (derived) | empty |
| board | ref or empty | empty (in a container) |
| position | list of two numbers, or a formula | empty (in a container) |
| rotation | number (degrees clockwise about the anchor, y down) | empty (read as 0) |
| z | number | empty (read as 0) |
| face_up | boolean | true |
| opaque | boolean | false |
| is_zone | boolean | false |
| shape | ShapeValue | empty (no shape) |

`is_template` and `is_character` are object fields, not readable cells.

packages/formula/test/support/:

- fake-env.ts: `FakeEnv` implements `EvalEnv` from a plain map `{[id]: {[cell]: Result}}` plus optional stubbed answers for `objectsOnBoard` (map board → ids), `objectsNamed`, `allObjects`. No formulas. Its `read` returns map values as given; dangling-ref validation is added by vtt-o9i.14 through vtt-o9i.6's shared helper.
- fixture-values.ts: `fromFixtureValue(v): Value` and `fromFixtureContent(c): CellContent`: a checked cast through `isValue`.
- scenarios.ts: `loadScenarios()`: every scenario in packages/fixtures/scenarios/, discovered via `import.meta.resolve("@vtt/fixtures")` → `../scenarios`, parsed with the fixtures loader.

Package setup: add `"@vtt/fixtures": "workspace:*"` to @vtt/formula devDependencies and `"@vtt/schema": "workspace:*"` to its dependencies (lockfile rides along). Add this bead's `export * from` lines (host types) to packages/formula/src/index.ts; Biome requires the lines sorted, so place yours in order; never edit other beads' lines.

Done when: test/host-types.test.ts: type-level tests (`expectTypeOf`) for `EvalHost`, `EvalEnv`, `Change`, `Dependency`; `FakeEnv` returns mapped values, `undefined` for missing cells, and stubbed query answers; test/fixture-values.test.ts: every literal value anywhere in every scenario (setup cells, step values, expectation values, dice script entries) passes `isValue` through `fromFixtureValue`, and a deliberately malformed value throws; `loadScenarios()` returns all ten scenarios; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); the mutable test document (vtt-o9i.15); exact spatial tests (vtt-o9i.8) and geometry (vtt-75c.7); the engine (vtt-o9i.9); any evaluation; visibility.

Depends on: vtt-o9i.2, vtt-o9i.12, vtt-75c.2.

title: Schema: cell value types
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2 (value table, including the shape value), §2.2 (roll result parts), §2.3 (error codes, including #SYNTAX), as written by vtt-o9i.12; DESIGN.md §4.4 (viewer sets); docs/FIXTURES.md §2 (encodings).

Create the value types every other package shares. Small and first: M2's schema bead (vtt-75c.3) and M1's host, dice, and value-semantics beads depend on it. The value types are the FIXTURES §2 tagged JSON encoding plus the shape value and the error value (FORMULAS §2, §2.3).

Files in packages/schema/src/:

- ids.ts: `ObjectId = string`; `ID_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/` (the fixtures `NameSchema` pattern); `isIdSyntax(s)`. vtt-75c.3 later adds reserved ids and board ids to this file and imports `ID_PATTERN` from here.
- values.ts: one exported type per kind, tagged on `type`, field names and JSON shapes identical to packages/fixtures/src/types.ts: `NumberValue {value}`, `TextValue {value}`, `BooleanValue {value}`, `EmptyValue`, `ListValue {items: Value[]}`, `RefValue {object: ObjectId}`, `DiceValue {expr}`, `RollValue {expr, dice: number[], dropped: number[], total}`, `ViewersValue {viewers: ViewerEntry[]}` with `ViewerEntry = "all" | "gm" | "owner" | RefValue`, `InkValue {strokes: Point[][]}`, `ShapeValue {type:"shape", shape: Shape}`. `Value` is their union. `ErrorCode` string union and `ERROR_CODES` array: `#CYCLE #NAME #TYPE #REF #DIV0 #LIMIT #SYNTAX`. `ErrorValue {type:"error", code, message?: string, origin?: {object, cell}}`. `Result = Value | ErrorValue`. Constructors `num`, `text`, `bool`, `EMPTY`, `list`, `ref`, `dice`, `shape`, `err(code, message?, origin?)`, and `isError(r)`.
- shape.ts: `Point = [number, number]`; `Shape = {type:"rect", width, height} | {type:"circle", radius} | {type:"polygon", points: Point[]}`; `Bounds = {minX, minY, maxX, maxY}` (axis-aligned box in board units; used by the host interface vtt-o9i.3 and returned by the schema geometry vtt-75c.7).
- cell.ts: `FormulaContent {type:"formula", source}`; `CellContent = Value | FormulaContent`.
- guard.ts: `isValue(x: unknown): x is Value` and `isCellContent`, hand-written, no dependencies. Contract, field by field (every object strict: an unknown key fails; `type` must be a known tag):
  - number: `value` a finite number (NaN and ±Infinity rejected).
  - text: `value` a string (may be empty).
  - boolean: `value` a boolean. empty: no other fields.
  - list: `items` an array of values (recursive; may be empty); an error item fails.
  - ref: `object` a string matching `ID_PATTERN`.
  - dice: `expr` a string that is not blank after trimming (its grammar is not checked here).
  - roll: `expr` non-blank; `dice` and `dropped` arrays of integers; `total` a finite number.
  - viewers: `viewers` a non-empty array of `"all"`, `"gm"`, `"owner"`, or ref values.
  - ink: `strokes` a non-empty array of non-empty arrays of points; a point is a two-element array of finite numbers.
  - shape: rect with finite `width`, `height`; circle with finite `radius`; polygon with an array of points (positivity and simplicity are document invariants checked by vtt-75c.3).
  - `type:"error"` is rejected (errors are not storable).
  - `isCellContent`: a value, or `{type:"formula", source}` with `source` non-blank after trimming.
- index.ts: one `export * from "./<module>.ts"` line per module. Rule for every bead that touches this package index: add only your own export lines, never reorder or edit others'.

The schema package must not import @vtt/fixtures (not even as a dev dependency). Conformance against real fixture values is tested in vtt-o9i.3. Zod schemas are not part of this bead; vtt-75c.3 adds zod wrappers that delegate to `isValue`.

Done when: test/values.test.ts round-trips one example of every kind (including shape) through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))` and `isValue`; negative tests, one each: NaN and Infinity in a number, a roll total, a die result (and a non-integer die), an ink point, a shape dimension; a ref whose id breaks `ID_PATTERN` (`"1abc"`, `"a-b"`, `""`); blank dice `expr` and blank roll `expr`; a viewers value with no entries and with an unknown entry; ink with no strokes and with an empty stroke; a formula with blank source (via `isCellContent`); an error value; a list containing an error; an unknown `type`; an extra key; a type-level test (`expectTypeOf`) shows `Result` = `Value | ErrorValue`; `ERROR_CODES` has exactly the seven codes; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (written by vtt-o9i.12); document, object, operation and protocol types (vtt-75c.3, vtt-75c.4); zod (vtt-75c.3); geometry (vtt-75c.7); dice grammar (vtt-o9i.5); equality and coercion (vtt-o9i.6); the fixtures `ErrorCodeSchema` (vtt-o9i.10).

Depends on: vtt-o9i.12.

title: Transcribe fixture: Fireball
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §10 fixture A Fireball card with a circle zone; DESIGN.md §4.1 (containment, templates), §4.3 (zones).

One scenario under packages/fixtures/scenarios/, in the format owned by the fixture scenario format bead. The format may not be changed by this bead; a gap blocks this bead and is reported against the format bead. Cover: template card owning its zone; spawn into a binder binding the new card and its new zone, asserting the card's zone reference was remapped to the new zone; dragging the zone onto the board removes it from the card's contents; creatures placed inside and outside the circle; Lock targets spawning one save_row per creature inside with target and owner set; scripted saves with one pass and one fail; Apply all adding damage_dealt per row; the Apply all log group (addressed by index) holds the resolved writes; a later change to a target dex_save drifts the live damage_dealt while that earlier log group is asserted unchanged; save rows are addressed through bind steps since they are created inside an action; Discard removing zone, card, and rows recursively.

title: Fixture scenario format
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §10 (notation and intent), §2 (values), §3.1 (structural cells), §8 (actions, whole section), DESIGN.md §4.1 (objects, containment), §4.4 (visibility), §7 (operations, undo).

Design the machine-readable form of the §10 fixtures in packages/fixtures. Deliver TypeScript types, a zod validator, docs/FIXTURES.md, and tests. This bead owns the format; transcription beads may not change it. A scenario must be able to express everything below.

Table setup. Objects with unique id, tags, cells, and ordered `contents` (owning, acyclic). `container` is derived from contents, never written. An object is either in a container or placed on a board (board id, position, and shape for zones and tokens), never both. Non-owning references are a tagged value. Templates are objects marked as templates; instances are made from them by a spawn step. Per-cell visibility as in DESIGN §4.4.

Cell values. Every §2 storable value has an unambiguous tagged encoding: number, text, boolean, empty, reference, dice expression, roll result (with its parts), viewer set, ink. Formula source is a separate tagged form from literal text. Errors are expectations, never setup values.

Dice script. An ordered list of roll results consumed in order during execution. Exhaustion is a scenario error. The script is execution input only; it is not a replay mechanism (DESIGN §7 replays recorded effects). Shuffle takes an explicit permutation from the script.

Actions on an object: name, optional `when` source, ordered steps as source text. Steps performed by an actor (GM or a named viewer): set literal, override a formula cell, clear override, invoke action, move object to board position, move object into a container at an index, spawn template into a container or onto a board with initial cells and a symbolic binding for the new object (and for objects it owns), undo last action group.

Expectations after any step: cell value, cell error code, cell has override marker, action enabled or disabled, action invocation rejected with a reason and no state change, object exists or has been removed (recursively), object container and index, object board placement, ordered contents of an object, cell visible or hidden to a named viewer, object visible or hidden to a named viewer, number of log groups, and that the latest log group's resolved effects include a given cell write or roll.

Deliverables: src/types.ts, src/schema.ts (zod), src/index.ts exporting them plus loadScenario(path), test/format.test.ts with malformed examples the validator rejects, test/samples/ with two test-only sample scenarios (hit points, die with modifier) that the cells transcription bead later replaces with production scenarios under scenarios/. A test/scenarios.test.ts that discovers every file under scenarios/ and validates it; it passes trivially now. docs/FIXTURES.md with the format walkthrough and one stub section per §10 fixture, each with a link slot the transcription beads fill in.

Done when: docs/FIXTURES.md walks through every §10 fixture and shows how the format expresses each behaviour the prose calls out, with no unexpressible construct remaining; validator and sample tests pass; pnpm typecheck, lint, format:check pass.

Out of scope: transcribing the remaining fixtures; any evaluator, parser, or runner; replay expectations (M2 extends the format additively); face layout and show-when (M5 extends the format additively); depending on the schema package.

title: Workflow scripts: worktree, bead review, plan review
description:
Implements: CLAUDE.md Loop per implementation bead and Tracking: beads.

Add scripts/ (bash, no build step) that encode the loop:
- scripts/worktree.sh <bead-id> <slug>: creates branch <bead-id>/<slug> from main in ../vtt-worktrees/<bead-id>, runs pnpm install --frozen-lockfile there, and verifies bd works from inside the worktree with bd show <bead-id> (bd 1.3.4 already finds the main repo's .beads from a worktree; the script only needs to check, and fail loudly if it does not).
- scripts/review-bead.sh <bead-id> [base=main]: builds a review prompt from bd show <bead-id> plus a reminder that findings are advisory and must each be tagged IN-SCOPE or OUT-OF-SCOPE and that the review must state whether every Done-when condition is met, appends git diff <base>...HEAD excluding pnpm-lock.yaml in a fenced block, and runs `codex exec --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check -o <outfile> -` with that prompt on stdin from the current worktree. Do NOT use `codex review`: it rejects a custom prompt together with --base. Prints the review to stdout and saves it under .reviews/<bead-id>-<timestamp>.md (already gitignored).
- scripts/review-plan.sh <epic-id>: dumps the epic and each child via bd show, with a prompt asking for missing dependencies, overlapping scope, oversized beads, gaps against named doc sections, and bad decisions, each finding with bead id, severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), problem, and proposed change, ending with an overall verdict. Runs codex exec as above. Saves output like above.
Each script has a usage line, uses set -euo pipefail, and fails loudly on missing tools (bd, codex, pnpm, git). Scripts touch only scripts/ and a Workflow section appended to README.md.

Done when: each script runs end to end against a throwaway bead (create one with bd create, delete it with bd delete afterwards) in a throwaway worktree that is removed afterwards; pnpm lint and format:check pass; the README documents the three commands.

title: Workspace root: pnpm, TypeScript, Vitest, Biome
description:

Create the monorepo root with no packages yet, and settle the conventions every package bead follows.

- tsconfig.base.json: strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, isolatedModules, module ESNext, moduleResolution Bundler, target ES2023, noEmit. No composite, no project references. Each package will have tsconfig.json extending it and a typecheck script running tsc --noEmit. Libraries are consumed as TypeScript source: each package's exports map "." to ./src/index.ts, and Vite, Vitest, and tsx resolve that directly. No build step for libraries in v1.
- No root vitest.config.ts yet: Vitest errors when a projects glob matches nothing, so the library skeletons bead adds the root config with projects: ["packages/*"] when the first packages exist. Until then the root test script is `vitest run --passWithNoTests`; the skeletons bead drops the flag. Each package will own a vitest.config.ts.
- Biome as the single linter and formatter: biome.json at root with recommended rules, noUnusedVariables as an error, organize imports, 2-space indent, double quotes, line width 100. Markdown formatting off (the design docs are not reformatted); tool-managed folders (.beads, .agents, .claude, .codex, .cursor) excluded; ignoreUnknown on.
- .nvmrc / .node-version at the installed major (Node 26). .editorconfig. README.md with two lines pointing at docs/ and CLAUDE.md. Extend .gitignore with .reviews/.
- Add a Conventions subsection to CLAUDE.md: run pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm format:check, pnpm test before asking for review; libraries are source-consumed; one vitest.config.ts per package.

Done when: fresh clone, pnpm install, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm format:check, pnpm test all exit 0 with zero packages present; introducing an unused variable in a scratch .ts file makes pnpm lint fail.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text:
How M5 reads its Done-when (M5 plan Q16): "every §10 fixture passes end to end in the UI" is carried by vtt-1xv.24 (P2). The ten FORMULAS §10 scenarios run against a real in-process authority (scripted dice), with the real React app in jsdom and a recording renderer.
- Every invoke step by the GM, or by a character whose view shows the object, is a click on the button drawn on the object's face, using view-as for character actors.
- Every action expectation is read from the drawn button's enabled state, and face_element from the drawn face.
- GM set/override go through the face editor or the inspector, clear_override through the formula bar, board moves through canvas drags, and undo through the log panel.
- Fixture objects have no layouts, so they are reached through the default face: the button strip, and the contents list whose non-template entries are expanded (UI-local state).
- Steps with no UI gesture use the same session's protocol client and are listed in the report: spawn (initial cells or owned bindings), bind, container moves with an index, non-invoke steps by a character, and invokes by a character who cannot see the object.
The same scenarios also complete in the direct runner (vtt-1xv.10) and over the protocol (vtt-1xv.13). There is no browser automation (M4 decision Q16); a manual checklist for §8.4 steps 9–12 is posted when vtt-1xv.24 closes.

(2) vtt-serve creates new tables stocked with a GM binder of example templates (`--empty` opts out; vtt-1xv.22), so step 1 is literal. (4) Step 5's agent can press buttons through the new MCP `invoke` tool (vtt-1xv.13).
(5) Step 14's "scroll the log back" is the log panel's Load older (vtt-1xv.20). The panel can also undo any group by index, including the agent's; Ctrl+Z stays `mine`.
(6) Step 9's "double-click each to roll" relies on the d20 template's `default_action` Roll; step 10's "drop a goblin onto target" is a drop onto the card's target editor element.
