- `keybindings.ts` exports `KEY_BINDINGS: readonly {keys: string; label: string}[]`, the table its handler dispatches from (refactored so dispatch and help read the one table if it does not already); `?` (Shift+/) toggles help and is added to the table; no binding fires while focus is in a text field.
- `help-content.ts` exports `HELP_GESTURES: readonly {gesture: string; effect: string}[]`, verbatim, in this order: "Space-drag or middle-drag" — "pan"; "Wheel" — "zoom (over a list that scrolls: scroll it)"; "Click" — "select"; "Alt+click" — "cycle through the objects under the pointer"; "Drag one template" — "drop a copy"; "Alt held at drag start" — "move the template instead of copying it"; "Alt held at drop onto an object" — "put the dragged objects inside it"; "Drop on a card's editor field" — "set that cell to the dropped object"; "Drop on a list" — "insert there"; "Drop a template on a binder" — "give that binder a template"; "Double-click" — "run the object's default action, else edit in place"; "Click an editor field" — "edit it"; "Chevron on a list entry" — "expand or collapse it (a template entry makes a working copy)"; "Gear" — "edit a template"; "Drag a cell row from the inspector onto an object (layout mode)" — "show the cell on the face"; "Delete" — "remove the selection"; "Move selection to board…" — "move objects between boards".
- `HelpPanel`: a dialog listing `KEY_BINDINGS` then `HELP_GESTURES`; opened by `?` and by a toolbar "?" button; Esc and its close button close it.

- `CRYPT_MAP` (exported constant): `{file: "crypt-map.png", width_px: 2400, height_px: 1600, px_per_unit: 100, rooms: Room[], corridors: Rect[]}`, `Room = {n: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6; name: string; rect_px: [x, y, w, h]}`. Rooms, in pixels from the image's top-left: 1 "Entrance" `[100, 1100, 500, 400]`, 2 "Hall" `[700, 1100, 500, 400]`, 3 "Guard room" `[1300, 900, 700, 600]`, 4 "Stair" `[100, 100, 600, 600]`, 5 "Barracks" `[900, 100, 700, 600]`, 6 "Shrine" `[1800, 100, 500, 600]`; corridors `[600, 1250, 100, 100]`, `[1200, 1250, 100, 100]`, `[300, 700, 100, 400]`, `[1400, 700, 100, 200]`, `[1600, 300, 200, 100]`. `GOBLIN_IMAGE = {file: "goblin.png", width_px: 128, height_px: 128}`. `exampleAssetPath(file)`: the absolute path under `packages/fixtures/assets/` (via `import.meta.dirname`).
- `raster.ts`: `rasterCryptMap(): Uint8Array` — one palette index per pixel, row-major: 0 rock `#2b2b2b` everywhere outside rooms and corridors, 1 floor `#b8a888` inside them, 2 wall `#5a4a3a` for a 4 px border along the inside of each room rect (not corridors), 3 numeral `#1a1a1a` for the room number drawn with a 5 × 7 bitmap digit scaled ×12 with its top-left at `[x + 30, y + 30]` of the room (any legible digit bitmaps; they stay inside `[x + 30, y + 30, 60, 84]`). `rasterGoblin(): Uint8Array` — index 1 green `#4f8a3a` for pixels within 60 px of `[64, 64]`, index 0 elsewhere (transparent through a tRNS chunk).
- `write-assets.ts` encodes both as 8-bit palette PNGs (colour type 3, filter 0 on every scanline, `deflateSync`) and writes them to `packages/fixtures/assets/`; it is run once from the repo root with `node --import tsx packages/fixtures/test/support/write-assets.ts` and both PNGs are committed.

title: Authority: intermittent vtt-mcp stdio test failure (SdkError: Connection closed)
description:
Implements: none (test reliability).

packages/authority/test/mcp/stdio.test.ts (vtt-5su.17) fails intermittently in full-suite runs with SdkError: Connection closed (seen at line ~331 during a Codex review run of vtt-3l6.6, and once during vtt-5su.17's own development); it passes when rerun alone and in most full runs. Likely a subprocess lifecycle race: the MCP client connects to a vtt-mcp child whose stdin/stdout closes early, or a port/session-file collision between concurrently running process tests under full-suite parallelism.

Done when: the cause is identified from captured child exit status and stderr (add that capture to the harness permanently), the race is fixed in the test harness or, if real, in bin/mcp.ts, and the stdio suite passes 20 consecutive full-suite runs locally; pnpm typecheck, lint, format:check, test exit 0.

Out of scope: unrelated test speedups.

Depends on: nothing.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text: Also observed: 4 failures in packages/authority/test/acceptance/step5.test.ts in one full run during vtt-1xv.5 ('Connection closed' from the vtt-mcp child under load), passing alone and in the next two full runs. Same child-process lifecycle; cover both files.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text: Root cause: a base64url token starting with '-' (1 in 64) passed as '--token <t>' is rejected by parseArgs, so vtt-mcp exited before its transport existed (SdkError: Connection closed). Fixed in the harness (--token=<t>, permanent exit/stderr diagnostics captured synchronously) and the product (generateToken redraws until alphanumeric; usage documents --token=<t>; PROTOCOL §2 and M3-D4 amended). 20 consecutive full-suite runs green. Codex review: one finding (exit capture timing) fixed in 4ba4cd5. Merge kept the serve-flags usage text with the --token=t spelling.

title: Epic acceptance: every §10 fixture end to end in the UI
description:
Implements: the epic vtt-1xv Done-when ("every §10 fixture passes end to end
in the UI") as interpreted by M5 plan decision Q16 (docs/plans/m5-plan.md §4;
also a comment on vtt-1xv); FORMULAS.md §10; FIXTURES.md §1–§9; review r1
finding 13; review r2 finding 12.

Exclusive files: `packages/ui/test/acceptance/fixtures-ui.test.tsx`,
`packages/ui/test/acceptance/ui-fixture-driver.ts`. Adds `@vtt/fixtures` as
a workspace devDependency of `@vtt/ui` (`pnpm install`, lockfile in the same
commit).

- For each of the ten scenarios: an in-process authority over
  `documentFromSetup` (from the `@vtt/authority/test-runner` subpath that
  vtt-1xv.10 adds, Q21) with a `ScriptedDiceSource` of the scenario's script;
  the real `<App>` (vtt-1xv.23) in jsdom with a recording renderer. Fixture
  objects have no layouts (except the Attack card's face, vtt-1xv.10), so
  their buttons and contained objects are reached through the default face
  (Q11): the button strip, and the contents list whose non-template entries
  the driver expands (UI-local state, no write; the driver never expands a
  template entry, which would spawn a working copy).
- Navigation (review r2 finding 12): before a click, suppressed or edit
  step the driver makes active the board of the target object's outermost
  container (Fireball's `fb1` and its rows: `shelf`, where `aldric_binder`
  stands); before a drag, the destination board (all drags are within one
  board; Fireball's step 5: `map`); fixture objects are never relocated to
  make a click possible. The matrix's Board column states it (the edit
  target is selected on its board by a click, then edited in the
  inspector; a contained target, such as Fireball's rows, is selected by
  clicking its row, vtt-1xv.25's entry click; review r3 finding 4).
- Action state is never read from button visibility: `action` expectations
  read `action_states` from the expectation's viewer's object view (GM by
  default); `face_element` reads the drawn face of that viewer (and, for an
  element not drawn, asserts its absence). Every other expectation is
  checked through `get_objects`/`log` with the expectation's viewer.
- Paths: **click** = view-as the step's actor (the GM view for `gm`), the
  driver asserts the button is drawn and enabled, then clicks it (located
  with `faceHitAt` on the app's face scene); **suppressed** = the driver
  asserts the UI suppression (button not drawn, or drawn disabled and a
  press sends nothing: the authority's revision is unchanged), then sends
  the `invoke` through the app's own `session.client` with the step's actor
  and asserts the predicted refusal; **drag** = a canvas drag by the GM (an
  entry drag out of a default contents list when the object starts
  contained); **edit** = the GM types into the inspector's value cell (into
  the face editor when the cell has one), `clear_override` = the formula
  bar's Clear; **log** = the log panel's Undo on the newest group that is
  neither undone nor an undo; **protocol** = the app's own `session.client`
  (same connection; reason given).

Fixed matrix (every step of the ten scenarios; step indices 0-based):

| dice-tray | 6, 7 | gm | move die_c, die_a → cup (index) | protocol | — (protocol) | container moves with an index |
| dice-tray | 8 | gm | move die_c (in cup) → board | drag | table | entry drag from the cup's contents list |
| dice-tray | 9 | gm | move die_b → board | drag | table |  |
| die-with-modifier | 0, 2, 5 | gm | spawn d20 → board (2 and 5 with `cells`) | protocol | — (protocol) | `as` bindings (and initial cells in 2 and 5) have no gesture |
| die-with-modifier | 1, 6 | gm | invoke Roll on gm_die, goblin_die | click | table |  |
| die-with-modifier | 3 | aldric | invoke Roll on aldric_die | click | table |  |

title: Client: tag locally generated failures so recovery need not guess
description:
Implements: PROTOCOL.md §10 (disconnected and timeout are client-produced codes).

enableRecovery (vtt-5su.19, packages/protocol/src/client/recovery.ts) must tell a locally generated transport failure (socket closed, send failure, request timeout) from a server error response in order to keep a subscription recovering versus failing it. ProtocolClient (vtt-5su.7, client.ts) marks nothing, so recovery matches message text and timing, which a late server response copying the client's wording can defeat (safe but wrong) and a backwards clock jump can misclassify. Found by the vtt-5su.19 implementer.

Change: ProtocolFailure gains a readonly `local: boolean` (true for failures the client synthesizes: disconnected, timeout, cannot-send, malformed result); a server response carrying a client-only code (disconnected, timeout) is treated as a protocol violation (the request fails with internal, details.type protocol). recovery.ts drops the message and timing heuristics and branches on `local`.

Done when: client tests for the flag on each local failure kind and for the client-only-code violation; the five recovery tests that run server responses with client-only codes still pass, now via the flag; recovery.ts contains no message matching or Date.now timing for classification; pnpm typecheck, lint, format:check, test exit 0.

Out of scope: any other recovery behaviour.

Depends on: vtt-5su.19.

title: Formula and protocol: object-free ad hoc evaluation
description:
Implements: PROTOCOL.md §9 (evaluate without `this`: 'the engine's ad hoc default applies'), FORMULAS.md §2.

The engine's ad hoc evaluation (packages/formula/src/engine/adhoc.ts, AdhocOptions.thisId required) has no object-free mode, so evaluateAdhoc in packages/authority/src/protocol/queries.ts (vtt-5su.8) evaluates on the first board in board order as a workaround, which invents semantics (this is a ref to a board; no boards gives #REF). Found by the vtt-5su.8 implementer.

Change: make thisId optional in AdhocOptions with defined semantics: with no object, `this` evaluates to #REF with message 'no object in scope', bare cell names evaluate to #NAME, everything else (literals, obj(), allObjects, spatial functions on explicit refs) works; budget and dependency recording unchanged. queries.ts evaluateAdhoc passes no thisId when params.this is absent and drops the board workaround; its JSDoc is updated. Record the rule in FORMULAS §2 (one sentence) and a decision-log row.

Done when: engine tests for the three cases above; queries tests: `1 + 2` → 3, `obj("Goblin").max_hp` → 27, `max_hp` → #NAME, `this` → #REF, with no boards in the document as well; pnpm typecheck, lint, format:check, test exit 0.

Out of scope: any other engine behaviour.

title: Authority: undo accepts an optional label
description:
Implements: PROTOCOL.md §4 (undo params: optional label), DESIGN §7 Undo.

PROTOCOL §4 gives undo an optional label, but the store's undo(store, actor, selector) (packages/authority/src/store/undo.ts, vtt-75c.8) takes none and hardcodes 'Undo <target label>', so executeUndo (vtt-5su.5, packages/authority/src/protocol/commands.ts) ignores params.label. title: Epic acceptance: §8.4 prep steps 1–4 by hand, minus binders
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §8.4 steps 1–4 as interpreted below (decision Q19),
§8.1; the epic vtt-3l6 Done-when; FORMULAS.md §10 (re-hiding a room; the
goblin's HIT badge); review r1 findings 5, 14; review r2 finding 14.

**Interpretation of "steps 1–4 minus binders" (Q19).** Step 1 without the
stocked GM binder: a new table whose GM board is empty. Step 2 with the
character template made by hand on the GM board (a token with the HIT badge
formula and an owned sheet object), copied four times by template drag,
values typed into the inspector and in place (sheet faces are M5; "each
binder already holds an Attack card template" is skipped). Step 3 as written.
Step 4 as written, the "owned attack d20" being a contained object whose
`owner` is the goblin. The HIT badge is visible in the inspector, not on a
face (faces are M5).

Exclusive files: `packages/ui/test/acceptance/prep.test.tsx`,
`packages/ui/test/acceptance/prep-script.ts`. The test drives the real
`<App>` in jsdom (recording renderer, `BoardCanvas` pointer events in screen
coordinates, user-event typing into the inspector, formula bar and in-place
editor) against an in-process authority on a temp table file
(`TableHost.open(createIfMissing)` + `startServer({http: [vtt-3l6.16's asset
handler]})`). Its header quotes steps 1–4 and maps each sentence to the
blocks below.

1. New table: the GM board exists and is empty.
2. On the GM board: a token "PC" with tag `pc` (header tag control), the HIT
   badge formula `hit = any(on(this).where(tag has "d20").total >= ac)`
   typed in the formula bar, made a character template (`is_character`,
   `is_template` via the header), with a "Sheet" note Alt-dropped into it
   and the sheet's `owner` written explicitly as `@<pc template id>` in the
   inspector (containment does not set ownership); drag the template four
   times on the GM board (four copies, each with its own sheet copy whose
   `owner` is remapped to its copy, and `template` refs); fill `name`, `ac`,
   `hp`, `attack_bonus`, `dex_save` on each copy by typing into the
   inspector, and the name in place.
3. Add board "Crypt"; import a PNG map with the image tool; draw six fog rect
   zones over it (`opaque`, `visible_to` gm); type the re-hiding formula
   `=if(len(contents(this).where(tag has "pc")) > 0, all, gm)` into
   `visible_to` of rooms 2 and 4.
4. Goblin template on the GM board: image, `ac` with per-cell visibility gm,
   `max_hp`, `damage_taken`, `attack_bonus`, `hit`, tag `creature`, and an
   attack die Alt-dropped into it: a token named "d20" with tags `die` and
   `d20`, `owner` = the goblin via `@id`, `value` (a literal), `modifier =
   owner.attack_bonus` and `total = value + modifier`. Drag the goblin
   template eight times on the GM board, select the eight copies with a
   marquee, use "Move selection to board…" → Crypt (vtt-3l6.10; there is no
   cross-board drag in M4, review r1 finding 5), then on Crypt drag four
   into room 3 and four into room 5.
5. Checks driven through the UI, with fixed numbers: the PC copy used here
   has `ac` 13 and the goblin copy used has `attack_bonus` 5 (typed in step 2
   and 4). Move that PC copy to Crypt with "Move selection to board…" and
   place it on the map outside all six zones. View as that PC; in GM view
   drag the PC into room 2 and check, viewing as the PC, that room 2 shows no
   cover; return to GM view, drag the PC out of room 2 to an uncovered spot
   outside all six zones, and check as the PC that room 2 is covered again.
   Return to GM view; take the goblin copy's die out ("Take out") and drag it
   onto the PC token (both outside all zones); type `9` into the die's `value`
   (total 9 + 5 = 14 ≥ 13: the PC's `hit` is true), then `7` (12 < 13:
   false). Finally view as the PC for the six-cover assertion below. Rolling
   stays M5.

Assertions (through the protocol, as a second GM client): every object,
cell, formula, tag, visibility entry, `owner` and containment above (each
sheet copy's `owner` is its own PC copy; each die copy's `owner` is its own
goblin copy); created ids are readable (`token_<n>`, `zone_<n>`, … via
`id_base`); `zones crypt` lists four goblins in room 3 and four in room 5;
each goblin copy's die `modifier` evaluates to that goblin's
`attack_bonus` and its `total` to `value + modifier`; room 2's `visible_to`
evaluates to `all` while the PC is inside and to `gm` after it left; the
PC's `hit` is true with `value` 9 and false with `value` 7; the app viewing as one PC
character on Crypt (the PC and the die outside all zones) draws six covers and no goblin
(recording renderer); `save`, close, reopen the file: the same objects and
the asset are there.

**Manual browser checklist (for the user; does not gate this bead).** On
close, the orchestrator posts this list as a comment on the epic vtt-3l6 for
the user to run:

1. `pnpm --filter @vtt/ui build`, then `pnpm serve /tmp/crypt.table.json`;
   open the printed URL.
2. The GM board tab shows; pan (Space-drag, middle-drag) and zoom (wheel).
3. Create a token, rename it in place, type a formula in the formula bar,
   override it in the inspector and clear the override.
4. Tag it `pc`, make it a character template with an owned note (Alt-drop)
   whose `owner` you set to the template (`@id`); drag the template four
   times on the GM board; fill the copies' cells.
5. Add a "Crypt" board, import a map image, draw six fog zones, put the
   re-hiding formula on two of them.
6. Build the goblin template (GM-only `ac`, tag `creature`, an owned die
   tagged `die` and `d20` with `value`, `modifier = owner.attack_bonus`,
   `total = value + modifier`); drag eight copies on the GM board, select
   them, "Move selection to board…" Crypt, and drag four into room 3 and
   four into room 5.
7. View as a character: six covers, no goblins; back to GM. Move a PC to
   Crypt and into room 2: it reveals itself; move it out: covered again.
   Put a goblin's die on the PC and type its `value`: the PC's `hit`
   follows.
8. Undo once, save, stop the server, restart it, reload: everything is there.

Done when: `prep.test.tsx` passes within 60 s; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm
lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0. (The manual checklist is
posted on close and does not gate.)

Out of scope: binders, faces, buttons and actions (M5); step 5 (vtt-5su.13
and M6); browser automation (none in v1, Q16); feel-good tuning (M6).

title: Epic acceptance: §8.4 step 5 headless
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §8.4 step 5 ("Through the MCP server, ask the agent: 'Make room 4 difficult terrain and hatch it, and make a Fireball card for Aldric with DC 14 and 8d6.' Check its work in the inspector. Correct the DC by typing over it."), §5.2, §4.4; FORMULAS.md §10 (Difficult terrain, Fireball); docs/PROTOCOL.md §6 (stale writes, undo targets), §8, §11; the epic vtt-5su Done-when.

The epic acceptance test, black box: the authority and the MCP server run as the real binaries (`vtt-serve` from vtt-5su.14, `vtt-mcp` from vtt-5su.17). Exclusive files: `packages/authority/test/acceptance/step5.test.ts`, `prep.ts`, `agent-script.ts`. The agent is a deterministic script (no model) doing what an agent would.

1. Start `vtt-serve <tmp>/crypt.table.json --port 0 --print-session` as a subprocess (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` in a temp directory); read `{url, token}`.
2. `prep.ts`, as the GM through a `ProtocolClient` (`kind: "ui"`): board `crypt` "Crypt"; character `aldric` (`is_character`) on `gm_board` with `aldric_binder` (owner `aldric`, `visible_to` owner) on `gm_board`; six zones `room1`…`room6` on `crypt` (`is_zone`, rect shapes, `opaque: true`, `visible_to` gm, names "Room 1"…"Room 6"); a token `pc1` (tag `creature`, `base_speed: 30`, the `speed` formula of FORMULAS §10 Difficult terrain) inside room 4; a goblin `goblin1` (tag `creature`) in room 3.
3. Start `vtt-mcp --url … --token … --name step5-agent` through the MCP SDK's stdio client transport. `agent-script.ts`: `table_info`; `zones {board:"crypt"}` → the zone named "Room 4"; `transact` (label "Room 4: difficult terrain, hatched"): `set_tag room4 ["difficult"]`, `set_value room4.pattern "hatch"` (the hatch is an ordinary cell; M4 decides appearance cells); `get_objects ["pc1"]` → `speed` 15; `transact` (label "Fireball card for Aldric"), one group: `create_object fireball_aldric` into `aldric_binder` with cells `name "Fireball"`, `owner` and `caster` ref `aldric`, `zone` ref `fireball_aldric_zone`, `dc 14`, `damage_dice 8d6`, `damage` empty, `locked false`, `applied false`, `save_row` ref `fireball_save_row`, formulas `targets = contents(zone).where(tag has "creature")` and `rows = contents.where(tag has "save_row")`, and the four actions of FORMULAS §10 Fireball with Roll damage as `roll(damage_dice) -> damage`; `create_object fireball_aldric_zone` into `fireball_aldric` (`is_zone`, a circle shape); `create_object fireball_save_row` into `aldric_binder` (`is_template`, tag `save_row`; cells `target` empty and `save_roll` empty; formulas `card = container`, `save_bonus = target.dex_save`, `passed = save_roll + save_bonus >= card.dc`, `damage_dealt = if(passed, floor(card.damage / 2), card.damage)`; action `Roll save` with `when: save_roll = empty` and steps `["roll(1d20) -> save_roll"]`, all per FORMULAS §10 Fireball); `explain_action` for each of the card's four actions and for the row template's `Roll save` (no `when_error` with `#SYNTAX`); `explain_cell fireball_aldric.targets` while the zone is still inside the card: value `[]`, and the recorded dependencies are cell dependencies only, with no `index` node (`contents(zone)` of a contained zone asks for no board candidates; dependencies are recorded dynamically, FORMULAS §7); then `transact` `move fireball_aldric_zone` onto `crypt` at a point outside every room, `explain_cell fireball_aldric.targets` now lists an `index` dependency, and `undo {type:"mine"}` puts the zone back inside the card (asserted with `get_objects`).
4. Check its work, as the GM: `get_objects` shows the zone, card, row template and every cell as written; the card group is one group whose actor is `{type:"agent", name:"step5-agent"}`; a subscription with scope `all` and viewer Aldric contains the card and its zone, no room zone, six covers on `crypt`, and no `pc1` (covered); the GM `spawn`s `fireball_save_row` into `fireball_aldric` (as `$row`), `get_objects` on the copy shows the `Roll save` action with its `when` and steps and every row cell, the card's `rows` lists the copy, and the GM then undoes that spawn (`undo {type:"mine"}`) so the remaining steps start from the agent's card (invoking `Roll save` stays M5).
5. Correct the DC by typing over it: the agent subscribes to `{type:"objects", ids:["fireball_aldric"]}` beforehand; the GM `transact`s `set_value fireball_aldric.dc 15`; the agent's `poll_changes` returns that cell change with actor `gm`; the agent's `transact` with its old `base_revision` writing `dc` is rejected `stale_write` naming the GM's group; the agent's `undo {type:"group", index: <card group index>}` is refused `undo_conflict` (the GM's later `dc` write touches the card); then the agent's `transact` writing `damage_dice 10d6` with the same old base commits; finally the agent's `undo {type:"mine", expect_index: <card group index>}` is refused `undo_target_changed` with `actual` = the `damage_dice` group's index (its newest group).
6. `save`; SIGTERM the server; restart it on the same file with `--port <same port> --token <same token>`; the MCP process reconnects; the agent's `poll_changes` on its subscription handle returns a `resync` record with `session_changed: true`; the agent's next `get_objects ["fireball_aldric"]` shows `dc 15`, `damage_dice 10d6`, and the four actions; `log` lists the agent's groups with their actor.

Done when: `step5.test.ts` passes within 60 s and leaves no subprocess or lock file behind (asserted in `afterAll`); its header comment quotes §8.4 step 5 and maps each sentence to the numbered blocks above; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: a model in the loop; the inspector UI (M4); invoking the card's actions (M5); hatch rendering (M4).

Depends on: vtt-5su.11, vtt-5su.14, vtt-5su.15, vtt-5su.16, vtt-5su.17.

title: Authority: fixture scenarios over the protocol
description:
Implements: FIXTURES.md §1–§8, §11 (as amended by vtt-75c.2); DESIGN.md §5.2 (the agent and the UI go "through the same invariants"); the M2 runner contract (vtt-75c.13, including its `onStep` observation hook); docs/PROTOCOL.md §4–§8 as written by vtt-5su.2; FORMULAS.md §7 (the maintained views must equal fresh evaluation).

Run all ten fixture scenarios through the protocol and show the protocol path matches the direct engine path; also the integrating subscription equivalence test across object, cover and log scopes (vtt-5su.9, vtt-5su.20). Exclusive files: `packages/authority/test/protocol-runner/*.ts`, `test/protocol-scenarios.test.ts`. Reuses vtt-75c.13's test helpers (`documentFromSetup`, `runScenario` with `onStep`, `RunReport`, value comparison) by import and never edits `test/runner/`; if a needed helper is not exported from its module, export it with a one-line change.

`runScenarioOverProtocol(scenario, {onStep?}): Promise<RunReport>`: `documentFromSetup` → `TableHost.inMemory(store, {dice: new ScriptedDiceSource(scenario.dice)})` (vtt-5su.4, vtt-75c.15) → `startServer` on port 0 (vtt-5su.10) → a `ProtocolClient` (vtt-5su.7, `kind: "test"`, Node's `WebSocket`). Steps: `set` and `override` → `transact [set_value]` (the M2 runner's scenario errors are decided from the GM view's `kind` per PROTOCOL.md §7.2: `set` is a scenario error when `kind` is `"formula"` (structural cells such as `position` included), `override` is a scenario error unless `kind` is `"formula"`, `clear_override` unless `overridden` is true; a `"structural"` or `"literal"` cell takes `set`); `clear_override` → `clear_override`; `move` → `move`; `spawn` → `spawn` with `as`, and `owned` bindings taken from the result's `copies`; `undo` → `undo {type:"latest"}`; `bind` → the contents of `in` (or `list_objects` with the tag filter) compared on GM views by FORMULAS §4 equality; a step's actor → `actor` param (characters as `{type:"character", id}`, GM by default); `base_revision` = the client's revision. Expectations: `cell`, `cell_error`, `override` from the GM view; `exists` from `missing`; `container`, `contents`, `placement` from structural cells; `object_visible` = present in `get_objects` with that viewer; `cell_visible` = the cell is present in that viewer's view (`cells` has the key), whatever its value, so a readable cell holding a redacted ref is visible (FIXTURES §7); `log_groups` from `log`; `log_includes` from `explain_group` (GM `EffectView`s); `replay` from `document`: vtt-75c.16's `replay` of the groups over the setup snapshot, compared with `storedStateEqual`; `rejected` from `status: "rejected"` mapped through `toFixtureReason` (vtt-75c.4). Truncation and skipped expectations exactly as the M2 runner (invoke stops the run; `action` expectations skipped and counted). After setup and after every executed step, `onStep({step, snapshot})` is called with the `document` result's snapshot (step -1 for setup).

Per-step comparison: the test runs each scenario twice, through vtt-75c.13's `runScenario(s, {onStep})` and through `runScenarioOverProtocol(s, {onStep})`, collects both snapshot sequences, and compares them pairwise.

Subscription equivalence (`test/subscription-equivalence.test.ts`, also exclusive to this bead): through `startServer` on port 0 and `ProtocolClient` mirrors (vtt-5su.7), seeded random sequences of 200 commits over a 60-object table (writes, formula sets, overrides set and cleared, moves between boards and containers, spawns, creates and removes inside containers, reorders, tag and shape edits, template and character flag changes including Aldric's own `is_character`, `set_actions`, board add, rename and remove, literal and override refs to objects and boards that are later removed, `visible_to` changes on containers, opaque zone toggles and moves including erroneous `opaque`, face flips, per-cell visibility, undo), for the GM and Aldric and for `board`, `objects` (subtree), `all` and `log` scopes: after every commit each mirror (objects, covers, log-window groups) equals the result of a fresh `subscribe` with the same params at that revision.

Done when: `protocol-scenarios.test.ts` produces for all ten scenarios the same `RunReport` table as vtt-75c.13's `scenarios.test.ts`; for every scenario the two `onStep` sequences have the same length and each pair of snapshots is equal by `storedStateEqual` with identity included; a test shows that `set` on a structural cell holding a formula (`position`) is a scenario error in both runners and `override` on it is accepted in both; a test shows `cell_visible` true for a cell whose value is `{type:"redacted"}` in the viewer's view; `subscription-equivalence.test.ts` passes for at least 5 seeds (seeds printed on failure); a self-test shows a wrong expected value fails with the scenario title, step index and expectation named; the server and client are closed after each scenario; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: `invoke`, `action` expectations and action rejections (M5); round-trip mode over the protocol (the direct runner covers it); new scenarios; fixture format changes; edits to `test/runner/` beyond one-line exports.

title: Authority: scenario runner (M2 subset)
description:
Implements: FIXTURES.md §1–§8 and §11 (as amended by vtt-75c.2, including `cell_visibility` mapping, the `replay` expectation and the rejection protocol for M2 step types); DESIGN.md §7; the runner contract in planning bead vtt-75c.1 comment 1.

Add @vtt/fixtures as a workspace devDependency of @vtt/authority and the runner in packages/authority/test/runner/ (test code, so M5 can extend it without a public API): setup.ts (`documentFromSetup`), steps.ts, expect.ts, run.ts (`runScenario`), plus packages/authority/test/scenarios.test.ts.

- `documentFromSetup(setup)`: boards; objects with `is_template`, `is_zone`, `tag`, `shape`, `contents`; `placement` → `board` plus a `position` cell (literal list or formula); `cells` → `Cell`s; `cell_visibility` → the object's `cell_visibility` metadata verbatim (any cell name, including structural and absent cells); `is_character` true for ids in `setup.characters`; actions copied as source; `revision 0`, `next_seq 0`. Fixture values are the schema values (the FIXTURES §2 encoding is the schema encoding), so conversion is the identity, checked with `isValue`.
- Steps: `set` (`writeValue`; a scenario error if the cell holds a formula), `override` (`writeValue`; scenario error unless a formula), `clear_override` (scenario error without an override), `move`, `spawn` (initial cells passed as cell content: literals through `writeValue`, formulas through `setFormula`; binds `as` and each `owned` key through the returned copy map), `undo` (`{type:"latest"}`), `bind` (tag, `where` by vtt-o9i.6's `equals` on `table.value`, `in`; zero or several matches is a scenario error; no group, no dice). `actor` maps to `Actor` (`gm` or `character`). Bindings resolve everywhere ids are used. Acting on a removed object is a scenario error.
- Every step runs through `transactWithDice` (vtt-75c.15): a `Rejected` is a refusal handled by the rejection protocol below; a `ScenarioError` (bad script, bad binding, set on a formula cell, …) propagates and fails the scenario as a scenario error, never as a refusal.
- Rejection protocol for the steps above: a refused primitive appends no group; a `rejected` expectation predicts it with the reason mapped by `toFixtureReason` (vtt-75c.4); an unpredicted refusal or a predicted one that does not happen fails.
- Expectations: `cell` (structural equality on tagged values: numbers exact, roll results all fields, lists elementwise), `cell_error`, `override`, `exists`, `container`, `placement` (evaluated position), `contents`, `cell_visible`, `object_visible`, `log_groups`, `log_includes` (`write` matches a `cell` effect whose resolved `after` value equals; `roll` matches a `cause: "roll"` effect; negative indices from the end), `replay` (vtt-75c.16's `replay` of the retained groups from the setup snapshot, compared with `toSnapshot()` by `storedStateEqual` (revision excluded), and the dice source's `remaining()` is unchanged). Any other expectation on a removed object is a scenario error.
- Truncation: the runner stops before the first `invoke` step and reports the scenario as partial. Expectations of type `action` are skipped and counted (they need M5's `when` handling). Leftover dice entries are a scenario error only for complete runs. `invoke`, `action`, and `when_*`/`step_error` rejections are M5's to add.
- Round-trip mode (`runScenario(s, { roundTrip: true })`): after setup and after every step, `serializeTable` → `parseTable` (vtt-75c.11) and continue on the loaded table, asserting snapshot and log equality at each hop. This is how "Save. Close. Reopen; everything, including the log, the undo… is there" is tested without a format change.
- `RunReport`: `{ title, complete: boolean, stepsRun, stepsTotal, skipped: Record<type, count> }`.
- Observation hook (for vtt-5su.12's per-step comparison): `runScenario(s, { onStep?: (report: StepReport) => void })` with `StepReport = { step: number; snapshot: Snapshot }`, called once after setup (`step: -1`) and once after every executed step (refused steps included, skipped `invoke` steps not), with `table.store.toSnapshot()` at that point (in round-trip mode, of the reloaded table). The hook only observes: its return value is ignored, it receives a copy, and nothing else in the run depends on it. Exported from `run.ts` with `StepReport`.

scenarios.test.ts runs every scenario in both modes and asserts the report against this table, so M5 must update it when it adds `invoke`:

| Scenario file | Status at M2 end | Steps run | Skipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| hit-points.json | complete | 5/5 | none |
| difficult-terrain.json | complete | 4/4 | none |
| re-hiding-room.json | complete | 6/6 | none |
| goblin-hit.json | partial | 4/6 | none |
| attack-card.json | partial | 2/7 | 6 `action` |
| fireball.json | partial | 2/12 | 2 `action` |
| die-with-modifier.json | partial | 1/7 | none |
| dice-tray.json | partial | 0/10 (setup expectations only) | none |
| drawing-a-card.json | partial | 0/4 (setup expectations only) | 1 `action` |
| shuffling.json | partial | 0/2 (setup expectations only) | 1 `action` |

Done when: scenarios.test.ts passes with exactly the table above in both modes (every non-skipped expectation in the run prefix holds, including the `replay` entries vtt-75c.2 added to the three complete scenarios and to fireball.json step 1); runner self-tests in test/runner/*.test.ts show that a wrong `cell` value, a missing predicted rejection, an unpredicted rejection, an unknown binding, a `set` on a formula cell, and a leftover dice entry in a complete run each fail with a message naming the scenario, step index and expectation; a test feeds a `ScriptedDiceSource` through `rollInto` to show script consumption and `remaining()`; a synthetic spawn whose initial cell is a formula (`modifier = owner.attack_bonus`) stores the formula and its value recomputes after commit (and again after `attack_bonus` changes); a scripted-dice mismatch inside a step is reported as a scenario error, not a rejection; `onStep` is called `stepsRun + 1` times with steps -1, 0, 1, … and its snapshots equal the table's state after each step (checked on hit-points.json), and a hook that mutates its argument does not change the run; a synthetic setup with `cell_visibility` entries on `contents` and `tag` (no such cells) converts, survives a round-trip hop unchanged, and is honoured by `cell_visible`; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); `invoke` steps, `action` expectations, `when_false`, `when_error`, `step_error` rejections (M5); new scenarios; changes to the fixture format beyond vtt-75c.2.

Depends on: vtt-75c.5, vtt-75c.16, vtt-75c.14, vtt-75c.12, vtt-75c.15, vtt-75c.11, vtt-75c.17, vtt-75c.2.

title: Formula: §10 acceptance suite
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §10 (every formula and `when` of every fixture, evaluated), §2.2, §4, §5, §6, §7 as exercised by them; docs/FIXTURES.md §9 (the states each scenario passes through).

The runner (vtt-o9i.10) stops at the first `invoke`, `spawn`, `undo`, or `bind` step, so most §10 formulas are never evaluated in the states those steps reach. This bead proves every §10 formula against those states by building them directly in a `MemoryHost` (vtt-o9i.15): literal roll results written with `set` in place of rolls, spawned objects added to the setup in place of `spawn`, and placements reached with `MemoryHost.move`, so spatial functions run on real geometry. One test file per fixture, test/acceptance/<scenario>.test.ts, each test quoting the scenario expectation it mirrors (scenario title + step index) and loading the formula sources from the scenario file itself (not retyped), so a fixture edit cannot silently diverge.

Cases (values are the scenarios' expected values):

- Hit points: 27, 22, and 17 after `damage_taken` 10.
- Die with a modifier: loose die `total` 0 → 14 after `value` = roll 14; Aldric's die `modifier` 5, `total` 5 → 16 (roll 11) → 17 after `attack_bonus` 6; goblin's die 4 → 13 (roll 9).
- Goblin HIT: `hit` false with nothing on the goblin and with a die beside it (footprints not overlapping), true with die1 (`value` roll 15, `total = value + modifier`) on top with higher `z`, false with a die whose total is 12, false with only a non-`d20` object on top.
- Dice tray: zone variant (dice moved into the tray's rect) and cup variant (the `contents` cell); sums 0, a die, two dice, a non-die ignored; a die leaving the cup changes the cup's sum.
- Difficult terrain: the scenario's `speed` formula (`zones_containing(this)` composed with `where` and the library) gives 30 / 15 / 30 as the token moves into and out of the difficult zone (composed query + library assertion moved here from vtt-o9i.8).
- Attack card: `bonus` 5; `total` 5 before the roll, 17 after roll 12; `hit` false before the roll (target empty: short-circuit), true with goblin `ac` 13; the three `when` guards via `engine.evaluate` at each state (Roll enabled only with target set and no roll; Roll damage only when hit and no dmg; Apply only when hit, dmg set, not applied).
- Fireball: `dc` = caster's `spell_dc`; `targets` = `[goblin1, goblin2]` with the zone moved to [10,10] on the map; `rows` from the card's `contents` cell; per row `card` = ref to the card, `save_bonus`, `passed`, and `damage_dealt` = 14 (a number) on a pass and the roll result itself (`{expr:"8d6", dice:[3,5,2,6,4,1,6,1], dropped:[], total:28}`) on a fail; the drift step (`dex_save` -5 flips a pass to a fail); Apply all's guard false with one `save_roll` empty, true with both.
- Drawing a card: `len(deck.contents) > 0` true, true, false as the deck empties; `first(deck.contents)` is the top card.
- Re-hiding a room: the room's `visible_to` formula (`contents(this).where(tag has "pc")` composed with `len` and `if`) gives viewers `["gm"]` / `["all"]` / `["gm"]` as the PC moves in and out (composed assertion moved here from vtt-o9i.8).
- Shuffling: no formula; the file asserts that and nothing else.

Done when: every case above passes; every formula and `when` source in every scenario is evaluated by at least one test (a meta-test collects the sources from the scenario files and fails listing any not exercised). `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); executing action steps, rolling, spawning, visibility, log (vtt-75c.13, M5); changing scenarios or the fixture format.

Depends on: vtt-o9i.15, vtt-o9i.7, vtt-o9i.8, vtt-o9i.16, vtt-o9i.12.

title: Protocol: public credentials getter on ProtocolClient
description:
Why: the MCP import_asset tool (vtt-3l6.20) needs the connection's current url and token to POST /assets, but ProtocolClient keeps them private, so the tool takes a credentials callback and a ConnectionCredentials tracker wraps the discovery source in bin/mcp.ts.

What: add a read-only credentials getter ({url, token}) on ProtocolClient that reflects the pair in use after every reopen; make importAssetTool's credentials option default to it and drop the tracker if nothing else needs it.

Implements: PROTOCOL.md §1, §11 (import_asset). Done when: the getter is covered by a client test across a reopen with new credentials, and import-asset.test.ts passes with the default. Out of scope: any new protocol message. Depends on: vtt-3l6.20 merged.

title: UI: drop a drag on a board tab to move or copy there
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.6 On the canvas ("Objects move between boards with Move selection to board…"); M6 plan decision Q8 alternative (docs/plans/m6-plan.md §4).

Dropping a canvas drag on a board tab moves the dragged selection to that board (positions kept, as "Move selection to board…" does) and activates it; a template drag (a copy) dropped on a tab spawns the copy on that board at the target view's centre. Removes the "Move selection to board…" detours of the first-session guide (GM binder on Crypt, the note to the GM board). If M6's triage (vtt-nb8.14) promotes it, it is re-parented under vtt-nb8.

Done when: jsdom tests show a move drop and a template-copy drop on a tab, each one group, and that a drop on the active board's own tab does nothing; the four repo checks exit 0.

Out of scope: cross-board geometry; dragging between two visible boards.

Depends on: vtt-3l6.10, vtt-1xv.23. (Followup from the M6 plan.)

title: Examples: a prepped first-session table for repeat playtests
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §8.4 (repeat playtests); M6 plan decision Q11 alternative (docs/plans/m6-plan.md §4).

A prepped example table (the state after §8.4 step 6) generated by the walkthrough's `runPrep` (vtt-nb8.9) and shipped with its assets, so a repeat playtest can start at step 7; a script regenerates it, and a test checks the shipped file equals a fresh generation (ignoring revision and ids that differ only by allocation order, or by fixing them).

Done when: `pnpm start <copy of the prepped table>` opens at step 7's state; the regeneration test passes; the four repo checks exit 0.

Out of scope: game content; templates beyond the stocked ones.

Depends on: vtt-nb8.11. (Followup from the M6 plan.)

title: UI: drop an image file onto an object to set its image
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.6 Appearance cells (image), §8.1 (objects with image); M6 plan decision Q7 alternative (docs/plans/m6-plan.md §4).

Dropping an image file from the operating system onto an object on the canvas uploads it (`POST /assets`, vtt-3l6.16's `uploadAsset`) and writes the returned path into that object's `image` cell, with the base revision captured at the drop; dropped onto empty board space, it creates an image object as the image tool does.

Done when: jsdom tests with an in-process authority show a file drop on a token sets its `image` in one group, a drop on empty space creates an image object, an unsupported type pushes a notice and writes nothing; the four repo checks exit 0.

Out of scope: drag of URLs or HTML from other pages; cropping.

Depends on: vtt-nb8.7. (Followup from the M6 plan.)

title: UI: show a guard's value while editing an action
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.5 (the inspector shows an action's precondition); M5 plan section 5.

While the action editor of vtt-1xv.19 is open, the typed `when` is evaluated ad hoc on the object (GM `evaluate` with `this`, debounced, keyed by revision and text) and its value shown beside the field.

Done when: typing `hp < 5` shows its current value and updates after a commit; stale responses are dropped; the four repo checks exit 0.

Out of scope: evaluating steps.

Depends on: vtt-1xv.19.

title: UI: layout-mode handles on expanded contained entries
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.6 (layout mode); M5 plan section 5.

vtt-1xv.18's layout tool works on board objects only; extend move and resize handles to the face of an expanded entry drawn inside a contents element (coordinates mapped through the entry's scale).

Done when: an element of an expanded binder card is moved and resized in place with one `set_face` per gesture; the four repo checks exit 0.

Out of scope: editing collapsed faces on the canvas.

Depends on: vtt-1xv.18.

title: UI: number formatting options on face value elements
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §11 (Text formatting of numbers on faces: a face element setting); DESIGN.md §4.6.

Face value elements gain an additive `style.format` (sign, fixed decimals) applied by the face model.

Done when: `+3`, `-1` and `2.50` render as configured; the four repo checks exit 0.

Out of scope: formula-language changes.

title: UI: grid or fan layouts in contents elements
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.6 (contents element), §4.7; M5 plan section 5; M6 plan decision Q12 (docs/plans/m6-plan.md §4).

Contents elements gain a layout: `"list" | "grid" | "fan"` (an additive face field, default `"list"`) for hands and trays. Scrolling of overflowing lists is already done (M5 review r2: vtt-1xv.14, vtt-1xv.16) and is not part of this bead.

title: UI: ink pen colours, widths and an eraser
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.6 Ink and text (as written by vtt-1xv.5); M5 plan decision Q19.

Ink strokes gain optional colour and width (a schema change to the ink value, additive) and the ink tool an eraser that removes whole strokes it crosses (one `set_value` per gesture against the gesture's base revision).

title: UI: keyboard access to face buttons and contents entries

title: Formula and authority: dependency-tracked guard and show-when expressions
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §7 (propagation); DESIGN.md §4.6; M5 plan decision Q10.

Replace vtt-1xv.12's per-commit re-view of every in-scope object with a `when` or `show_when` by engine-tracked expressions: a formula-engine API that evaluates a keyed expression (not a cell, not readable by formulas) with recorded dependencies, invalidated like cells, so `invalidate` reports which guards and show-whens may have changed.

Done when: views carry the same results as with the rescan (the vtt-1xv.12 tests pass unchanged); a commit that touches nothing a guard reads re-views no object for presentation; the four repo checks exit 0.

Out of scope: changing view shapes; other subscription optimizations (vtt-qf5.4).

title: Client: handshake timeout when the server never answers hello
description:
Implements: PROTOCOL.md §2 (handshake).

ProtocolClient.connect/reopen (vtt-5su.7) never settle if the server accepts the socket but never answers hello; the 5 s hello timeout is server-side only, and enableRecovery (vtt-5su.19) then waits forever. Found by the vtt-5su.19 implementer.

Done when: the client has a handshake timeout (injectable, default 10 s) after which connect/reopen reject with disconnected, the socket is closed with 4000, and recovery continues its backoff; a fake-server test covers a server that opens but never replies; PROTOCOL §2 states the client-side timeout; pnpm typecheck, lint, format:check, test exit 0.

Out of scope: server-side changes.

Depends on: vtt-5su.19.

title: Formula: export geometry helpers reused by authority
description:
Implements: none (code hygiene).

anchorOf, geometryNumber and compareIds in packages/formula/src/functions/spatial.ts are not exported from @vtt/formula; packages/authority/src/protocol/views.ts and queries.ts, and engine/cover.ts, each carry their own copies. Found by the vtt-5su.6 and vtt-5su.8 implementers.

Done when: @vtt/formula exports the three helpers (one module, one index line), the authority copies are removed in favour of the imports, behaviour unchanged (existing tests pass), pnpm typecheck, lint, format:check, test exit 0.

Out of scope: semantic changes.

Depends on: vtt-5su.8.

title: Protocol: formula error messages can name hidden or deleted ids
description:
Implements: PROTOCOL.md §7.3 (error redaction), DESIGN §4.4.

Formula error messages carry ids ('reference to deleted object <id>', 'N objects are named …'). PROTOCOL §7.3 removes the message only when the error's origin is invisible to the viewer; an error whose origin is visible, or which has no origin, keeps a message that can name a deleted or hidden object. Found by the vtt-5su.6 implementer.

Done when: a decision is recorded (either character views strip ids from messages they cannot see, or messages never contain ids and carry them in structured fields), PROTOCOL §7.3 states it, ViewBuilder.redact implements it, and a test shows a character cannot learn a hidden object's id from a #REF or #NAME message.

Out of scope: GM views.

Depends on: vtt-5su.6.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text: Also: PROTOCOL §7.3 says a ref to an id that is neither a live object nor a board becomes 'redacted' without limiting that to group views; object views produce #REF (vtt-5su.9, §8). Reword §7.3 when fixing this bead.

title: UI: cell-name autocomplete in the formula bar
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.6 (formula bar); FORMULAS.md §3 (names, dot-access), §6 (functions).

Suggest the focused object's cell names, function names and, after a dot on a reference cell, the target's cell names (from the views the viewer has), in the formula bar (vtt-3l6.13).

title: UI: multi-object transforms and multi-select inspector editing

Implements: DESIGN.md §4.6 ("I want HP visible on all these tokens" without code), §8.1.

M4 handles and the inspector act on one selected object (vtt-3l6.9, vtt-3l6.12). Add group rotate/scale handles for a multi-selection and an inspector mode that edits a cell present on all selected objects in one transact.

title: UI: snapping and grids
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §3.3 (snapping and stacking yes), §8.1 (pan, zoom, objects).

An optional grid per board view (drawn by the renderer) and snapping of drops, creation and handle edits to grid points or other objects' edges, toggled in the toolbar; UI-only state.

title: UI: drag from the inspector contents list onto the canvas
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.1 (moving out of a container onto a board), §4.6 (inspector).

M4 takes contained objects out with a Take out button only (vtt-3l6.12). Allow dragging an entry from the contents list and dropping it on the canvas at the pointer (move with a board destination).

Done when: a jsdom test drags a die from a token's contents list onto the canvas and the authority shows it on the board at the drop point.

Out of scope: the contents face element (M5).

Depends on: vtt-3l6.12, vtt-3l6.7. (Followup from the M4 plan.)

title: Authority: garbage collection of unreferenced assets
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Persistence (assets beside the file), as amended by vtt-3l6.2 (no garbage collection in v1).

Imported images accumulate in <table>.assets/ and in the file's assets list (vtt-3l6.16). Offer an explicit command that lists assets no cell in the snapshot or retained history references and removes them from the list (and optionally the directory).

Done when: a test imports two images, references one, runs the command, and the other is unlisted after save while the referenced one is kept, including one referenced only by a retained group's effects.

Out of scope: automatic collection on save.

Depends on: vtt-3l6.16. (Followup from the M4 plan.)

title: Authority: CSP and security headers on served UI pages
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Platform; docs/PROTOCOL.md §1 (HTTP routes, as amended by vtt-3l6.2).

vtt-3l6.14 serves the UI with no-store and nosniff only. Add a Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self'; connect-src the authority's ws origins; img-src 'self' blob: data:), Referrer-Policy no-referrer and frame-ancestors 'none', verified against the built Vite output.

Done when: tests show the headers on GET / and static files; the built UI still loads and connects (manual check noted in the close comment).

Out of scope: TLS and remote access (vtt-y1w.8).

Depends on: vtt-3l6.14. (Followup from the M4 plan.)

title: UI: per-object render bitmap cache
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Platform ("Canvas2D with viewport culling and per-object render caching").

M4 renders with viewport culling and an image decode cache only (vtt-3l6.6). Add an offscreen bitmap cache per draw item keyed by the item's drawn content and a zoom bucket, invalidated when the item's view or the zoom bucket changes, once profiling on a table of a few thousand objects shows a need.

Done when: a renderer test with RecordingContext shows an unchanged item is drawn from its cached bitmap across frames and redrawn after its view changes; a benchmark note records the frame time before and after on a 3,000-object board.

Out of scope: PixiJS; image tiling (vtt-y1w.4).

Depends on: vtt-3l6.6. (Followup from the M4 plan.)

title: Authority: ActionContext.read clones the change summary on every read
description:
Implements: DESIGN §7 (transactions), performance only.

ActionContext.read (packages/authority/src/engine/action-context.ts, vtt-75c.15) calls tx.changes() on each read to apply the 'changed in this transaction' rule, and Transaction.changes() structuredClones the ChangeSummary. Cost grows with reads × summary size. Fine for M2; worth fixing before large actions in M3+.

Done when: reading a cell through ActionContext does not copy the summary (e.g. a cheap change counter on the transaction, or a read-only summary view), with the existing action-context tests unchanged and a test that a 1000-read action over a transaction with 1000 changed cells stays well under a second.

Out of scope: any semantic change to the rules in ActionContext.

Depends on: nothing.

comments.author: Theodore Gast

title: Docs: FIXTURES.md §9 Fireball example uses a stale 8d6 roll
description:
Implements: docs/FIXTURES.md §9 (Fireball example only).

docs/FIXTURES.md §9 (around lines 246, 404, 611) shows the Fireball 8d6 roll as dice [3,5,2,6,4,1,6,1] total 28, giving damage_dealt 14 on a pass and roll(28) on a fail. The committed fixture packages/fixtures/scenarios/fireball.json scripts [3,5,2,6,4,1,5,1] total 27 (13 on a pass, 27 on a fail; Apply results goblin1 13, goblin2 30), and its description text agrees with 27. The engine agrees with the fixture (vtt-o9i.11 acceptance suite). Found while implementing vtt-o9i.11.

title: Protocol: persistent txn_id deduplication
description:
Implements: docs/PROTOCOL.md §6 (idempotent retries).

The txn_id cache (vtt-5su.5) is in memory and lost on authority restart, so a retry across a restart may double-apply. Persist recent txn_ids (e.g. on each group) so a repeat after restart returns the original result.

Done when: commit with txn_id, restart the authority from the file, resend: no new group, the original result is returned.

Out of scope: cross-table dedup.

Depends on: vtt-5su.5, vtt-5su.4. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q8.)

title: Authority: automatic log compaction policy
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Persistence (log compaction allowed; the log panel shows what is retained).

v1 never compacts automatically (vtt-5su.4). Decide and implement a policy (e.g. keep the last N groups or groups newer than D days, at save time) on top of compactLog (vtt-75c.11), recorded in the decision log.

Done when: the policy is configurable on TableHost, runs at save, keeps absolute indices and barrier rules, and a test shows undo below the kept range is nothing_to_undo and changes_since reports truncated.

Out of scope: in-memory checkpoints.

Depends on: vtt-5su.4. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q24.)

title: Protocol: read-set preconditions on transact
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §5.2 (writes rejected on conflict), docs/PROTOCOL.md §6.

The stale-write rule (vtt-5su.5) refuses only when an intervening group touched a key the transaction writes. Add an optional expect: [{object, cell}] read set to transact, refused stale_write when an intervening group touched any of those keys, so a write computed from a value that changed meanwhile is caught.

Done when: a transact with base_revision r writing B and expecting A is refused after an intervening write to A and commits otherwise; PROTOCOL.md and the MCP transact tool schema document the field.

Out of scope: automatic rebase.

Depends on: vtt-5su.5. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q7 c.)

title: Protocol: cell-level deltas in commit events
description:
Implements: docs/PROTOCOL.md §8 (subscriptions, commit events), FORMULAS.md §7 (propagation).

Commit events currently upsert whole object views (vtt-5su.9). Send cell-level patches ({object, cells: {name: CellView | null}}) instead, as an additive protocol extension negotiated in hello, to cut bandwidth for large sheets.

Done when: the vtt-5su.9 equivalence property test passes with patch deltas; ViewMirror (vtt-5su.7) applies patches; a protocol version or capability flag keeps old clients working.

Out of scope: changing which cells are recomputed.

Depends on: vtt-5su.9, vtt-5su.7. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q10.)

title: Fixtures: quote prose in card and Fireball scenario notes

Audit and bring the other four to the same standard without changing expected values. Out of scope: any value change.

title: Vitest empty-project reporter misbehaves in watch mode
description: From Codex review of vtt-1me.3. In watch mode, deleting a package's last test file does not trigger onTestRunEnd, and after a later rerun detects it, restoring the test leaves process.exitCode at 1. Fix: track per-project state and clear exitCode on recovery, or skip the guard in watch mode. Root vitest.config.ts.

title: UI: vite.config.ts imports authority source relatively; move to the runner config loader
description:
Implements: none (tooling hygiene).

packages/ui/vite.config.ts (vtt-3l6.15) imports ../authority/src/server/{http-ui,session-file} relatively because Vite 8's default config loader externalizes bare imports and Node then fails on @vtt/authority's extensionless TypeScript imports; every vite/vite build prints a cosmetic warning about extensionless imports and the future configLoader native default. The proxy default port 4747 is hardcoded for the same reason.

Done when: the UI scripts use --configLoader runner (or an equivalent that lets the config import @vtt/authority and @vtt/protocol by name), the relative imports and the hardcoded port are replaced, plain pnpm --filter @vtt/ui dev/build work without warnings, and the vite-config tests pass; pnpm typecheck, lint, format:check, test exit 0.

Out of scope: plugin behaviour.

Depends on: vtt-3l6.15.

Refresh the proxy destination alongside bootstrap credentials when fixing the loader.

Store the invoked action's definition (when and steps) in each action group so the log and `explain_group` can show the steps as written at commit time (schema and file change).

title: Schema: export the absolute-path check used by serialize and TableHost
description:
Implements: none (code hygiene).

The ABSOLUTE_PATH regex for asset paths exists in three places: packages/schema/src/file.ts, packages/authority/src/persist/serialize.ts (vtt-75c.11) and packages/authority/src/host/table-host.ts (vtt-3l6.25 addAsset). Found by the vtt-3l6.25 implementer.

title: Authority: createIfMissing on a dangling symlink replaces the symlink
description:
Implements: PROTOCOL.md §2 (canonical table path), edge case only.

canonicalTablePath (vtt-5su.18) resolves a dangling symlink to <realdir>/<alias name>. TableHost.open with createIfMissing (vtt-5su.4) then writes the new table file at that path, replacing the symlink instead of creating its target. Found by the vtt-5su.4 implementer; untested.

Done when: a dangling symlink passed to TableHost.open with createIfMissing either creates the symlink's target (preferred) or refuses with a clear error; a test covers it.

Out of scope: any change to the lock protocol.

Depends on: nothing.

title: Per-object card backs: a back appearance cell in the face-down exemption set
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.4 (face-down shows its back), §4.6 Appearance cells (as written by vtt-3l6.2: generic back in v1).

v1 draws a generic back because FACE_DOWN_EXEMPT (vtt-75c.10) has no appearance cell, so a per-object back image would be hidden from non-owners. Add a back cell (image path or color) to the exemption set and draw it for face-down objects; no fixture needs it yet.

title: Per-board units and grid metrics

title: Boards: reordering

Boards are shown in document order with no way to reorder them (vtt-3l6.10). Needs a reorder-boards edit primitive with an undoable effect, a protocol op and the tab drag in the UI.

A help overlay (?) listing the M4 key bindings (vtt-3l6.17, vtt-3l6.7) generated from the binding tables so it cannot drift.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text: Superseded by vtt-nb8.8 (M6 plan vtt-nb8.1, Q12): keyboard help generated from the binding table, extended with gestures and M5's keys.

title: Protocol: chunked initial subscription snapshots
description:
Implements: docs/PROTOCOL.md §8 (subscriptions), §10 (limits); DESIGN.md §7 (scale: tables of a few thousand objects).

In v1 server-to-client messages have no size limit: an initial `subscribe` result for an `all` or large `board` scope is one message, and the slow-consumer threshold `max_buffered_bytes` is 64 MiB (vtt-5su.2, vtt-5su.10). For much larger tables (see vtt-y1w.4, very large map performance) deliver initial views in bounded chunks with a revision-consistent completion boundary: the subscription is pinned to the revision of its first chunk, commits after it are queued and delivered after the final chunk, and a reconnect restarts the snapshot without looping on the same failure.

Done when: a subscription over a table whose initial view exceeds a configured chunk size arrives in several chunks over the real transport, the mirror equals a fresh subscribe at the completion revision, commits made during delivery are applied after completion, and an additive protocol extension (PROTOCOL.md §12) keeps v1 clients working.

Out of scope: cell-level deltas (vtt-qf5.4); tiling of map images (vtt-y1w.4).

Depends on: vtt-5su.9, vtt-5su.10, vtt-5su.7, vtt-5su.19. (Followup from M3 plan review r1, finding 21.)

title: Protocol: persistent command deduplication across authority restarts
description:
Implements: docs/PROTOCOL.md §6 (deduplication, client retries, `uncertain`), DESIGN.md §7 (persistence).

In v1 the (`client.instance`, `txn_id`) deduplication store is in memory (vtt-5su.5), so it is lost when the authority restarts; clients then report a lost write as `uncertain` instead of retrying, and a retained-entry miss is `retry_unknown` (vtt-5su.19, vtt-5su.5). Persist recent deduplication entries (client instance, txn id, fingerprint, result) with the table, e.g. on each group or in a bounded section of the file, so a retry after a restart returns the original result and clients may retry across a `session` change.

Done when: commit with a `txn_id`, save, restart the authority from the file, resend from the same client instance: no new group and the original result is returned; a resend with a different fingerprint is rejected `invalid`; PROTOCOL.md §6 and the client retry rule are updated (retry across sessions allowed for persisted entries); the file format change is a migration step and recorded in the decision log.

Out of scope: cross-table deduplication; deduplication of `undo`.

Depends on: vtt-5su.5, vtt-5su.4, vtt-5su.19. (Followup from M3 plan review r1, finding 12. Supersedes the earlier Polish bead vtt-qf5.7, which predates the client-instance scoping.)

title: MCP: Streamable HTTP transport
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §5.2 (bring your own agent).

v1 serves MCP over stdio from vtt-mcp (vtt-5su.11). Add an in-process Streamable HTTP endpoint for agent hosts that prefer HTTP.

Done when: an MCP client over HTTP lists the same tools as over stdio and passes the same tool tests.

Out of scope: auth beyond the local token.

Depends on: vtt-5su.11. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q1 a.)

title: Protocol: multiplayer rights over actor and viewer
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §8.2 (participants mapped to characters, rights model), §4.4.

In v1 every connection has GM authority and viewer is a view-as selector, not a security boundary (vtt-5su.10, vtt-5su.6). Multiplayer must bind a connection to participants, enforce viewer server-side, and gate writes by the rights model; commit-event group headers and labels must then be filtered per viewer.

Done when: to be planned with multiplayer.

Out of scope: v1.

Depends on: vtt-5su.10. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q4, Q9, Q15.)

title: Authority: remote access over TLS
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Platform, §8.2 (multiplayer needs a server authority).

v1 binds 127.0.0.1 with a per-start token (vtt-5su.10). Serving remote clients needs TLS, a non-loopback bind option and stronger auth.

Done when: to be planned with multiplayer.

Out of scope: v1.

Depends on: vtt-5su.10. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q4.)

title: Drop the fixtures Node typing shim
description: packages/fixtures/src/node.d.ts hand-declares node:fs/promises, node:path and import.meta.dirname because the package typecheck does not see the root @types/node. Fixing the shim should also let authority tests reuse formula's test hosts.

The fixtures node.d.ts comment saying the workspace has no @types/node is now stale. Resolve both when fixing the shim: give the packages that need Node an explicit types setting and drop the ad hoc reference.
